News.title: Man in his 20s dies after falling from balcony at flat as two men arrested over ‘murder’ with tributes paid for victim
News.content:
FALL 'MURDER' Man in his 20s dies after falling from balcony at flat as two men arrested over ‘murder’ with tributes paid for victim

A MAN who died after falling from a balcony has been named as detectives continue to question two people on suspicion of murder.

Shay Bishop, aged in his 20s, sadly passed away in hospital on Saturday night, sparking a full murder investigation.



He was earlier admitted with serious injuries following an incident at a block of flats off Liverpool Street in Salford.

Police were called to the scene shortly after midnight on Saturday.



How far he fell hasn’t been confirmed, but specialist scenes of crime investigators were pictured inside the flats on Saturday morning working on a top-floor balcony.

Now two men have now been arrested on suspicion of murder in connection with Shay’s death, cops said.

“They both remain in police custody for questioning,” said a spokesperson.

One man arrested was in his 20s, but no age for the second man has been given.



Shay’s friends have paid tribute to him on social media.

One told the Manchester Evening News: “Shay was a good guy who did a lot for people without realising. He stood for what was right and I will carry that with me. I hope he’s at peace.”

Another said: “It’s heartbreaking. I send my condolences to his family and friends. It’s extremely sad. He was young. It’s just very sad.”

Police chiefs said it is believed to be an “isolated incident” with no wider risk to the public.

Reports from neighbours living nearby the scene said members of the public rushed to help Shay and performed CPR on him.



Police said a post-mortem examination was due to take place today to establish a cause of death.

“A team of detectives are working around the clock to establish the full circumstances of this incident,” added the spokesperson.

“Officers are still appealing for witnesses to assist with ongoing enquiries.”

Chief Inspector Lee Gridley said on Sunday: “Firstly, our thoughts remain with the man’s family and friends as they grieve the death of their loved one. We now have two men in custody, and they are being questioned by detectives.

“We believe this is an isolated incident and that there is no wider risk to the public.



Anyone with information has been asked to contact police on 101 and quote log 8 of 29/08/2026 or speak to Crimestoppers anonymously.

More to follow… For the latest news on this story keep checking back at The Sun Online

News.title: All the new school rules coming into force across England this September – and one can save parents £50
News.content:
MANY parents sending their children back to school this week may be unaware of several new rules.

These term-time changes could help families cut costs, with one expected to save as much as £50.

Rules on uniforms, school dinners, mobile phones, safeguarding and more are all set to change when children return to school this week.



With so many rules taking effect, it is no surprise that parents have questions, and may need a quick refresher before the new school term begins.



English state schools will be given attendance targets to help improve rates

The Department for Education will set all state schools in England an attendance target, as one in five pupils continue to miss at least 10 per cent of schooling.

Schools have also been encouraged to offer more activities on Fridays to improve attendance at the end of the week.

Pupils will not be punished if a school’s attendance misses its targets, but the Department for Education will contact the school to make sure they are taking adequate action.

Parents, however, will still receive a penalty notice if a child accumulates 10 unauthorised absences during a rolling 10-school-week period, starting at £80 per parent.

All schools must follow statutory guidance to improve allergy safety

From September, schools are expected to implement the statutory requirements of Benedict’s Law to improve allergy safety.



This includes the development and publication of a whole-school allergy policy, as well as comprehensive allergy and emergency response training for all staff.

Schools must also hold spare in-date EpiPens and adrenaline devices on site and create individual action plans for all pupils with serious allergies.

Schools can only limit branded uniform items to a maximum of three pieces

Parents will be able to cut costs on uniform items this year, as schools can only limit branded uniform items to a maximum of three pieces.

This will include jumpers, blazers, trousers and skirts, with the new rule hoping to improve affordability and reduce household costs.



Ties are not included in restrictions for secondary schools, meaning four branded items are permitted if one of these is a tie.

Under the new school rules, families are expected to be able to save around £50.

Free school meals is extended to even more children

Announced by former Prime Minister Keir Starmer last year, all children in families who receive Universal Credit will now receive free school meals.

This is expected to lead to more than half a million more school pupils being entitled to free meals, saving families around £495 per year.



Research from Child Poverty Action Group, however, revealed that more than half of parents with newly eligible children may not realise their kids qualify.

To check eligibility, parents can register online using the Government Free School Meals page, or through their local council.

Mobile phones will be completely banned in schools

Following on from regulations that came into force at the end of June, UK schools must now be mobile phone-free by law.

This means that children cannot access their phones during lessons, time between lessons, break times or lunchtimes.



Other smart technology that has similar functions, such as receiving notifications and the ability to send messages, will also be restricted.

Volunteers supervised by teachers will now require a full DBS check

Previously, if a parent or volunteer regularly helped out at a school, they did not require a full criminal background check as long as a teacher was supervising them.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Now, if a volunteer helps children regularly, they must also have a full background check.

This includes volunteers who teach, train, look after and supervise children overnight or more than three times a week over a four week period.

News.title: Smirking Maduro shares new photos from US jail as ousted Venezuelan president flashes peace sign in prison jumpsuit
News.content:
NICOLAS Maduro has shared new photos from his US jail – and the bizarre pics show him smirking and flashing peace signs.

US forces seized the dictator, 63, and threw him behind bars on drug trafficking charges in January – where he has languished ever since.



His wife Cilia Flores, 69, has also been imprisoned in the New York jail after being captured during a dramatic night-time raid on their compound in Caracas.

Sporting a grey prison track suit and nike trainers, the tyrant looked slimmed down – but in jovial sprits.



Madura grins at the camera – clutching his glasses in one hand and flashing a peace sign with the other.

“I am sending these photos as a small gift to all my grandchildren, to the boys and girls, and to all the good people who love us,” he wrote on Telegram.

“I want you to know that we are standing firm, with our hearts full of your love,” he added.

The photos emerged on Sunday – but camera data suggests they were taken on June 25, a day after two devastating earthquakes decimated towns and killed more than 6,500 people in northern Venezuela.

“We will remain strong, calm and confident: God is with us. God will provide. Venezuela will rise again”, Maduro said online.

The deposed dictator has been running Venezuela since 2013 – and has close ties to Russian tyrant Vladmimir Putin.



Now, both Madura and his wife are locked inside a “jail within a jail”.

Prosecutors accuse the pair of collaborating with cartel kingpins to ship thousands of tons of cocaine into the US – claims which the couple vigorously deny.

“I am a decent man. I am still president of my country“, insisted Maduro at his hearing in January.



The ousted tyrant joked his way through a court appearance in July – telling his lawyer he looked “very serious”.

It was the third hearing since his abduction at the start of the year with the trial on the narco-terrorism charges scheduled for June 1, 2027.

It comes two days after Donald Trump struck a landmark deal with Venezuela which will see the US importing 65 billion barrels of oil.

The US president hailed it the “biggest oil deal in history” and claimed it would double Washington’s reserves and slash gas prices for ordinary Americans.

Trump reached the agreement with temporary president Delcy Rodriguez who has been running the country since US forces booted out Maduro at the start of the year.



He said on Truth Social: “This Historic Transaction MORE THAN DOUBLES American Oil Reserves, greatly increases our Oil Supply, and will substantially lower Gas Prices for all Americans, long into the future, while helping to continue to set Venezuela on a course toward Tremendous Success and Great Prosperity.”

News.title: Cyclist, 16, dies in hospital after collision with car as cops arrest man, 47, over ‘dangerous driving’ near stadium
News.content:
TEEN TRAGEDY Cyclist, 16, dies in hospital after collision with car as cops arrest man, 47, over ‘dangerous driving’ near stadium

A TEENAGE cyclist has died in hospital after a collision with a car near to Birmingham City’s stadium – as cops arrest a man on suspicious of dangerous driving.

Officers descended on the scene in Small Heath in the early hours of Friday morning where a 16-year-old boy was fatally struck by a car.

West Midlands Police said a car had been involved in a collision with a bike at the junction of Cattell Road and Templefield Street at around 5.25am.



The boy was raced to hospital with serious injuries but tragically passed away on Saturday, the force said.



His family are being supported by specialist officers.

Cops have now arrested a man, aged 47, on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving – he remains in custody.

A spokesperson for West Midlands Police said: “We are still urging anyone who has information or footage to get in touch with us.

“You can contact us via Live Chat on our website, or by calling 101, and quote log 580 of 28 August.”

A police cordon was in place at the scene outside the football ground on Friday.

West Midlands Police previously said that they believed a silver Vauxhall Astra abandoned at the scene was involved in the incident as they attempted to track down the driver.

Det Sgt Julie Lyman, from SCIU, said at the time: “I am appealing directly to the driver of this car to contact us urgently.



“A teenage boy has very serious injuries and we are working hard to establish exactly what happened and who was responsible.

“I would also urge anyone else with information or footage to contact us as soon as possible.”

An ambulance service spokeswoman said: “We were called to reports of an RTC involving a car and a pushbike at the junction of Cattell Road and Tilton Road in Nechells, Birmingham, at 5.23am and sent three ambulances, a paramedic officer and a MERIT trauma doctor with a critical care paramedic to the scene.

“On arrival, a man, the cyclist, was found in a critical condition.

“He received specialist trauma care before being conveyed under emergency driving conditions to Queen Elizabeth Hospital.”

News.title: Horror drive-by shooting leaves man, 46, seriously injured after ‘bullets riddled home’ as boy, 16, among two arrested
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

'IT WAS CHAOS'

'IT WAS CHAOS' Horror drive-by shooting leaves man, 46, seriously injured after ‘bullets riddled home’ as boy, 16, among two arrested

A MAN has been rushed to hospital after his home was targeted in a drive-by shooting with a 16-year-old boy among two arrested.

The teenage suspect and a 20-year-old were both detained on suspicion of attempted murder after the victim, 42, was left in a critical condition.



Emergency services were called to the address in County Durham, just after 8.10pm following reports of a shooting.

A number of suspects had driven to a house and fired shots from their car before making off in Balmer Hill, Gainford, cops said.



The property was left “riddled” with bullets and the house in disrepair, sources say.

A 20-year-old man and a 16-year-old boy have now been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder.

The boy has also been arrested on suspicion of theft, failing to stop and driving without a licence. They both remain in custody.

Crime scene investigators have spent the day scouring a property on the quiet County Durham street.

The front window of the home was left shattered and the front door appeared to have been shot at.

Residents said the entire street was shut off after the incident as police flooded the area.



One local, who didn’t want to be named, said: “We didn’t hear anything last night, but we saw about eight police cars all with flashing lights and it was chaos.”

The North East Ambulance Service (NEAS) confirmed it dispatched an ambulance crew, duty officer and clinical team leader after being called at 8.10pm.

A NEAS spokesperson said: “We were called to an incident at a private address in Gainford, Darlington at 20:10 on Saturday 29 August.

“We dispatched one ambulance crew, one duty officer, one clinical team leader and were supported by Great North Air Ambulance Service (GNAAS).

“One person was taken to hospital by road.”



The Great North Air Ambulance Service (GNAAS) also attended the incident.

News.title: Two more teens, 17 & 18, charged with murder after boy stabbed to death in daylight attack at council HQ near Wembley
News.content:
KNIFE HORROR Two more teens, 17 & 18, charged with murder after boy stabbed to death in daylight attack at council HQ near Wembley

ANOTHER two teens have been charged with murder after a 17-year-old was stabbed to death at a council HQ near Wembley Stadium.

David Wynter, 17, tragically died after the horror broad daylight attack at the Brent Civic Centre in North West London, on Tuesday, August 25.



Metropolitan Police and London Ambulance Service (LAS) crews rushed to the council HQ on Engineers Way at around 2.30pm.

Upon arrival, paramedics discovered David with stab wounds and quickly began giving him medical treatment.



However, despite the best efforts of medical teams, the teen was sadly pronounced dead at the scene.

The Metropolitan Police later confirmed a murder investigation had been launched and arrested a 15-year-old boy the same day, who was later charged with murder.



Now two more teenagers and a 20-year-old have been arrested.

Jahquarn St Hillaire, 18, and an unnamed 17-year-old have been charged with murder and possession of an offensive weapon.



The 20-year-old, Diego Farquharson, has been charged with assisting an offender.

All three have been remanded to appear at Willesden Magistrates’ Court on Monday, 31 August.

Detective Chief Inspector Aytac Necati said: “We are continuing to investigate David’s tragic death.

“I am aware that a number of individuals were in the area at the time of this incident. They may have video footage or information that could assist our investigation.

“While I would urge people not to share video footage of this incident online, we are aware that some clips may already be circulating on social media.



“I would urge anyone who sees such footage or who has information that could help officers to get in touch with us.”

The force also reiterated there will be an increased police presence in the area over the coming weeks.

Anyone with information can call 101 and quote CAD 4032/25AUG26, or contact Crimestoppers anonymously.

News.title: I want ugly monsters who murdered my dear Isabelle to die behind bars – I was so wrong about her killer mum
News.content:
GRIEVING dad Joshua Welsh felt like he got justice for his “little angel” – but the more he dwelled on the tragedy, the angrier he became.

The painful knowledge that one day her evil mum and boyfriend who brutally murdered the two-year-old will walk free – while his little Isabelle had her life stolen and he carries a life sentence of grief – left him furious. Now Joshua is calling for them to be given a full life term, like serial killers Rosemary West and Levi Bellfield.





Evil mother Alexandra Walker and her sick partner Harrison Simpson murdered Isabelle after a “sadistic” campaign of violence that included sexual assault and inflicting multiple fractures to 21 bones in the weeks leading up to her death.

Both were sentenced to a life term, with Simpson given a minimum of 27 years and 231 days and Walker a minimum of 21 years and 48 days.

But Joshua, of Thornaby, North Yorkshire, said his initial feeling of relief at the guilty verdicts was dashed just hours after the sentencing.

He believes they should rot in jail forever.

He tells The Sun: “The sentence was absolutely shocking. I now need to fight for justice for my daughter.

“They will get out when they are 50. Isabelle won’t have a life. She was a beautiful, innocent and loving little girl.





“What was done to her is the worst thing imaginable. They will get out and be able to live their life.

“When the verdict was guilty there was a feeling of justice. There was a sigh of relief but then the sentencing a few hours later left me very angry.

“For what they did, and for what they put Isabelle through a whole life order should have been made. If I could swear I would – but I have no other comment to make on my feelings towards them at the time.

“I am still broken and in bits. I’m still grieving and struggling with my mental health. It is so horrific to lose your daughter in such circumstances.

“I thought she was being well looked after by her mum. Clearly she wasn’t.”

Joshua has also hit out at the litany of missed opportunities by authorities that could have stopped them before Isabelle was killed.

In a glaring missed chance, Joshua discovered police had failed to execute an earlier arrest warrant against Simpson for a staggering 18 months – as they “couldn’t locate him.”

He adds: “What they both did was absolutely disgusting. That is no man. As for her – I don’t know if I’ve got the words to describe her. She was meant to love her and protect her. She did not do either.

“They are just two callous monsters.

“I just want justice for Isabelle and be her voice now she is not alive. I need to spread the message and make sure she is never forgotten.



“Isabelle was bubbly, full of smiles and had so much love to give. Every time you would see her her little smile would light up a room.”

And devastated Joshua gives a warning to other parents.

“My main message would be not to let any strangers into your house,” he says.

“Do the right tests and checks before you let anyone take care of your children.

“But she was also failed by the authorities and there were several chances to save her.”

The grieving dad said his relationship with Walker began in May 2022 and they moved in together just three weeks later.

He had believed her to be a good mum and said he had no welfare concerns for Isabelle despite not being able to see her as much as he wanted to after they split in August 2024.

He had last seen Isabelle days before her second birthday and had never heard of Simpson until his arrest.



Paramedics attended her home in Thornaby on 13 September 2025 and found the tot covered in cuts and bruises.

The trial heard Walker had initially delayed ringing 999 wrongly believing Isabelle was dead and was trying to get her story straight – including internet searches on “why would my toddler be bleeding”.

Isabelle was rushed to hospital but had sustained an unsurvivable head injury and was pronounced dead the following day.

The judge Ms Justice Norton said Isabelle had either hit her head against a hard surface when she was violently shaken, or she had been swung by the legs into a wall or a piece of furniture.

After a five- week trial at Teesside Crown Court, Simpson, 22, was found guilty of murder, sexual assault by penetration and child cruelty while Walker, 26, was found guilty of murder and child cruelty.

Recalling the horrific events for the first time, Joshua says he had been living with Isabelle and her mum for the first year and a half of her life before they split.

He adds: “I last saw her a few days before she turned two. Alex stopped me from seeing her. I tried to and never wanted to not see her – but she wouldn’t allow it.

“When Isabelle was in hospital, she didn’t even declare I was her father so I lost the chance to say goodbye to her.



“I had a very close bond with Isabelle. I was the first to hold her when she was born. I would always get a special cuddle from her and she was my little angel.

“I did not have a clue about her new boyfriend. I did not know him from Adam. I had no suspicions of her while we were together. I did not in any way think she was capable of something like this.

“I thought she was a good mum. I think it’s all his influence to tell you the truth. I am trying to get more information on it. But I knew nothing at the time.”

Joshua says the first he had heard of Isabelle’s death was when police turned up at his home.

Describing the heartbreaking moment, he added: “They sat me down on the sofa and said there had been an incident and something had happened with Isabelle.

“They just said she had passed away in hospital – but nothing about a murder or that she had been sexually abused.

“I just broke down instantly and cried my eyes out.”

He said he has only since learnt about all the failings – with one of the most serious being a failure by Cleveland police to execute an arrest warrant issued by Teesside magistrates court in March 2024 – 18 months before the murder.

At the time he had failed to attend court for breaching a non-molestation order in place after reports Simpson had harassed and threatened a woman.

Joshua added: “He had a warrant out for his arrest. I did not know about this and the police did not inform us.



“I thought I was in the loop but was clearly not. I was not a witness in the trial but sat in the public gallery and got fed bits and bobs. Little bits here and there but obviously nothing like the detail I heard in court.

“There was not one thing that I could say was the worst revelation. The whole thing was horrible, absolutely heart-breaking. I am shattered and will never be the same.”

Joshua said he found out two days after the verdict about the outstanding arrest warrant.

“I did not get told by the police. My sister found out about it on local radio. I was absolutely raging. I was angry, hurt and upset. The police should be ashamed of themselves.

“If they had done their job properly Isabelle would still be alive today. I want to campaign and raise awareness – to make sure the police do proper checks to stop this happening again.

“Instead of leaving innocent kids in the hands of monsters I want them to do their jobs properly.”

Joshua said he was still living with the mum before they split up in August 2024 and said the first time he ever heard the name of her partner was when he was arrested and charged with Isabelle’s murder.

He added: “I will remember Isabelle for her smile, for the happy and cheeky girl she was. Not by a photo of her next to those ugly monsters. As that is all they are.

“It has all been very hard – from the moment I was first told about it until now.

“The support I have got from my family and friends has been all that has got me through it. They have been a rock to me and without them I don’t know where I would be now.”



During the sentencing, the judge described the injuries to the girl as “sadistic” and said she was “obviously in pain and distressed and, in the final week of her life, gravely ill”.

Senior Investigating Officer, Detective Chief Inspector Steve Chatterton, released a statement after sentencing, and said: “Isabelle was an innocent child who should have been safe and happy at home. The pain and suffering she experienced at the hands of Walker and Simpson was sickening.

“This has been, without a doubt, one of the worst cases my team and I have dealt with. The severity and scale of Isabelle’s injuries were shocking and the fact that Walker repeatedly lied to try and cover their tracks further added to the pain of Isabelle’s family. Our thoughts remain firmly with Isabelle’s loved ones.”

In relation to the outstanding warrant, Cleveland Police said: “Multiple inquiries and arrest attempts were carried out to try to locate and arrest him, but these proved unsuccessful.

“We recognise the time Simpson had an outstanding arrest warrant is far from adequate. A review of this was immediately conducted upon his arrest for murder.

“This review, along with a determination to continually improve our processes around suspect management, has led to a number of recent changes, such as ongoing improved visibility across the force around outstanding warrants, a comprehensive data system which tracks all outstanding warrants, and stringent oversight including a governance group led by a superintendent.”

News.title: Man, 41, dies after crashing into tree during police chase involving marked car
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

CRASH PROBE Man, 41, dies after crashing into tree during police chase involving marked car

A MAN has died after his car hit a tree following a police chase involving a marked car.

Officers in a marked police vehicle were informed of a grey Audi driving without its lights on in High Street South in Dunstable shortly before 10.30pm on Saturday, according to the force.

The 41-year-old male driver failed to stop for police and a pursuit ensued as the Audi drove off on the A5183 towards Markyate.



At around 10.37pm, the Audi left the road and hit a tree near Caddington, police said.



No other vehicles were involved in the collision.

Officers conducted first aid and were supported by emergency service, but the driver was pronounced dead shortly before 11.30pm.

His next of kin have been informed and are being supported.



Following the incident, Bedfordshire Police made a mandatory referral to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC), which has since launched an investigation.

A cordon was in place on the A5 between the Kensworth Turn (northbound) and Caddington (southbound) whilst emergency services responded.

The road has since reopened.

News.title: Teen, 16, one of two arrested after man, 46, 'shot in the stomach' at house in quiet village
News.content:
Teen, 16, one of two arrested after man, 46, 'shot in the stomach' at house in quiet village

A 46-year-old man suffered injuries to his abdomen in Gainford with police arresting two males, aged 16 and 20, on suspicion of attempted murder

View Image Police and forensic officers at the scene on Balmer Hill (Image: North News & Pictures Ltd)

A 16-year-old boy and 20-year-old man have been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after an alleged shooting in County Durham which left a man critically injured.

The 46-year-old suffered "birdshot injuries" consistent with being shot with a shotgun to his abdomen at an address on Balmer Hill in Gainford just after 8.10pm on Saturday, August 29, police said.

Emergency services were called following reports that the suspects had allegedly driven to a property and fired at it from a car before fleeing the scene.

The man was taken to hospital, where his condition has been described as "critical but stable". No one else at the address was injured and officers remain at the scene today, reports Chronicle Live.

A statement from Durham Constabulary said: "A 20-year-old man and a 16-year-old boy have been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder. The boy has also been arrested on suspicion of theft, failing to stop and driving without a licence.

Article continues below

"They both remain in custody. An investigation is ongoing and anyone with information is asked to call 101 quoting incident reference 479 of August 29."

Crimestoppers can also be contacted anonymously on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Energy Secretary says 'no one should doubt our resolve' on tackling climate change as she hits back at criticism
News.content:
Energy Secretary says 'no one should doubt our resolve' on tackling climate change as she hits back at criticism

EXCLUSIVE: Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh said Britain’s communities 'will not forgive us if we do not act to protect them' after the UK was ravaged by heatwaves and wildfires this summer

View 4 Images Climate activists at a demonstration in August calling on the Government to block more drilling in the north sea (Image: Vuk Valcic/SOPA Images/Shutterstock)

The Energy Secretary has said “no one should doubt our resolve” on tackling climate change as she hit back at criticism.

‌



Miatta Fahnbulleh said Britain’s communities “will not forgive us if we do not act to protect them” after the UK was ravaged by heatwaves and wildfires this summer.

‌



New PM Andy Burnham faced criticism over the summer for not being explicit enough on the climate emergency facing the country - and the long-term action needed.

‌



Firefighters tackled nearly 200 wildfires in the first 10 days of August alone, while droughts ruined farmers' crops. Nurses warned the extreme heat was making the NHS an "impossible environment" to care for people and schools were forced to close or send students home early.

4 View 4 Images Miatta Fahnbulleh said Britain’s communities 'will not forgive us if we do not act to protect them' (Image: TIM ANDERSON) 4 View 4 Images Miatta Fahnbulleh was appointed as Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero by Andy Burnham (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



Mr Burnham called an emergency Cobra meeting and announced a temporary ban on disposable barbecues. He also announced a package of support to help farmers manage the impacts of the dry weather.

But leading climate organisations - including Greenpeace, WWF and Green New Deal Rising - wrote to the PM and accused him of “remaining silent” on the climate crisis, noting how a statement released after his Cobra meeting failed to mention climate change.

Asked about the criticism, Ms Fahnbulleh told The Mirror: “Well, I think it was a bit unfair because, to be fair, he'd only been in the job for a couple of weeks, and there's only so much that you can cover.

‌



“Look, I know Andy. He is as committed to climate change as I am. I think people should judge us by our actions. There has never been a Labour government that hasn't made climate transition an imperative.

“We are a global leader in climate action. We always have been, and that is an action that the last government took under Labour, and it is an action that we are taking now.

“So no one should doubt our resolve about it. And the reason I say it matters is because it's happening here, and ultimately, our communities will not forgive us if we do not act to protect them. That's the first job of government, and that is why we're taking it seriously.”

‌



View 4 Images Firefighters tackle a blaze in Sheffield in August (Image: Paul Atkin / SWNS)

She said tackling the climate crisis was "absolutely a priority" for Labour, adding: "You can't have gone through the last summer - we've seen heatwaves, we've seen droughts, we've seen wildfires.

"For me, the reason I care about this is that if we do not do our job as government of both protecting people by mitigating the impacts of climate change, but also adapting - because it is here - in order to respond and be resilient, that's families, that's homes, that's businesses, that are communities that are impacted in the here and now today. But it's also our kids. So we've got a responsibility to do this and do it well."

‌



Ms Fahnbulleh - who resigned as a minister under Keir Starmer after losing confidence in him - defended Labour's steadfast support of renewable energy, saying the Tories and Reform are “in the wrong place” on their climate policies.

Kemi Badenoch has declared the 2050 Net Zero target impossible. In July, the Conservative leader said the plan to go carbon neutral by 2050 was “a political fiction bankrupting the country”.

Net Zero is the policy aimed at balancing out the amount of greenhouse gases with those being removed from the atmosphere. The 2050 target was set under Theresa May's Tory government in 2019.

‌



Richard Tice has repeatedly labelled the plans "Net stupid Zero", claiming there is no evidence the strategy will work. The Reform UK deputy leader also faced criticism after saying people should be less “doom and gloom” about the hot weather and celebrate the benefits it could have on English wine.

Asked if Labour was losing the fight on Net Zero, Ms Fahnbulleh said: “My personal view, and that's backed up by the science, is that I think some of our colleagues and other political parties have got themselves into a slightly nonsense position on this. That's not where the public is.

“We are constantly testing this, polling, speaking to the public. The majority of the public supports action on climate, and they are seeing the impact on it in their lives and their communities.”

‌



The newly appointed Cabinet minister said the UK must "diversify our energy" to move away from international markets and protect British families' bills from global shocks like the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran.

She added: "The thing I say to the Tories and Reform is, when you say let's not do renewables, even though we know it's cheaper, when you say let's not do clean energy at a time that we can see that the thing that is driving up bills is gas, what is your answer on affordability? And they don't have one."

As Parliament resumes next week, Ms Fahnbulleh and Mr Burnham must soon make a decision on drilling in the north sea. Unions are in favour of approving Rosebank, an oil field north-west of Shetland, and Jackdaw, a gas field east of Aberdeen, as they say it will protect jobs, while green campaigners say signing them off would lead to devastating environmental impacts.

Article continues below

Asked how she feels that she will upset people no matter the decision, Ms Fahbulleh said: “I think the debate has become a little bit too polarised. The way that I see it is, we've been really clear and really pragmatic that oil and gas are part of the mix as we do the transition.”

She admitted jobs were decimated in the north sea under the Tories and said Labour will ensure there is “a proper plan for Aberdeen that is about protecting and preserving jobs now, but also creating jobs for the future”.

But she also admitted more drilling will not make energy bills more affordable. “If you care about affordability, and that's my number one priority, the reality is that because (Margaret) Thatcher sold off the North Sea, because oil that is drilled in the North Sea is sold on global markets that we have no control over, it doesn't solve the problem of affordability.”

News.title: Woman who claims Jeffrey Epstein flew her to UK for sex with Andrew 'may testify'
News.content:
Woman who claims Jeffrey Epstein flew her to UK for sex with Andrew 'may testify'

The unnamed woman's US lawyer, Bradley Edwards, has revealed he has been in contact with police in the UK after his client changed her mind about assisting the ongoing criminal case

View 3 Images Jeffrey Epstein, 66, was found dead in his cell at a Manhattan federal jail in August 2019 as he awaited trial on sex trafficking charges (Image: Getty)

An accuser who claims she was flown to the UK by paedophile Jeffrey Epstein to have sex with Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor says she might be ready to testify against him.

The unnamed woman - who alleges she spent a night with the ex-prince at Royal Lodge in Windsor - previously declined to make a formal complaint to British detectives investigating trafficking claims because she did not want to "risk losing her privacy".

Now her US lawyer, Bradley Edwards, has revealed he has been in contact with police in the UK after his client changed her mind about assisting the ongoing criminal case. The woman says she was in her 20s when, at Epstein's request, she spent a night with Andrew at Royal Lodge in 2010. Andrew has consistently denied any wrongdoing.

View 3 Images Bradley Edwards said his client had gone "from a hard no, to a maybe" about speaking with the authorities in the UK (Image: EPA-EFE/Shutterstock)

Sarah Ferguson to appear in TV documentary as part of UK comeback plan READ MORE :

Jeffrey Epstein partner Ghislaine Maxwell loses fresh bid to have sex trafficking conviction overturned READ MORE :

It is alleged she was also given a tour of Buckingham Palace and tea afterwards. Mr Edwards said he had spoken to British police about interviewing his client in the US, but nothing had been agreed. He told the Mail on Sunday: "She has gone from a hard no, to a maybe. Her main concern is to protect her child and she doesn't want her kid being harassed.

"If those issues can be addressed it could happen. She is thinking about it. I think she should testify because what happened was wrong. But I'm not going to push her. It has to be her choice."

Andrew was arrested on his 66th birthday in February on suspicion of misconduct in public office after documents released by the Trump administration appeared to show him passing sensitive information to Epstein during their decade-long friendship.

View 3 Images Andrew was friends with Epstein but denied any wrongdoing (Image: Getty)

In May, Thames Valley Police, which is leading the investigation, said it was widening the inquiry to include sex trafficking. The former duke denies any wrongdoing.

Mr Edwards, who has represented more than 200 alleged Epstein victims, previously sued Andrew on behalf of the late Virginia Giuffre, who alleged she had sex at 17 with the former duke of York in London, New York and on Epstein's Caribbean island.

Andrew settled for a reported £12million before the case went to trial but did not admit liability. The files released by the Department of Justice contained damning messages from Andrew to Epstein in 2010 talking about setting him up with a woman.

Epstein offered to set the former prince up with a "friend" who was "26, russian, clevere [sic] beautiful, trustworthy". It is not known if the woman in the email is the same one Mr Edwards represents.

Article continues below

British socialite Ghislaine Maxwell was sentenced in the US in June 2022 to 20 years in prison following her conviction on five counts of sex trafficking for luring young girls to massage rooms for Epstein to abuse.

She asked the US Supreme Court to overturn her conviction, but it was thrown out. Epstein, 66, was found dead in his cell at a Manhattan federal jail in August 2019 as he awaited trial on sex trafficking charges. His death was ruled a suicide.

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's office has been contacted for comment.

News.title: Middlesbrough house fire suspect released as investigation into murder of 7-year-old continues
News.content:
Middlesbrough house fire suspect released as investigation into murder of 7-year-old continues

Police are continuing to question a 23-year-old man in connection with the murder probe while a 31-year-old man has been released with no further charge

View 2 Images The blaze in Grangetown (Image: Newcastle Chronicle)

A 31-year-old man arrested on suspicion of murder over a fatal house fire which killed a seven-year-old girl and her aunt has been released with no further action.

‌



Officers were called to reports of a blaze at Birchington Avenue in Grangetown at 5.23am on August 26. Natalie McDonald, 34, and her niece Valentina Foster both died while four others were injured.

‌



Cleveland Police said a 23-year-old man continues to be questioned in connection with the murder investigation.

‌



Officers said on Friday that a 48-year-old woman remains in the Royal Victoria Infirmary in a "critical but stable" condition and a 27-year-old man is still at James Cook University hospital receiving treatment.

View 2 Images Valentina Foster, seven, and her aunt Natalie McDonald, 34

‌



Two teenage girls have both been discharged after suffering non life-threatening injuries.

The property remains unstable and there will be work carried out on the building over the coming days to make the site safe, the force said, adding that enquiries were ongoing.

Paying tribute to Natalie, her mum Lisa Kirton described her as "a beautiful soul, who would have done anything for anybody".

Article continues below

Valentina, who was known as Tina, was staying at the house for the summer holidays and had been "dancing around the living room" only the previous night.

"She was a cute little kid," Kirton said. "I can't believe it, seven years old - it's just a disgrace."

On Friday, Cleveland Police ACC Dave Sutherland said the force was not currently linking the fatal blaze to a crash on the A66 which killed seven people, including two police officers.

News.title: Terrifying moment airliners fly just feet over crowded sports stadium in 'dangerous' stunt
News.content:
Terrifying moment airliners fly just feet over crowded sports stadium in 'dangerous' stunt

Nailbiting new footage shows two Embraer E190 and an Embraer E195 planes coming within just metres of the roof of Cape Town's DHL Stadium during a close flyover

Planes fly dangerously low over stadium in Cape Town

Twin airliners participating in a flyover of a major stadium packed with tens of thousands of people were came within metres of the building's roof, shocking new footage shows.

‌



The two Airlink Embraer E-Jets soared over the DHL Stadium in Cape Town, South Africa, ahead of a rugby game between the country and New Zealand's national teams on Saturday afternoon. Airlink, an official partner of the Rugby's Greatest Rivals series, marked the game by flying the 98-seater jets over the open arena's top.

‌



What was meant to be an electrifying spectacle ended up anxiety inducing as footage showed the planes coming extremely close to the the 55,000-capacity venue.

‌



Jet2 flight from London to Ibiza declares emergency at 35,000ft and diverts to Paris READ MORE :

View 3 Images The planes could already be seen flying low on their approach to the stadium

Footage taken from the roof and posted online showed the Embraer E190 and an Embraer E195 jets zooming within what FlightRadar says was just between 41 and 46 feet (12 and 14 metres) of the stadium. As they came in close, colourful streamers were puffed into the air, which the massive aircraft were seen cutting through.

During one especially alarming part of the manouevre as the jets moved off the other side of the stadium, the jet pitched upwards, pulling its tail even closer to the surface.

‌



The display was welcomed by Airlink, which afterwards praised what it said were "spectacular scenes". But social media users were less enthused, criticising the display for being "absolutely unnecessary and dangerous". One user on Reddit said: "Next level reckless. That is way too small of an envelope for error."

View 3 Images Social media users were shocked to see just how close the planes were to the roof

Another questioned: "Is this like impressively stupid or calculated?" Airlink said in a statement following massive backlash that it "notes the concerns", but pushed back, saying it was a "safe flyby" that followed careful planning.

‌



A spokesperson for the airline said: "Airlink notes the concerns expressed in various social media and online forums regarding yesterday’s formation flyby over Cape Town’s DHL Stadium.

"The flight demanded careful planning and rehearsal, as it required navigating at low altitude, at around 150 knots. The South African Civil Aviation Authority and Air Traffic Navigation Services provided valuable guidance, approval and support to ensure a safe flyby."

View 3 Images Airlink said the display was carefully planned and within aviation regulations

Article continues below

"The two aircraft were flown by highly-experienced crew, with each comprised of three senior captains operating in the roles of commander, co-pilot and safety/technical officer."

The spokesperson added that flight data showed the flyover was performed within the safe altitude set by the SACAA. They said: "The flight data recorded by both aircraft confirms that the flights were performed within the SACAA’s approved and rehearsed safety altitude and speed limits for the flypast."

News.title: GK Barry bravely reveals she was assaulted and raped on work experience placement
News.content:
GK Barry bravely reveals she was assaulted and raped on work experience placement

I'm A Celebrity and podcasting star GK Barry - real name Grace Keeling - has bravely shared her experience of sexual assault in the hope it will help other women

View 3 Images Grace Keeling - better known as GK Barry - has opened up about a sexual assault trauma (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

GK Barry says she felt compelled to include a traumatic rape experience in her new life advice book, in the hope it will help others to not go through the same agony that she experienced ten years ago.

‌



The 27-year-old podcaster, whose real name is Grace Keeling, says It’s Giving Life: A Guide To Surviving And Thriving by GK Barry, is not an autobiography. But it does include deeply personal stories - including the assaults she experienced at the age of 17, while doing work experience for a media company near to her childhood home in Suffolk.

‌



Grace, who rose to fame via TikTok in 2022 and later appeared on ITV's I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out Of Here!, admits it took her years to acknowledge what had happened to her. She decided to include the ordeal in her book after becoming aware of startling statistics that reveal almost a quarter of women have been raped or sexually assaulted from the age of 16.

‌



Posting on social media, Grace opened up to her online followers about her ordeal. She wrote: “This is the first time I’ve spoken about a chapter in my book that I’ve never shared publicly before. When I was 17 I was raped and I’ve spent the last 10 years not telling anyone out of fear.

3 View 3 Images The reality, social media, and TV star has shared her experience in a new book (Image: Brett D. Cove / SplashNews.com) 3 View 3 Images Grace previously told her partner, footballer Ella Rutherford, about her past experience (Image: James Gourley/ITV/REX/Shutterstock)

‌



"I have been extremely nervous about speaking about this and for a long time tried to push it to one side and not think about it but I hope by speaking about it it might help others to know they can too, and it wasn’t their fault.

“I also hope this can help other people not be in the same situation that I was in. I’ve been speaking with an amazing charity Rape Crisis who I wish I’d known about at the time. They offer 24/7 support and advice if anyone needs it.”

In the book, Grace says the first assault happened when the man who was her manager during a week of work experience offered to give her a lift in on her second day. "He was about 27 so around ten years older, attractive, tattooed and muscly, and I was impressed by him – I was flattered that he was giving me the time of day," she explains. "However, as we were driving in that morning, he kept touching my leg which was making me feel uncomfortable although I didn’t feel able to ask him to stop. There was a massive imbalance of power going on which he was 100 per cent taking advantage of, banking on the fact I wouldn’t push back."

‌



He assaulted her that day, and the rape took place on the last day of her week with the company. She writes: "At 4pm on my last day, he kicked out the two other members of staff who were there, leaving only me and him in the building. I start to panic because I feel like I know what’s about to happen but I’m powerless to stop it. He signals me towards a side room, making a point of saying there are no cameras in there and I go in because, again, there’s no ability in my body to refuse. I’m also pretty certain he’s locked the office, so I’m trapped.

"And then he rapes me. It’s taken me a long time – years, in fact – to realise that’s what it was. Even longer to be able to say it out loud." She now reflects: “I wish I’d known that it wasn’t my fault. I wish I’d known what to be on guard for. I’d had no idea that rape can take so many different forms and it doesn’t always look the way you expect. I think we imagine it to be a stranger attack in a dark alley, but it’s far more likely to happen between people who know each other – friends, partners, classmates or colleagues."

Grace's book is published by Penguin, which includes an overview that is written by the TV and social media star. She explains in a statement: "I should probably tell you what this book isn’t. It’s not an autobiography (I’m still too fresh out the womb) or self-development guide (er, be real).

‌



"Neither does it contain a magic formula that’s going to give you the solution to surviving every plot twist life decides to throw at you. None of my ‘advice’ – and I use the term in the loosest possible sense – should be taken as gospel. Or even at all."

Explaining that she is simply sharing the details of life as she has experienced it so far, she adds: "I’m laying every last bit of personal trauma out there for the greater good of humanity which basically makes me a saint and you can thank me later."

** If you've been the victim of sexual assault, you can access help and resources via www.rapecrisis.org.uk or calling the national telephone helpline on 0808 802 9999

News.title: Gareth Gates stuns fans with Pride performance in tiny trunks and bottomless pink chaps
News.content:
Gareth Gates stuns fans with Pride performance in tiny trunks and bottomless pink chaps

Pop Idol star, Gareth Gates, sent fans into a frenzy at Manchester Pride this weekend when he rocked up on stage belting out his greatest hits and showing off his buff body

View 5 Images Pop Idol finalist, Gareth Gates, looked a world away from his squeaky clean debut on the ITV show (Image: FARRELL / BACKGRID)

Pop Idol finalist, Gareth Gates, looked a world away from his squeaky clean debut on the ITV show 25 years ago at Manchester Pride this weekend.

‌



The singer, 42, who was only 17 when he shot to fame with show winner, Will Young, on the iconic talent series, sent fans into a frenzy when he rocked up on stage showing off his ultra buff body.

‌



Singing his heart out, sporting in a number of revealing outfits, including a pair of tiny trunks - as well as an eye-popping pair of bottomless pink chaps - the dad-of-one looked like he was having the time of his life.

‌



5 View 5 Images Pop Idol star, Gareth Gates, sent fans into a frenzy at Manchester Pride (Image: FARRELL / BACKGRID) 5 View 5 Images He whipped off his jeans to reveal his tiny trunks (Image: FARRELL / BACKGRID)

With slick choreography, Gareth had the crowd on their feet as he whipped off his jeans to reveal a pair of tiny sequin-strewn underpants. As fans whooped and cheered the Bradford-born star had a smile a mile wide as his audience screamed with excitement.

Gareth shot to fame on Pop Idol as a spiky haired teenager with a stutter when he lost out to Will Young in the first-ever offering of the show back in 2002.

‌



Then an overnight success, the star found himself mixing with a whole host of famous faces, including Katie Price.

Katie, then known as glamour model, Jordan, claims she took Gareth's virginity in news which hit all the headlines. Setting the story straight on Jamie Laing's podcast recently, the singer said: "I'll just say I was extremely inexperienced with a girl who was extremely experienced. I could see why she thought that.

5 View 5 Images Cheeky! (Image: FARRELL / BACKGRID) 5 View 5 Images Gareth shot to fame on Pop Idol at the age of 17 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"I haven't ever spoken about relationships. I believe that relationships are between two people and I couldn't believe that somebody else was selling stories about very, very intimate details."

Admitting the story being splashed all over the newspapers was a "real learning curve" he added: "And I was shocked and I learned a lot about that - about people and about the industry, and about trust I guess. I would never have ever done that to her or to anybody else, and so it was a real learning curve for me."

Despite losing out to Will on Pop Idol, Gareth was finally crowned victorious when he won Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins in 2023.

Article continues below

Speaking to the Mirror about the gruelling experience, he said: "It actually felt like I’d been preparing for this my whole life. The struggle with my speech and having to be mentally strong to hear them say [I had passed]. I was like, ‘Wow, this is incredible’.

"I thought at last, I’ve actually won a talent TV show and not came second this time. It was a massive weight off my shoulders. I’ve finally redeemed myself from being the biggest loser in the UK back in 2002."

News.title: Nepal floods teacher saves more than 1,600 lives with alarm calls as death toll tops 700 and thousands missing
News.content:
Nepal floods teacher saves more than 1,600 lives with alarm calls as death toll tops 700 and thousands missing

A teacher at a school directly in the path of the horror torrent that crushed buildings along the Trishuli river has been credited with saving every child and all but two staff

People trapped on balcony in Nepal floods

A quick-thinking teacher who sounded the alarm as a wall of water came crashing down a major river in Nepal has been credited with saving more than 1,600 lives.

‌



Principal Rajendra Dawadi, 47, had already welcomed 900 children to his school, the Tribhuvan Trishuli secondary school in the Trishuli valley of north-central Nepal, when he received an urgent phonecall from a friend on Wednesday, August 26. The friend informed him that the school five miles up river had been taken in the devastating floodwaters that would go on to kill 752 people in Nepal alone, and 16 in Tibet, and leave more than 2,500 others missing.

‌



The impending doom rushing down the Trishuli river to Mr Dawadi's school could have killed another 1,643 people, but they were saved thanks to his quick thinking.

‌



Final happy photo of Brits on Nepal tour - then they were gone READ MORE :

View 7 Images The Tribhuvan Trishuli secondary school was swept away in the floods (Image: FACEBOOK)

The Times reports that floodwaters put every single one of the 900 children already at school and 700 more arriving by bus in the path of a deadly torrent of water, with the Tribhuvan Trishuli secondary school located just 200 feet - 60 metres - from the river's banks.

As the severe floods tore through the Himalayan river system, Mr Dawadi sounded the school bell and told teachers to get the children out of their classrooms.

‌



The teacher then called the drivers of approaching school buses, asking them to turn back moments before they crossed the bridge to their campus. With the warning extended, some of the children had started to panic as they realised the danger.

View 7 Images Principal Rajendra Dawadi saved all his students from the flood

Mr Dawadi followed people rushing away on foot, and after finding shelter under a bodhi tree watched the floodwaters sweep away their school buildings.

‌



He decided not to delay any longer after reports came that floodwaters had already swept through the upstream settlement of Betrawati. "Even if the flood was not coming, it was just a matter of a single day's classes," he told the BBC.

As they evacuated to higher ground, Dawadi could see a hostel building about 100m (328ft) from the river being engulfed by floodwaters. "If we had made the decision 10 minutes later, all of us, including the students and me, would not be able to speak to you today."

Every child and all but two staff members were saved by the principal's quick thinking. Santos Pariyar, 32, was sadly washed away after he returned to his rented room beside the rapidly rising river to cook breakfast that morning. Sultan Lama, the janitor, was killed as a returned to close the doors.

‌



The children saved by Mr Dawadi were lucky not to have been impacted by the water, but others were only rescued after becoming caught in the deadly deluge. One of the 900 students saved by the headteacher's decision was 16-year-old Yunisha, who says she escaped only moments before the flood.

"I, along with my friends, survived by just 10 seconds," she told the BBC. Yunisha describes running up a narrow and muddy route behind the school with other students. "Within no time, the bazaar was swept away in front of my eyes", she added.

Yunisha, who was speaking alongside her mother Sabina Shrestha, said the family spent hours desperately trying to contact her after hearing news of the flood.

‌



"I was panicking. I tried multiple calls to my daughter and her father, but both were not reachable." When she finally got through, Shrestha recalls feeling some relief. But the family remained anxious until Yunisha returned home - three days later. "I am so happy and relieved. God saved my girl."

View 7 Images Photos show hollowed out buildings in flood-hit areas (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Urgent rescue operations launched

One five-year-old girl, Manisha, was rescued two days after the floods by emergency teams in Syabrubesi, in Nepal's Ruswa district. She was reunited with her parents at the Teaching Hospital in Kathmandu, the BBC reports, and is in stable condition after emergency workers were alerted to what they thought was a cat miaowing under rubble.

‌



Police officer Sanju Khatri, with Nepal's Armed Police Force, said teams found Manisha trapped after they started moving debris, and it took them two hours to free her.

Other rescuers have been attempting to reach hydropower workers believed to have been trapped in tunnels on the Trishuli 3A and 3B sites which have been clogged by flood debris. On Sunday, they deployed heavy machinery as rain and rising river waters hampered their earlier efforts.

View 7 Images People were seen desperately scrambling for safety both before and after the disaster (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Nepal's energy ministry said in a statement: "Drilling of four holes has been completed... preparations are now underway to enter the tunnel directly... and proceed with search and rescue operations."

Also rescued were Laxmi Pandey Pyakurel and her family, who were trapped on a balcony at their home as they were surrounded by floodwaters. Now viral footage showed the family looking down onto the grey waters with seemingly nowhere to run. Laxmi, 42, told the Daily Telegraph: “We saw death very closely. Death was staring at every one of us. We thought these were our final moments. I told everyone that if we had to die, we would die together.”

Brits missing following disaster

As well as local residents swept up in the horror, hundreds of tourists, including 33 Brits, have been reported as missing. Among them is former Mrs India UK Surabhi Manmath Padhy and her husband, Santosh Sahu, who were in the country with their 18-year-old son Spandan and 13-year-old daughter Saina, when the floods hit.

‌



They had reportedly travelled to Nepal en route to Kailash Mansarovar, but have not been heard from since communications were wiped out by the floods.

Spandan had just finished his A-levels at Royal Grammar School, Guildford, and according to his Linkedin page was preparing for a degree in philosophy, politics and economics. A spokesperson for his school said they have been "reported missing" in Nepal.

View 7 Images Satellite footage shows where the massive torrent of water burst the banks of the Himalayan rivers (Image: 2026 Planet Labs PBC/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



They said: "It is with great concern that we have been informed that a former student, along with members of his family, have been reported missing in Nepal.

"Whilst we are hoping for positive news, we do not have any further information at this time. Our thoughts, love and deepest sympathies are with all of the families and loved ones of anyone affected by this tragedy in Nepal at this incredibly difficult time."

The brother of another missing Brit, Neetu Goyal Tiwari, has pleaded "help us find her" after revealing she had not been seen since Wednesday.

‌



View 7 Images Rescuers are digging through a mass of dirt carried down river by the flooding (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

He said his family has " called every helpline given by the Indian government and reached out to the British Embassy in Kathmandu" as they are "very scared" while worrying about what may have happened. Newlywed food truck owner Pramod Poudel said his wife Sumitra went missing following the floods and started his own search for her.

He told The Sun that her last words to him were "I love you so much", saying: “When I last spoke to her, she said to me, ‘How are you? I love you so much.’

‌



“I have not had contact with her since then. It’s devastating — I don’t even know how to explain how I’m feeling right now. I’m so worried about her, and all my family. I work so hard for them and they are my whole world. I’m very hopeful of finding them but I’m also praying to God.”

More flood warnings

Flood warning notices were sent to people's phones early Sunday as rescue crews worked to clear a major highway connecting Kathmandu to one of the areas worst hit by Wednesday's catastrophic floods, as some residents began returning to ruined homes to see what can be salvaged.

Residents sat in homes with walls washed away by the floods, shovelling sludge-like mud and rubble off balconies or window frames.

‌



The latest warnings came after Chinese authorities informed their Nepalese counterparts of increased water flow upstream, according to Dharam Raj Uprety, chief executive of Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.

View 7 Images Footage taken on the ground shows people stuck in mud and slush following the disaster (Image: Nepalese Army/AFP via Getty Images)

But residents of the flood-hit villages said they were struggling to make sense of near-constant alarms they've received since the initial floods.

Article continues below

"Sometimes they say a flood is coming, then we have to run again to higher ground, even at night. There is also rain," said Govind Shreshta, a resident. "It's really difficult for me. I have a 72-year-old father and 70-year-old mom. I must carry them and I am exhausted. It's going on like this for those who are still alive."

News.title: Head teacher evacuated 900 children minutes before Nepal floods hit school
News.content:
At first, many students did not realise how serious the situation was.

Pupil Yunisha Amatya, 16, said she scrambled to safety with her friends just before the flood hit.

"I along with my friends survived by just 10 seconds only," she told the BBC.

"Just before the flood came, we were in the class studying. Teachers had gathered in one place and initially had no idea what had happened. After five minutes teachers came and informed us about the flood and asked us to go home."

She said one student fainted after hearing about the disaster, but many initially underestimated the danger and waited for classmates who were in a maths lesson.

Yunisha and her friends scrambled uphill through an escape route behind the school.

"I could not walk fast, and my friends helped me to climb uphill. We tried our best to be in the safer zones then. We escaped through a narrow ladder from backside of the school. Within no time, the bazaar was swept away in front of my eyes," she says, referring to the local market around the school.

"If there was no grip in my shoes I would have fallen and students and other people were jostling each other to reach the safer area while escaping. The people who choose to escape from another route are apparently swept away."

News.title: Seven killed and 23 missing in boat capsizing off northern Cyprus
News.content:
At least seven people have died and 23 others are still missing after a passenger boat capsized off northern Cyprus, the head of the Turkish administration there has said.

Ãnal Ãstel, prime minister of the self-proclaimed Turkish republic there, said the ferry had been carrying 259 passengers and eight crew members when it began taking on water after departing the coastal town of Kyrenia.

The ship's captain and seven crew members have been detained as part of an investigation into "how this tragedy occurred", Ãstel wrote on social media.

A search and rescue operation to find the passengers still unaccounted for is under way, which Turkish authorities have joined. Turkish media is reporting the death toll has risen to eight.

The privately owned ferry left the left the popular holiday resort of Kyrenia at 12:30 local time (09:30 GMT), local media reported.

Ãstel said the boat had been scheduled to travel to Turkey on Saturday, but had been delayed due to poor weather conditions.

He told Turkish media outlet TRT that the boat was hit by two waves before it capsized.

While the captain of the vessel was trying to recover from the first wave, a second wave hit and it began taking on water, he told the outlet.

News.title: PC Harper's killers to stay in jail as PM announces changes to early release scheme
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has told the BBC that PC Andrew Harper's killers will remain behind bars as he announced changes to the early release scheme aimed at easing prison overcrowding.

In an exclusive interview with BBC Breakfast, Burnham said anyone convicted of unlawful killing, including all forms of manslaughter, would be excluded from the scheme, which would have made two of the officer's killers eligible for early release.

Burnham said extra prison space would be created by deporting foreign prisoners and releasing some inmates serving indefinite sentences.

It follows months of campaigning from PC Harper's family and former colleagues to block the release of his killers.

The 28-year-old was responding to a burglary in Berkshire in 2019 when he was dragged along a road by a vehicle as three teenagers fled the scene of a quad bike theft.

When it emerged that two of the killers, Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, could be released early, there were passionate calls for the government to intervene and block those convicted of manslaughter from early release.

"I heard obviously what Andrew Harper's family were saying, I mean who couldn't? Nobody would want a position to arise where those guilty of killing a police officer are let out early from prison," Burnham told the BBC.

He conceded the announcement would mean "hundreds" more people stay in prison, meaning additional space will need to be found in a system that is more than 97% full in England and Wales.

News.title: "A giant leap forward": Nasa launches powerful new space telescope to explore mysteries of the Universe
News.content:
Nasa's powerful next-generation telescope has blasted off into space from its launchpad in Florida, with a mission to explore dark energy, black holes and other mysteries of the Universe.

The Nancy Grace Roman telescope will capture vast panoramic views of space, with a field of vision 100 times larger than both the Hubble and James Webb space telescopes, Nasa says.

The mission begins with a 100-day journey to a vantage point roughly one million miles from Earth, where the telescope will then start charting planets outside our solar system, known as exoplanets.

"Roman is going to change the way we look at the Universe," said Nicky Fox, a Nasa administrator.

News.title: Sons of officer who died in A66 crash lead out Man Utd as mascots
News.content:
The two sons of a police officer killed in a crash on Teesside led out the Manchester United team as mascots for Sunday's Premier League match against Ipswich at Old Trafford.

PC Matthew Blades, described as a "proud Red" by United, was a regular at Old Trafford.

The club paid tribute to him in Sunday's match programme, while his widow attended the game with their children.

PC Blades and his colleague PC Tom Clough died in a head-on collision between their police car and a vehicle going the wrong way on the A66 near Middlesbrough early on 22 August. Five people in the other vehicle also died.

United said they learned of the deaths of the two officers "with great sadness".

"Matthew was a proud Red, a devoted family man and a police officer who dedicated his life to helping others," said the club, in a tribute in the programme.

At Elland Road, match officials for Leeds United's Premier League fixture against Brentford on Sunday wore black armbands as referee Tony Harrington was a friend of PC Blades.

On Saturday, there was a minute's applause in memory of PC Blades and PC Clough before Middlesbrough's Championship encounter with West Brom at Riverside Stadium. Pictures of the two men were displayed on a screen.

People also gathered to pay tribute at Seaton Carew FC's game against FC Hartlepool. PC Blades had been a junior football coach at both teams.

Earlier this week, 17 people were arrested in connection with the investigation into the crash, bringing the total number of arrests to 24.

The occupants of the other vehicle, a Passat - Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, 17, and Cole Robert Worthy, 17, also died.

News.title: Church names pastor killed by falling sign at Christian festival
News.content:
The man killed at a Christian festival in West Sussex on Friday has been named by his church as Robert Guanco, 41.

He was a pastor at Jesus the Living Water Church in Eastbourne, East Sussex.

Six other people were injured at the event by a falling sign at the Big Church Festival, near Steyning, four of whom were taken to hospital for treatment.

In a statement, his church said: "Pastor Robert was a faithful servant of God, a loving husband to Isay, a devoted and caring father to Ellie, and a blessing to so many people whose lives he touched. His life, his faith, his love, and his service to God will never be forgotten."

On a fundraising page for Guanco's family, pastor Norman Ponce from Jesus the Living Water Worldwide Church, said he was a "faithful servant of God".

"What was meant to be a time of worship, fellowship, and celebration became an unimaginable tragedy," he added.

Ponce said Guanco was a "beloved son, cherished brother, loving husband" and "great father".

"He was also a good friend, mentor, and a blessing to so many people whose lives he touched," Ponce said.

"His life reflected humility, faith, love, compassion, and service. Through his ministry, kindness, prayers, and encouragement, he touched many lives."

News.title: Police release one of two men arrested over fatal house fire
News.content:
A 31-year-old man arrested on suspicion of murder over a fatal house fire has been released with no further action while a second man, aged 23, continues to be questioned.

Natalie McDonald, 34, died in the blaze in Grangetown, near Middlesbrough, in the early hours of Wednesday, along with her niece Valentina Foster, seven.

Cleveland Police said a 48-year-old woman had been left in a critical condition in hospital and another three people had injuries that were not life-threatening.

The force added enquiries were ongoing.

Natalie's mother, Lisa Kirton, described her as "a beautiful soul, who would have done anything for anybody".

Valentina, who was known as Tina, was staying at the house for the summer holidays and had been "dancing around the living room" only the previous night.

"She was a cute little kid," Kirton said. "I can't believe it, seven years old - it's just a disgrace."

In an update on Friday afternoon, Cleveland Police ACC Dave Sutherland said the force was not currently linking the fire to a crash on the A66, in which seven people died, including two police officers.
