News.title: British woman killed in stabbing at German railway station
News.content:
A British woman has died after being stabbed at a railway station in southern Germany in the early hours of Sunday morning, police have said.

The 31-year-old woman was attacked at the station in Rosenheim, Bavaria, shortly before 01:00 local time (00:00BST). She was taken to hospital where she died as a result of "severe" injuries, the Bavarian Police said in a statement.

Officers arrested a 27-year-old German man at the scene immediately after the incident. The background and motive for the attack is under investigation, the statement added.

Police have asked anyone who may have witnessed "an argument or physical altercation" at the station late on Saturday or early on Sunday to contact them.

The suspect, from the FÃ¼rstenfeldbruck district, will be brought before magistrates later on Sunday, according to German news agency DPA.

It is not known if the two knew each other or what the woman was doing in Bavaria, DPA also reported.

Rosenheim is one of the largest cities in Upper Bavaria and is a busy rail hub for passengers travelling to Austrian cities including Vienna, Salzburg and Innsbruck.

The Rosenheimer Herbstfest - an event similar to the Oktoberfest beer festival - is currently taking place in the area.

Responding to the attack, Rosenheim Mayor Abuzar Erdogan said "there are no indications of a security threat in our city or of any link to our Herbstfest".

"The criminal investigation department is working closely with the public prosecutor's office to investigate the circumstances and motive behind the crime as a matter of urgency," he wrote in a statement.

A Foreign Office spokesperson told the BBC: "We are supporting the family of a British woman who died in Germany [and] are in touch with the local authorities."

News.title: Burnham gets the early prison release changes he wanted - but at what cost?
News.content:
The prime minister's announcement that he will keep hundreds of criminals behind bars who would otherwise have been released early is one he has wanted to make for weeks.

Andy Burnham had already expanded the list of people ineligible for early release and had consistently said he wanted to go further.

What is not clear is exactly what has changed to allow him to do so.

Earlier this month, the Ministry of Justice warned that exempting any more prisoners risked "prisons reaching capacity and collapsing".

The prime minister himself previously said he had "pushed to the very limits of what is possible to do".

In his exclusive interview with BBC Breakfast, Burnham picked out the release of people on controversial indefinite sentences and the deportation of foreign criminals as measures that had made his latest intervention possible.

It is understood extra capacity will also be created by immediately beginning work to create new cells in existing prisons.

But none of these are short-term solutions.

Ending indefinite sentences will require new legislation, meaning it could be years before space is freed up.

Previous governments have struggled to quickly deport foreign offenders and there are not thought to be any new returns agreements with other countries. The case of grooming gang ringleader Shabir Ahmed, who Pakistan has resisted attempts to deport, is one example.

Retrofitting prisons to create more cells is also expected to take months.

People in government concede that in the short-term, Burnham will only be able to follow through on today's announcement by making prisons even more full.

With the adult male prison estate already running at 98% capacity, it is a move that could worry some in the sector.

But in the end, the prime minister believed he simply had to act.

The extra exemptions Burnham has announced are being described within government as a "political decision".

That is not surprising given the intense pressure that had built up, especially around the potential for PC Andrew Harper's killers to be released early.

Burnham's inner circle are mindful that political misjudgements at the start of Sir Keir Starmer's premiership caused long-lasting damage.

They believe Sir Keir never recovered from early rows over freebies and winter fuel payments, and point to a lack of major mishaps in Burnham's first six weeks in office as evidence of a more slick political operation.

There was some surprise in Downing Street about how much media attention the issue of early release received over the summer.

That is one reason why the prime minister's aides are relishing the new parliamentary term, when news stories come along at a faster rate and so are less likely to linger in the headlines.

After the initial flip-flopping on whether the government would be able to exempt more prisoners, the mother of PC Harper told BBC Breakfast that the handling of the situation had been a "hash".

Government officials working on the plans have spoken to the families of victims, who made it clear they did not want the new measures to be dripped out in leaks to the media.

Instead it was decided one big announcement would be the neatest option.

It had seemed likely that would come in the form of a parliamentary statement on Tuesday from the justice secretary.

Instead, the prime minister decided to make the announcement himself in an interview with BBC Breakfast.

It is understood Burnham was mindful of mounting speculation and wanted to give victims and the public as much certainty at the earliest possible opportunity.

In doing so, he may have risked the ire of the Speaker Sir Lindsay Hoyle, who is generally disdainful of governments that make major announcements outside of Parliament.

He may also have offered up ammunition to the Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch, who has already accused Burnham of being a "people pleaser" who finds it difficult to say no to people.

That characterisation is likely to be tested again when more stories inevitably appear about the victims of prisoners who will still be released early.

It already started on Sunday morning, when the domestic abuse commissioner said she remained "deeply concerned about the number of abusers" still set to be freed.

While this is not the first time Burnham has said he has pushed the system to the limit, Whitehall sources are now adamant there will be no more additional exemptions.

News.title: Two missing as French fishing boat sinks in Channel
News.content:
Searches are continuing for two crew members after a French fishing boat sank in the English Channel, the Maritime and Coastguard Agency said.

A coastguard rescue helicopter, fixed-wing plane and two RNLI lifeboats began searching an area south-west of Eddystone Lighthouse off Plymouth after the crew released a distress call at 18:00 BST on Saturday.

HM Coastguard in Falmouth said three people were rescued from the boat and have been taken to hospital.

A large number of civilian vessels are assisting the "intensive search" for the two remaining crew members, an HM Coastguard spokesperson added.

They also confirmed that the search is continuing this afternoon.

They said: "An HM Coastguard aircraft equipped with the latest technology including a multi -function search radar and high resolution cameras has been sent.

"Mayday relay broadcasts are continuing, requesting vessels in the area to keep a sharp lookout."

Lifeboat crews from Newlyn and Salcombe have taken over the search from the Plymouth and Falmouth RNLI crews, who worked through the night.

News.title: Third murder charge over Brent Council HQ stabbing
News.content:
A total of three people have now been charged with murder over the fatal stabbing of a 17-year-old boy at Brent Civic Centre in Wembley.

David Wynter died after he was attacked on Engineers Way at about 14:30 BST on 25 August.

A 15-year-old boy was charged with murder two days later, and two more teenagers - a 17-year-old boy and 18-year-old Jahquarn St Hillaire - were charged with murder and possession of an offensive weapon on Saturday.

The 15-year-old was remanded in custody and is due to appear at the Old Bailey on 24 September, with the other pair due at Willesden Magistrates' Court on Monday.

News.title: Dementia patient's deportation from Sweden delayed
News.content:
A man with dementia will be able to remain in Sweden while a legal bid to delay his deportation is considered.

The Swedish authorities said they wanted George Mason, originally from Hinckley in Leicestershire, to leave the country by midnight on 20 August, after his application for permanent residency was rejected.

Mason's daughter, Michelle Torossian, said the family had been told an injunction to halt his deportation would be decided by Swedish authorities in a timeframe of two weeks to six months.

Torossian said she was told by the British Embassy in Stockholm that the original deportation decision would not be enforced by the authorities while the injunction order was considered.

The BBC has contacted the Swedish Migration Agency, which said it was unable to comment on individual cases.

News.title: Two murder arrests after balcony fall man dies
News.content:
Two men have been arrested on suspicion of murder after a man who fell from a balcony died.

Officers were called to reports that the man had fallen at flats on Liverpool Street in Salford shortly after midnight on Saturday, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said.

The force said the man died later that night. A man arrested on suspicion of attempted murder has now been arrested on suspicion of murder.

A second man has also been arrested on suspicion of murder.

The incident has been referred to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) because the men had earlier contact with police, GMP said.

An IOPC spokesperson said: "After being notified by the Greater Manchester Police of the previous police contact with the parties involved in this incident, we sent investigators to the police post-incident procedures in Manchester in assessment mode to gather further information.

"We continue to remain in assessment mode and will assess a GMP referral in due course."

News.title: Girl faces six-month recovery after 'freak accident' bus crash on holiday
News.content:
After eight days in hospital, Greta was transported back to the UK for treatment with Williams in an air ambulance which their Â£106 travel insurance policy covered.

"They [the pilots and medics] told me it cost â¬50,000 just for the flight. That was quite scary, Â£106 paid for that. Anything can happen."

Williams said Jet2, which sold them the package holiday, waived the cost of changing Len and Eiry-ana's flights back to the UK.

Greta was admitted to The Grange University Hospital in Cwmbran and had physiotherapy, and will find out on 2 September whether she can return to school.

"We can't do anything until that assessment. It's strict bedrest at the minute.

"She's not allowed to do much, she's not allowed to walk loads or do much which is a massive shame. Her friends have been fantastic."

Williams added: "She was petrified when it happened. All she wanted was reassurance from me. We tried to keep it as positive as we could in the circumstances.

"She was phenomenally strong. I'm so proud of how she coped."

"This is something that's going to haunt us forever," added Williams.

"It's going to take a long time to get over it all. We need normality to hit first, as we're in the summer holidays, before we can process it properly.

"You can see the accident has impacted them, and being in a foreign country has escalated their fears.

"We were trying to fill it in with so many experiences and memories as possible to make it fun-filled.

"They don't want to go on holiday ever again. We're going to try and take them somewhere - probably not on an excursion - to ease their mind. It was a one-off freak accident, and these things don't generally happen."

Graeme Buck from the Association of British Travel Agents said travel insurance was "one of the must-haves whenever you travel overseas".

"While most holidays go ahead without any problems, accidents and unexpected events can happen, and the costs of medical treatment and getting home can be significant.

"Cheap isn't always the best, and it's important not to choose a policy based on price alone. Holidaymakers should check what their policy covers and make sure they have comprehensive cover that is appropriate for their trip, including any activities they plan to take part in, such as winter sports."

News.title: Heavyweight Itauma handed harsh world-title lesson
News.content:
It would be too simplistic - and unfair - to say Hrgovic won the fight purely through mind games, but the 34-year-old had succeeded in making the build-up uncomfortable.

Hrgovic spent fight week repeatedly attacking Itauma's age, dismissing him as "just a kid". As the week wore on, Itauma looked increasingly irritated and eventually lost his composure at the weigh-in, shoving Hrgovic before the Croatian responded with a slap.

Itauma prides himself on being unusually cerebral for a heavyweight. He reads psychology and self-help books, talks openly about sharpening his mind and appears to spend far more time analysing himself than most 21-year-olds.

But there is always a danger that deep thinking becomes overthinking, something Anthony Joshua has been accused of repeatedly during the latter stages of his career.

Whether the pre-fight barbs played any part or not, Itauma's gameplan once the bell rang was clear; he wanted to end the night early.

"Someone said to me he doesn't feel like he'd win a world title unless he knocks him out. I didn't like that," Warren said.

That mindset was understandable because it had served Itauma extraordinarily well until now. But perhaps Hrgovic had been underestimated by almost everybody - Itauma, the media, pundits, former fighters and bookmakers who installed the Briton as a heavy favourite.

Hrgovic is an Olympic bronze medallist who went 12 hard rounds with the giant Zhilei Zhang, while against Daniel Dubois - the only defeat on his record - he was leading on two of the three scorecards before the fight was stopped because of cuts.

'El Animal' knew what it felt like to be hurt, to become tired and to remain in a fight when things were going badly. Itauma did not.

News.title: Swimmers told to avoid beauty spot as 'hidden hazards' revealed by drought and fires
News.content:
People have been warned to stay away from a popular beauty spot pond used for swimming and other water sports due to "hidden hazards" exposed by reduced water levels.

Keepers Pond in Abergavenny poses "serious safety risks" with levels dangerously low, according to Bannau Brycheiniog National Park, also known as the Brecon Beacons.

It said that along with the prolonged dry spell, the water had been used to tackle recent wildfires.

"As the water has receded, previously hidden hazards and unknown objects have been exposed on the pond bed, creating serious safety risks. For your own safety, you must not enter the water under any circumstances," the park authority said in a Facebook post, external.

News.title: The Bruno Fernandes show gives Manchester United lift off in Premier League
News.content:

New season but a distinctly familiar script for Manchester United. They could be grateful for that, too. Even after a summer when they have spent £150m on midfielders, their finest remains the same. It is no secret that Bruno Fernandes is by far and away their outstanding individual in the era since Sir Alex Ferguson retired. In the week he was crowned PFA Player of the Year, Fernandes began his bid to retain the award with a reminder of his extraordinary productivity. A third United hat-trick was followed by his first assists of the season. What began as proof of his capacity to spring comebacks turned into a masterclass that inspired a rout.

Recognition from his fellow players came in a campaign when Fernandes was the creator supreme, with a record 21 Premier League assists. Nevertheless, he only scored nine goals. Now, after serving as the scourge of Ipswich, he is a third of the way to that tally already. United, unconvincing initially, were rampant at the end, Fernandes the catalyst for a transformation. An eventual tally of 33 shots was testament to the attacking ambition of Michael Carrick’s team.

It was the first time in five years that United scored five times in a Premier League game; that, against Leeds, also featured a Fernandes treble and came when Carrick was on Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s coaching staff. If this scoreline had echoes of the United of old, they showed defensive frailties, a cavalier streak and a willingness to carry on charging forward.

open image in gallery Leif Davis (centre) fired Ipswich into the lead ( AP )

open image in gallery Bruno Fernandes got the equaliser before scoring again from the penalty spot ( Reuters )

It helped that, in Fernandes, they have a player who rarely takes the safe option in his bid to make something happen. Often the provider in his thirties, he underlined his ability to score different types of goals. He has never possessed raw pace but, when Marcelino Nunez slipped and Matheus Cunha capitalised to feed the ball forward, he ran in behind the Ipswich defence to level with an unstoppable shot.

Fernandes had missed two spot kicks in pre-season. Undaunted, he slotted in a penalty from 12 yards after Cunha was felled by Jacob Greaves; the Brazilian has spent too little of his time as the auxiliary No 9 making driving runs into the box but when he did, it brought a caution for the defender and a goal for United.

Fernandes’ third illustrated his predatory instinct. He was lurking near the penalty spot when Bryan Mbeumo’s misdirected shot fell to him. The Portuguese’s aim was better, finding the corner of the net. It was not Mbeumo’s only piece of faulty finishing – from a yard, he managed to knee the ball against the bar from Marcus Rashford’s volleyed cross – but when he did score, it got Fernandes off the mark in his quest for another 21 assists.

open image in gallery Fernandes completed his hat-trick and set up Bryan Mbuemo's goal ( Getty )

open image in gallery Harry Maguire's deflected shot was controversially awarded as a Jacob Greaves own goal despite a potential handball in the build-up ( Getty )

It was classic Fernandes, with the quarterback pass from deep for the advancing runner. With goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen caught in no-man’s land, Mbeumo’s lob went in off the underside of the bar. It was not United’s most audacious effort: that was Fernandes, performing his best David Beckham impression, trying to score from the half-way line and coming very close as he instead found the roof of the net.

United’s other goal came courtesy of his predecessor as captain, even if it was not credited to him. Harry Maguire’s drilled shot put United ahead but if Ipswich were irritated a handball in the build-up was not given, a deflection off the luckless Greaves was the reason and meant it was deemed an own goal.

With that, though, the chance of a first Ipswich win at Old Trafford since 1984 disappeared. The eventual scoreline suggested otherwise but Town were the better side in the first half, United at risk of the wrong sort of double against promoted clubs, following last Saturday’s loss to Hull.

open image in gallery Marcus Rashford had a fine outing for the hosts having been awarded a starting berth ( Reuters )

open image in gallery Ipswich's Chuba Akpom scored a late consolation in torrential rain ( PA )

Initially, United were open to the counter-attack and reliant on Senne Lammens to preserve parity, Julio Enciso running clear from his own half to have a shot blocked by the goalkeeper and Daizen Maeda seeing a vicious shot brilliantly tipped wide.

Warnings went unheeded. Ipswich led when Abdul Fatawu, fresh from consecutive relegations with Leicester, nonetheless looked electric as he burst past Luke Shaw to find Leif Davis, whose shot went in off the underside of the bar.

Amid torrential rain in the closing stages, United did not look watertight at the back when Ipswich added a late second, scored by Chuba Akpom after Lisandro Martinez lost the ball to Enciso.

Yet it was a footnote. It was tempting to recall that, in the sunshine before kick-off, United had presented this week’s recruit Carlos Baleba to the crowd. Then, the focus was on the new. By the end, and after the latest episode of the Fernandes show, it was all about the old.

News.title: Burnham’s pledge to scrap indefinite jail terms brings campaigners ‘justice and hope’ after years of anguish
News.content:
The Way Back. Read our Privacy notice

The prime minister’s pledge to end the scandal of indefinite jail terms “will finally bring justice and hope” to thousands of prisoners languishing without a release date, campaigners say.

Andy Burnham announced on Sunday he will “end the injustice” of Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) jail terms by the end of this parliament as he unveiled plans to limit the number of other prisoners being released early, including Pc Andrew Harper’s killers.

The Independent has long campaigned for all IPP prisoners to have their sentences reviewed, highlighting the plight of thousands jailed without hope.

Campaigners have hailed the move as an “essential first step towards healing” after years of anguish.

“This will finally bring justice and hope to IPPs and their families,” said Bernadette Emerson, co-founder of the IPP Solidarity Movement, whose husband Abdullahi Suleman has served almost 20 years for a laptop robbery.

His case, previously reported by The Independent, formed part a major complaint to the United Nations, which issued a damning legal opinion issued last month concluding he and several other IPP prisoners are being arbitrarily detained. The government is now facing a major legal challenge over their imprisonment.

open image in gallery Clockwise, from top left: Leroy Douglas, Luke Ings, Liam Bennett, Wayne Williams, Abdullahi Suleman, Yusuf Ali, James Lawrence and Thomas White are all trapped on IPP sentences ( Samantha Ings/Margaret White/Mandy Lawrence/Jacqueline Ali /Handout )

Campaigner Shirley Debono, whose son Shaun Lloyd has been recalled five times and served nearly 14 years for snatching a phone, said she was “absolutely overwhelmed”.

“After all these years of campaigning, fighting, being ignored and watching IPP prisoners and their families suffer, to finally hear the prime minister say he will end the injustice of IPP sentences this parliament feels incredible,” said the mother, who co-founded IPP Committee in Action.

“The words “people will no longer be trapped indefinitely under a sentence abolished more than a decade ago” are something I never thought I would hear from a prime minister.

“I’m so excited, but also emotional, because I know what this has meant for so many families. I’m thinking of every IPP prisoner who has spent years trapped under this sentence and every family who has fought alongside them.”

Campaign group United Group for Reform of IPP (UNGRIPP) said the IPP nightmare may finally be ending, halting “decades of disproportionate punishment, institutional trauma, and loss of hope”.

CEO Marc Conway said: “This is a day that thousands of families have spent years fighting for. For too long, their loved ones have been trapped by a sentence that was acknowledged as flawed over a decade ago.

“While we welcome this critical action by the government, we do so with heavy hearts for those who did not live to see this day, and for the families torn apart by years of endless uncertainty.

“Legislation alone cannot undo twenty years of damage, but it is the essential first step toward healing.”

open image in gallery Andy Burnham said he will bring legislation to end the injustice of IPP sentences this parliament ( PA Wire )

Tragically, the move comes too late for 96 IPP prisoners who took their own lives after losing hope of getting out, including Tommy Nicol, who died aged 37 in 2015. Before he died, Tommy described his IPP sentence as “psychological torture of a person who is doing 99 years.”

UNGRIPP urged the Ministry of Justice to ensure that the implementation of this decision is swift, transparent, and includes comprehensive community and mental health support.

Announcing decision on Sunday morning, Mr Burnham said he had listened to the voices of families with loved ones convicted under IPP sentences and taken a “common sense” approach.

"I was faced with a situation where people on those sentences who have more than served their time, not being released when others who've committed very serious crimes being released early," he told BBC Breakfast.

"The judgement I've made is the public, in my view, would prefer a situation where people who have served their time to be considered for release before those who haven't.”

The government will table legislation to terminate the sentences by the "end of this Parliament", he added.

He noted the government will take a “very careful” approach to how this is done and said a cross-party oversight group would be established.

open image in gallery Shirley Debono and her son Shaun Lloyd ( Supplied )

The open-ended sentences – which The Independent has campaigned for more than two years to have reviewed – were outlawed in 2012, but not retrospectively. Introduced under New Labour in a bid to be tough on crime, they were handed to many repeat offenders, even if their crimes were minor. They have left thousands languishing without a release date, with some now having served up to 22 times longer than their original tariff.

The UN has repeatedly raised concerns the jail term causes psychological torture. In a damning legal opinion this month, their Working Group on Arbitrary Detention said Britain’s treatment of five IPP prisoners is unlawful, including Abdullahi Suleman, who is still in custody 20 years after he was handed an IPP for a laptop robbery; Leroy Douglas, who has served 20 years for a phone robbery; Wayne Williams, who has spent more than 19 years in prison without release for a 23-month jail term for attempting to injure a police officer in a fight; and Mr Lloyd, 39, who was recently hauled back to prison for the fifth time for street robbery.

Sadly, Joshua Mcrae, died in prison aged 34, having served more than 16 years for a four-year tariff for grievous bodily harm.

The are almost 2,300 IPP prisoners still trapped on the jail term, including more than 800 who have never been released. Eight in ten of those who have never been freed have served at least ten years longer than their original minimum tariff.

open image in gallery Clockwise from top: UN complainants Wayne Williams, Leroy Douglas, Josh Mcrae, Shaun Lloyd and Abdullahi Suleman ( Supplied )

Lord David Blunkett, who has previously admitted ushering in the jail terms under Tony Blair’s government is his “biggest regret” and led calls for reform, welcomed the news.

“I am very pleased,” he told The Independent, adding that both the prime minister and justice secretary are “committed to getting this right”.

He cautioned that the sentence will “take time to resolve” and some prisoners whose mental health has deteriorated on the jail term may need some longer term specialist provision.

“I am both relieved and enthused,” he added. “I am relieved for the individuals and enthused that the justice secretary and prime minister care so much.”

Lord Woodley, who has previously tabled a bill for all IPP prisoners to be resentenced, said although the end of this “terrible injustice” has come too late for those who have taken their own lives, it gives “real hope” to other prisoners and their families.

“It is welcome and long-overdue, and I pay tribute to the many campaigners for bringing us to today's historic announcement,” he added.

open image in gallery Lord David Blunkett welcomed the news ( PA Archive )

Andrea Coomber, chief executive of the Howard League for Penal Reform, said: “It is fantastic that the prime minister is using this moment of crisis in prisons to do the right thing regarding to the IPP sentence.

“This is a group of people, most very many years over tariff, have suffered a grave injustice and deserve supported release. It is vital that the promise of this moment is not lost and that government follows through on this commitment. People on the sentence and their loved ones have suffered so much – they can not be let down again.”

However shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy said he had “serious questions” about the government’s proposals, including the release of IPP prisoners.

“Will they all be released? Just some? How many? And on what timescale? What about those who would have had a life sentence had IPP not existed?,” he wrote on X.

An explosion at a New York City housing authority building that left a teenager dead and set the building on fire over the weekend was linked to an e-bike’s lithium-ion battery, according to a report.

Fire officials said the blaze broke out around 7 p.m. Friday at the New York City Housing Authority Albany Houses apartment complex in Crown Heights, Brooklyn.

Sources told NY1 that they believe the fire was caused by a lithium-ion battery. It was not immediately clear where the e-bike was at the time of the fire.

At least 34 fire trucks and first responder vehicles responded to the public housing development, located at 162 Troy Avenue.

On their arrival, first responders found smoke and flames coming out of the building.

A fire at a New York City housing authority apartment killed a teenager, authorities said ( Google Maps )

Authorities found an 18-year-old man unconscious inside an apartment in the building. He was taken to the hospital, where he died from his injuries.

Residents described the fire as fast moving.

“I was talking to the mother last week … we was having good talk about our kids. And that’s messed up how we both moved here young and our small children and for her to lose one … ,” a neighbor told Pix 11 about the victim’s family.

The victim’s identity has not been released by authorities and the cause of the explosion remains under investigation.

The blaze was put out by about 8 p.m., authorities said.

A resident told Pix 11 that it was the second fire at the location in two years.

News.title: Why did ministers, civil servants and lawyers tolerate the inhumanity of IPP jail terms for so long?
News.content:

Some U-turns are so damaging that they haunt a prime minister for the rest of their careers. Others are forgotten almost soon as they are made. A few are welcomed unreservedly; such is the case with the news that those involved in the killing of Pc Andrew Harper are to remain behind bars after all – and that the longstanding injustice of prisoners held indefinitely on “throw away the key” sentences is to end.

These two developments are related because space needs to be found in our creaking jails and low-risk “indefinite public protection” (IPP) prisoners are an obvious answer. Nonetheless, Andy Burnham is to be congratulated on the way he used the power of his office to insist ministers and officials were “turning over every stone” in the search for a publicly acceptable resolution to the prison overcrowding crisis.

After months of hard work, it seems they have succeeded. More places on the prison estate are being found, and the processing of foreign prisoners due for deportation is being expedited. But one particularly large and egregious stone left undisturbed until now has been the thousands of prisoners given indefinite sentences for relatively minor offences, often committed decades ago. The Independent is proud to have campaigned for many years to end this scandal. That it has taken an overcrowding crisis of unprecedented severity to force the issue shows how determined the families who have had their lives destroyed by these injustices have had to be in seeking some redress.

It takes a perverse kind of administrative genius to create a system where those convicted of the manslaughter of a police officer are set free years before those who stole a smartphone or a laptop in the 2000s. But that is precisely – and unbelievably – the kind of thing that has been tolerated by successive governments and the legal establishment for far too long. It is astonishing that Britain operates a system of criminal justice where dangerous criminals are released because there is no room for them while others in nearby cells posing no such danger to the public have zero chance of freedom. It is said the law is an ass; the IPP scandal created previously unimagined asinine outcomes.

IPP sentences were typically handed down for crimes such as theft and robbery – though some offences were certainly more grave – but spending 20 years or more incarcerated for them was grotesque beyond belief. Those languishing under the IPP regime were in practice required to prove the unprovable to a parole board – that they would never offend again. The bar was set so high it was impossible to reach, but nobody much seemed to mind about that. Assuming there’s no inquiry into how this regime was allowed to continue despite known flaws, there needs now to be at least some accountability on the part of those concerned: the ministers, civil servants, lawyers. Why did they tolerate this for so long?

How The Independent has campaigned on behalf of IPP prisoners ( The Independent )

And it was a long time. The IPP system, introduced by New Labour in 2005 during its “tough on crime, tough on the causes of crime” phase, became so discredited that even the subsequent Tory government found it unsustainable and IPP sentences were finally abolished in 2012. Lord Blunkett, the minister responsible for bringing in IPP, has since denounced it. However, the legislation that ended this inhumane approach to tariffs could not act retrospectively, as is the constitutional norm, so those already sentenced were simply left in jail. They have been treated beyond disgracefully.

Some are still there. Leroy Douglas, was sent down for the non-violent theft of a phone when he was 24 and had an unenviable record of stealing to fund his drug addiction. He should have been in for two years and six months for his offence, instead, under IPP, he has been transferred 36 times and suffered years of psychological distress. Now, at 44, he is to be returned to his family, but he highlights a painful irony about the IPP victims: “Most of us haven’t committed crimes for over 10 years, yet still the government tries to portray us as some danger to the public. Most have been so traumatised that they now have psychological or psychiatric problems and need more help than when they first went away.” Mr Douglas lost his grandparents and his daughter during his time in jail.

Even the United Nations has felt impelled to condemn the IPP system on human rights grounds; and an application for a writ of habeas corpus for some of the IPP prisoners has now been served in the High Court by senior lawyers on behalf of some of the victims. The action obviously has potentially wider repercussions. It requires the secretary of state for justice, Alex Norris, prison governors and a hospital director to give an account of themselves and justify the detention of people who should have been properly considered for release. It will be interesting to see what they say.

Public attention in recent weeks has been understandably focused on the killers of Pc Harper, but many more serious injustices have been brought into the open as a consequence of the overcrowding crisis. Some, at least, are now being rectified, but the damage to family life and mental health inflicted on the victims can never be repaired.

News.title: Chelsea v Brighton LIVE: Blues clinch win in seven-goal thriller but suffer Moises Caicedo injury scare
News.content:
Why Chelsea Are SERIOUS Title Contenders

Chelsea secured a second Premier League win in as many games under manager Xabi Alonso as they came out on top in another thrilling contest beating Brighton 4-3 at Stamford Bridge.

The Blues dominated the first half and took advantage of some early pressure, and a mistake from Bart Verbruggen, as Romeo Lavia poked in the opening goal. Pedro Neto then arrived in the far side of the box to meet a Morgan Rogers cross to double the lead but Joao Pedro rolled in a fine finish to send Chelsea three goals up.

But Brighton pulled a goal back before the break as Malick Yalcouye blasted in a rocket to keep the Seagulls in the game. Things improved for the visitors as a Pascal Gross shot deflected off Joao Pedro to reduce the deficit to one.

Cole Palmer calmed the nerves with a beautifully worked goal before Gross nodded in the seventh goal of the game just seconds before the final whistle. Two wins from two for Chelsea in another chaotic encounter.

Harry Maguire played a big part in Manchester United’s second goal in their 5-2 win against Ipswich Town in the Premier League with controversy surrounding a VAR review.

The United defender handled the ball in the build-up before gathering the ball and striking at goal.

His effort was not going on target and instead deflected off Jacob Graves to hand the hosts the lead at Old Trafford, before Bruno Fernandes struck twice more to send the Red Devils clear at 4-1.

But United’s second sparked widespread debate, mainly due to the hosts’ good fortune that Maguire didn’t convert the chance himself.

The VAR reviewed the incident, but due to the fact that Maguire’s benefit did not directly result in the goal, with his shot deflecting off Graves, the goal was allowed to stand.

"It wasn't handball on purpose,” Maguire told Sky Sports. “That [it being an own-goal] is why it counted, if it was my goal, it'd have been disallowed, luckily we were on the right side and I think we deserved a bit of luck."

Darren Bent reacted: "He's going to say it's accidental, almost trying to protect himself, I understand the rules, but it directly impacts the goal.”

Gary Neville admitted the rule would need to be looked at after discovering the reason for the goal standing.

The Premier League match centre responded to the controversial incident: “The referee’s call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball.

open image in gallery Manchester United's Harry Maguire celebrates after Ipswich Town's Jacob Greaves scores an own goal ( PA )

open image in gallery Harry Maguire's deflected shot was controversially awarded as a Jacob Greaves own goal despite a potential handball in the build-up ( Getty )

open image in gallery Manchester United's Harry Maguire celebrates their second goal ( Reuters )

VAR added: “It’s an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you award the goal.”

The rule’s definition reads that the “It is an offence if a player scores in the opponents’ goal:

“-Directly from their hand/arm, even if accidental, including by the goalkeeper

“-Immediately after the ball has touched their hand/arm, even if accidental.”

But mitigating factors include:

“-Goal not immediate

“-Goal scored by a teammate

“-Ball not entering goal; however action of a defender

results in an ‘own goal’”

Some debate will surround the wording “accidental handball,” with the handball crucial to Maguire gaining possession.

After Fernandes completed his hat-trick, Bryan Mbeumo added a fifth to help United on their way to their first points of the 2026/27 season.

News.title: ‘The IPP scandal has toyed with people’s lives. Here’s why I began investigating – and what should happen next’
News.content:
For free real time breaking news alerts sent straight to your inbox sign up to our breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

When I first started investigating indefinite sentences in November 2023, there had been horrifying spike in suicides among prisoners.

I discovered seven men serving Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) jail terms had taken their own lives in a few short months since their hopes of release were dashed by the then-Conservative government.

Many had dared to start believing the end to their “throw away the key” sentence might finally be in sight after the cross-party justice committee had led an inquiry into the toxic legacy of the abolished jail term, concluding the punishment was “irredeemably flawed”.

The committee had handed the incumbent justice secretary, Dominic Raab, a string of recommendations, including – crucially – one calling for a panel to be established to oversee the resentencing of all remaining IPP prisoners. But Mr Raab refused.

We will never know what went through the minds of prisoners who took their own lives that year, including one just two weeks after Mr Raab’s refusal was made public, but campaigners fear the flurry of deaths was linked to the devastating news.

That is why it is so important that Andy Burnham follows through on what he has now promised, with meaningful, carefully planned action to finally draw a line under this failed sentencing experiment.

To date, a total 96 IPP prisoners have taken their own lives in custody. That number must not get any bigger.

Amy-Clare Martin has investigated the IPP scandal since 2023 ( The Independent )

Over the years of The Independent’s campaign, I met family after family whose lives have been devastated by this hopeless sentence, with shocking examples of prisoners whose punishment has stretched on for so long it no longer matches their crime.

Some have now been inside for the best part of two decades for relatively low-level offences, like Leroy Douglas, who we reported on Sunday is finally going home after 20 years in prison for a mobile phone robbery. Others committed crimes which are undeniably much more serious, but eight in 10 of those who have never been released have served at least 10 years longer than their minimum tariff.

With each new story I encountered a family which acknowledged that their loved one committed a crime and deserved to be punished. But what they did not expect was for them to be tortured by a sentence with no end date and constantly moving goalposts, consigning them – and their innocent loved ones – to years of limbo.

Many such prisoners only learned what an IPP sentence was when their tariff expired and they were refused parole for the first time. For thousands, this rejection happened again and again – with each knockback condemning them to another two years in prison before they were granted another shot at release. All too often, they were told to complete courses which they could not access or had to wait years for a space to become available, only to be asked to complete another course at their next hearing.

Prisoners felt wrongfooted by a system which appeared to change the rules at every turn, leaving them to rot even after the sentence was outlawed in 2012. And when this process took an inevitable toll on their mental health, that too was used against them as a means to justify detaining them even longer.

In the face of widespread condemnation – including from the United Nations, which has found some IPP prisoners are being arbitrarily detained, resulting in a major legal challenge – the prime minister has today rightly acknowledged that he must correct this injustice.

From everything I have learned over the past few years, I believe it is possible to find a way to balance the vital need to protect the public with what is fair and just.

A clear starting point is those IPP prisoners who have been recalled to prison indefinitely for no further offence. Unlike most other offenders, who typically serve a fixed term recall period of 56 days, they are returned to prison indefinitely for something as simple as missing a probation appointment. They serve more than two years on average each time they slip up, which, under the early release scheme, is akin to serving the custodial portion of a four- to six-year prison sentence.

But the government must not avoid the complex cases, including more than 800 who have never been released and 200 in secure hospitals, whose circumstances must each be carefully and meticulously reviewed to find them a clear path towards release. Many will need mental health support from the damage this sentence has inflicted on them.

At a time when the prison overcrowding crisis demands that other prisoners are released early, continuing to ignore these over-tariff prisoners would be unacceptably cruel.

The details of the government’s plans have not been revealed, but a cross-party oversight group is expected to lead the project.

Mr Burnham has admitted it will take time to put this right and promised to end the injustice before the end of parliament. For the sake of IPP prisoners and their families, justice secretary Alex Norris and the Ministry of Justice must start this important work as soon as possible.

Ontario Premier Doug Ford hit back at Donald Trump again on Sunday but seemed to regret the personal nature of their dispute after the two traded insults over Trump’s attempt to rename Lake Ontario.

Ford appeared on ABC’s This Week after getting into a war of words with the president coinciding with the larger trade war erupting between the U.S. and its northern neighbor, Canada. The U.S. and Canada levied tariffs as high as 50 percent on various imports this month after trade talks collapsed.

And while Ford backed away from the personal jabs he’d aimed at Trump at a press conference this past week, the premier reiterated that he thought that Trump’s move to direct the federal government to refer to Lake Ontario as “Lake America” was “absolutely backwards”. Ford had referred to Trump as a “loser,” a “dictator” and a “bully” in his comments to reporters.

“I don’t see the purpose,” said Ford, who installed a massive billboard declaring that the lake was “now and always” Lake Ontario on its shore this week. "It was something out of Saturday Night Live when he signed documents saying 'change it to Lake America.' No one is going to call it Lake America.”

Of the tenor of the debate, he added: “It's unfortunate that he stoops down to that level, and unfortunately, I did that day.”

open image in gallery Ontario's premier, Doug Ford, says that Canada and the rest of the world will never recognize Trump's name change ( AP )

Ford’s comments come after Trump held a signing ceremony on Thursday to publicize a new executive order making the name change an official U.S. government policy. Private organizations are under no obligation to adhere to the name change, but Google Maps has already announced that it will feature the name change in maps presented to U.S. customers.

At the signing ceremony, Trump hinted that he could even attempt to rename one or more of the world’s oceans next. The event was cheered on by some of the president’s various allies who have supported his efforts to tighten the screws on Canada in an attempt to secure a more favorable trade agreement, but even some Republicans admitted openly that the president’s actions seem like a distraction in the face of a growing trade war and the conflict with Iran, which hit its sixth-month mark on Friday.

open image in gallery Donald Trump announced that he would direct the federal government to refer to Lake Ontario as “Lake America” on Thursday ( Getty )

Canadian officials of all political stripes roundly denounced Trump’s move as a provocation, and said they would not recognize the change.

“You’ve got to eventually stand up to someone that just continuously attacks our country,” said Ford. “We believe in Canadian sovereignty.”

Trump responded to Ford in typical fashion on Truth Social, referencing Ford’s late brother who died after a battle with cancer.

“Lots of ’bluster’ from Doug Ford, who is the Premier of the Canadian Province of Ontario, but who is better known as the less charismatic, intelligent, and overall unimpressive brother of the late, great, Rob Ford,” wrote the U.S. president.

Apart from the obvious issues that attempting to rename Lake Ontario raises, some of the president’s supporters have found even more creative reasons to oppose the change. On Fox News, former congressman Trey Gowdy warned that the new acronym spelled out by the names of the Great Lakes would shift from “HOMES” to “HAMES”, which he warned was dangerously close to Hamas — the Palestinian militant group in charge of Gaza, designated as a terrorist group.

U.S. and Canadian officials have said that trade talks fell apart at the last minute over a dispute surrounding tariffs on trucks manufactured in Canada, including in Ontario. In the days since the talks collapsed, both sides have levied new tariffs on a range of goods including steel, aluminum, lumber and dairy products.

open image in gallery Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney speaks about the trade dispute with the United States ( AFP/Getty )

Canadian officials have warned that they are willing to wait out the entirety of Trump’s presidency rather than capitulate to the White House’s demands.

"You're at war when you get attacked. We got attacked," Prime Minister Mark Carney said.

U.S. officials have warned that further retaliation from Canada would provoke a response from Trump.

“If there’s further retaliation from the Canadian side, we, of course, we’re not going to just sit down and take that. Our view is don’t retaliate,” U.S. trade representative Jamieson Greer told a Canadian broadcaster this past week.

“But I know that, you know, I know how people are feeling in Canada and what they think. So, you know, it’s unfortunate, but it is what it is. And we have our own trade policy, and we’ll proceed with it in the way that’s best for the United States,” he added.

News.title: Robinson’s Victorian-style bowling figures secure series victory over Pakistan
News.content:
The only missing aspect was a five-fer which would have brought a 100th Test wicket. Even so, his career average is now 19.53, the best for England since Frank Tyson of those with 50 or more wickets.

Mr Nude Nuts, as Matthew Hayden called him, could be devastating against Australia and, like Root the captain, deserves to be judged on what happens in his second incarnation rather than what went before.

Robinson’s pace has lingered around the 79mph mark and inevitably that throws up Rob Key’s assertion you cannot succeed in Test cricket bowling in the 70s with the keeper standing up. Key was referring to county bowlers pitching it up and relying on the Duke ball to do the rest.

It was thrown in his face in Australia but Michael Neser and Scott Boland are not county trundlers: they extract more energy off the pitch than that.

Robinson is also no dobber. His high release point combined with a mastery of length means he is always threatening the top of off stump. He also knows which way the ball is going to nip, giving no clues to the batsmen due to his sleight of hand skills.

With Jamie Smith improving under the tutelage of Sarah Taylor, he can operate with the keeper standing up which pins batsmen in the crease, bringing all modes of dismissals into play. Robinson was as effective with the new ball as the old: his two seven over spells were two for 13 and two for 11.

How snarling Robinson adds edge and precision

At 32, he has become a combination of Stuart Broad and James Anderson, although down on their pace with the height and bounce of the former, and tricks of the latter. He can move the new ball further either way than Anderson or Broad but the question is whether he has their durability and sheer competitiveness.

He has not been tested this summer by pitches or opponents. He has not bowled more than 18 overs in an innings and was injured when England played on the best batting pitch at the Oval. He was not trusted at Trent Bridge because the old management had burned their fingers before. That decision may well have cost the coach his job.

Like Broad and Anderson he has a snarl too, sending Abdullah Shafique on his way with a word or two. There was no need for that but maybe it was just a carried away reaction to bowling an absolute beauty that angled in, seamed away and hit the top of off.

News.title: Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness
News.content:
Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

News.title: Moses Itauma lifted out of ring after losing IBF title bout to Filip Hrgovic
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the heavyweight clash between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic.

Itauma is on the cusp of becoming a British boxing star, but for now there remain questions. It is not that people doubt his talents, more that he needs to prove them emphatically to the wider boxing world.

At just 21, Itauma has been creating rumblings since 2023. He has 10 straight knockouts. He is undefeated. His last two wins were against Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin, but he is yet to beat a fighter you might regard as a gatekeeper to a title fight.

Hrgovic might normally be seen as that gatekeeper. At 34, the Croatian has plenty of experience in the ring, with 21 fights bringing 20 wins, 15 of them by knockout. His only loss was against Daniel Dubois in 2024, but his wins since then have been against Joe Joyce, David Adeleye and Dave Allen. Not the highest quality, by any means. Hrgovic, then, has something to prove to us too.

However, this is no eliminator, this is for the full IBF world heavyweight championship. A win for Itauma would see him become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in boxing history.

As Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury circle one another, threatening to never fight at all, Itauma looks set to be Britain’s next heavyweight star. All he has to do is win at the O2 Arena tonight. If he does that, he could then be a fixture at the top of the sport for a decade, perhaps more.

Ringwalks are expected at around 10.30pm for the main event. So if men in dressing gowns is your thing, get ready.

News.title: £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle
News.content:
“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

News.title: Lawrence seizes his opportunity on rain-ruined day at Lord’s
News.content:
On a bleak day for batting, Dan Lawrence seized an opportunity that he must have feared had passed him by.

Lawrence was one of the victims of Bazball excess, shoved up to open in place of Zak Crawley two years ago in a punt that backfired and could have ended his Test career.

It took the sudden retirement of Ben Stokes and an injury to first-choice replacement Sam Curran to open up a position at No 6, Lawrence’s natural home, and it has come at just the right time.

At 29 he is a much more rounded cricketer than the one who debuted in Sri Lanka under Joe Root in 2021 and he showed it here with a hard-fought half-century on a gloomy, dank Saturday when only 25 overs were possible between the frequent drizzly showers, forcing MCC into a 50 per cent ticket refund.

It was a second fifty in three innings since his recall and he will not have faced many tougher conditions than this, with the ball seaming around on a spiteful pitch. With Mohammad Abbas teasing the ball off the surface and the athletic Mohammad Rizwan snaffling everything up to the stumps, this was a real challenge of mind and technique.

Lawrence will never win awards for aesthetic beauty but he chose the right balls to put away in a 66-ball unbeaten 50 that stretched England’s lead to 357 at 177 for seven in their second innings. Lawrence settled any wobbles about Pakistan pulling off a miracle recovery.

News.title: Springboks level Greatest Rivalry series with blood-and-thunder victory over All Blacks
News.content:
South Africa aim to bounce back from losing the first game of the Greatest Rivalry Tour as they take on New Zealand in game two from Cape Town. The All Blacks claimed an impressive 33-16 win in game on in Johannesburg last weekend, outscoring South Africa five tries to one. That victory takes New Zealand above South Africa in the world rankings into top spot.

The Springboks know that a defeat today will mean they cannot win the series. They have not lost two consecutive Tests since November 2022. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has been given the nod to start at fly-half but Handre Pollard has pulled out of the matchday squad due to a calf injury.

“There were a handful of positives and negatives last week, but the main thing that let us down was that we created so many chances, but mistakes at crucial times cost us,” South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus said.

“We will put in a lot of work this week to ensure that we are sharp in that regard this weekend because if we had used even some of those chances, the result could have been completely different. That said, we know New Zealand will be charged up after winning last week, and they will want to build on that. But the key for us will be to focus on our game and ensure that we are as effective as possible all around.”

News.title: Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty
News.content:
He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

News.title: Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow
News.content:
Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

Sports.title: Angry ex-Brighton star tears into Joao Pedro after Chelsea star’s wild celebration after scoring against old team
Sports.content:
JOAO PEDRO has been torn into by a former Brighton player after the striker’s wild celebration against his old club.

The Brazilian netted for Chelsea in the 4-3 Premier League victory over the Seagulls at Stamford Bridge.



Pedro, 24, signed for the Blues from Brighton in a £60million transfer in 2025.

Since making the transfer, the striker lost one game to Brighton and missed another due to injury.



He made his mark against his former side on Sunday with a goal as well as an own goal in the victory.

It was his actions after his goal that caused anger from his former supporters.

Pedro slotted past Bart Verbruggen and started to run off to celebrate with the home crowd.

However, he then changed his direction of run and instead celebrated his goal in front of the travelling fans.

This sparked a furious response from the fans as well as another former Brighton favourite.

Anthony Knockaert, 34, shared his view on Instagram and hit out at Pedro’s actions.

Sports.title: Man Utd player ratings: Kobbie Mainoo runs show as Bruno Fernandes nets hat-trick but Luke Shaw to blame for goal
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED overcame an early scare to brush aside Premier League new boys Ipswich Town 5-2 in a rampant second half.

The Tractor Boys were ahead through Leif Diop’s sweet volley amid atrocious defending from Michael Carrick’s side, sending shivers down the home crowd who lost at Hull City on the opening weekend.



But Bruno Fernandes’ third United hat-trick and an own goal from Jacob Greaves from Harry Maguire‘s deflected shot, following an accidental own goal, avoided another blunder result.

Greaves endured a hellish afternoon at Old Trafford as he narrowly avoided a second own goal after Bryan Mbeumo‘s lob crossed the line as United dodged a first defeat to Ipswich since 1997.



Here’s how SunSport’s Katherine Walsh rated the United players during their first home game of the season.

Senne Lammens – 6

The Belgian had another good game. Three big first half saves kept United in it, with his backline leaving him vulnerable. Enjoyed a quiet second half, only being called off his line for a corner routine.



Diogo Dalot – 6

A step up from Noussair Mazraoui‘s showing in the Hull debacle, but far from perfect, with yet another opponent using the width of the pitch to punish United’s full backs.

Two mistakes at both inside a few minutes saw Dalot fluff a cross, before misreading Daizen Maeda‘s run in behind, leaving Lammens’ goal gaping. A brilliant Kjell Scherpen save denied the Portuguese an opener inside 10 minutes.

Lisandro Martinez – 5

Had to start after 19-year-old Ayden Heaven‘s showing against Hull City, but the World Cup finalist looked out of rhythm.

Caught out by Enciso and lost possession for Ipswich’s late consolation and needs to get up to speed quickly.



Harry Maguire – 6

The 33-year-old was part of the mess at the back for the second successive weekend, but unlike last Saturday his distribution left a lot to be desired.

That being said United’s second goal summed up Maguire, his deflected finish off Greaves counted despite his handball in the lead up. His 18th goal for the club put United ahead.

Luke Shaw – 5

His nightmare for Ipswich’s opener has only highlighted the will-they won’t-they debate around signing a left back for Tuesday’s 11pm deadline.

The 31-year-old needs competition this season and on this evidence, struggling to contain former Leicester winger Abdul Fatawu, United need to sign a proven left back in the next 48 hours.

Kobbie Mainoo – 8

The 20-year-old was United best player. He seemingly played with a point to prove to Thomas Tuchel for his lack of World Cup minutes.



Mainoo was sharp, fast and as composed as ever, drawing countless fouls throughout. The visitors could not get a grip on the United academy graduate and he set up Cunha’s penalty. Slowed down to bait the press and dictated play.

Youri Tielemans – 6

The former Villa man needs to cover more ground for a pivot with Mainoo to work – but that isn’t the 29-year-old’s game.

Tielemans is a great player but his lack of pace was glaring again. Did show more show physicality in the box when Ipswich were ahead amid some sloppy mistakes.

Bruno Fernandes – 8

Ever eternal. A hat-trick of goals for the PFA player of the year. The United skipper levelled with an excellent touch and finish before the break, his cool spot-kick made it 3-1 and kept himself onside to slot in a fourth.

Added an assist a great home opener, when he picked out Mbeumo’s run beyond Ipswich’s back-line.



Marcus Rashford – 7

A real handle down the left and an obvious step up from Patrick Dorgu on his first Prem start for United since December 1 2024. The England star is staying at Old Trafford this season, it is all but confirmed.

He linked up well with Matheus Cunha and had the fair share of United’s opportunities before the break and worked hard to keep several chances alive in the second half. A fit and firing Rashford is nothing but a good thing for United.

Bryan Mbeumo – 6

His early momentum stalled when he was caught sleeping to Enciso’s 20 yard run, cashed back back but did not cover himself in glory.

Should have levelled when his goal-line knock blasted off the bar. Worked hard but was outshone by his fellow forwards. Lobbed the keeper to score the fifth.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Matheus Cunha – 7

Back as United’s official striker through the middle, Cunha took a while to settle before a terrific assist with a through ball to Fernandes saw the hosts equalise.



The Brazilian often has the cutting edge needed from Old Trafford players and won the penalty when Greaves cut him down before the hour mark.

Noussair Mazraoui (for Shaw, 73) – 6

Leny Yoro (for Dalot, 74) – 6

Patrick Dorgu (for Rashford, 80) – 5

Benjamin Sesko (for Cunha, 80) – 6

Andrey Santos (for Mainoo, 80) – 6

Sports.title: Man Utd 5 Ipswich 2: Fernandes scores scintillating hat-trick as Michael Carrick’s side get off mark despite early scare
Sports.content:
BRUNO FERNANDES bagged an incredible hat-trick to inspire Manchester United to a thumping 5-2 win over Ipswich Town on Sunday.

Old Trafford was stunned midway through the first half as Abdul Fatawu skinned Luke Shaw and crossed for Leif Davis to rifle home off the crossbar.





But United skipper Fernandes settled the nerves after running through on goal and supplying a cool finish just before the interval.

Harry Maguire’s deflected strike went in off Jacob Greaves to make it 2-1 before Fernandes scored their third from the spot.





And it was 4-1 minutes later as Fernandes tapped home to complete his treble after Bryan Mbeumo’s blocked shot.

The Red Devils wrapped up a crushing win as Fernandes turned provider and played in Mbeumo – who lobbed Ipswich keeper Kjell Scherpen.

Ipswich scored a late consolation through Chuba Akpom.

More to follow.

Sports.title: Gary Neville pokes fun of Ipswich keeper after cheeky tactic backfires as brave Bruno Fernandes scores Man Utd penalty
Sports.content:
GARY NEVILLE hit out at Ipswich goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen after Manchester United hat-trick hero Bruno Fernandes netted from the penalty spot.

The Red Devils came from behind to notch a comfortable 5-2 win over the Tractor Boys.



And Neville, 51, poked fun at Scherpen after his cheeky tactic backfired when he looked to keep out Fernandes’ spot-kick.

Ipswich’s summer signing was spotted standing to the right of his goal as the United skipper started his run-up.



Scherpen then dived to his left, with newly-crowned PFA Player of the Year Fernandes placing his effort exactly where the Dutchman was initially standing.

United legend Neville, who was on co-commentary duties at Old Trafford, said: “It seems the only person confused by the goalkeeper’s actions is himself.”

Scherpen became the TALLEST Premier League star of all-time when he joined Ipswich from Belgian outfit Union Saint-Gilloise last month.

And the 6ft 9in giant, 26, made a string of brilliant saves as the Tractor Boys chased a shock win.

But Scherpen could not stop United staging a stunning fightback to clinch all three points.

Leif Davis had Ipswich in dreamland when he converted Abdul Fatawu’s inch-perfect cutback.

But Fernandes, 31, profited from Marcelino Nunez’s costly slip and found an equaliser just before half-time.

Harry Maguire then added his name to the scoresheet in controversial circumstances.

And Fernandes went on to complete his hat-trick by converting from the penalty spot and close range shortly after.

The Portuguese talisman then turned provider as his sensational through ball found Bryan Mbeumo, who lobbed the onrushing Scherpen after missing a sitter earlier in the second half.



United’s comeback allowed them to bag their first points of the Premier League campaign despite Chuba Akpom’s stoppage time consolation goal.

Michael Carrick’s side suffered a woeful defeat to newly-promoted Hull City last weekend.

Sports.title: Fans baffled as Harry Maguire goal stands despite handball in build-up due to little-known rule in Man Utd vs Ipswich
Sports.content:
THE handball rules were at the centre of debate once more as Harry Maguire helped give Manchester United a 2-1 lead against Ipswich.

The centre back marauded forward after winning the ball back and fired an effort across the box that was deflected home by Jacob Greaves for an own goal.

The ball appeared to hit Maguire’s hand when he won it back, but because he is not the actual goalscorer, the goal is allowed to stand.



Only if Maguire had directly benefited from the handball and scored himself would the free-kick have been given and the goal ruled out.



Many would quite rightly argue that Maguire certainly did benefit from the handball!

The Premier League match centre explained: “The referee’s call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball.

VAR: “It’s an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you award the goal.”



Is that an accidental handball? He wouldn’t have won the ball otherwise. But that’s another point of contention.

Fans were left totally bemused by the decision and flooded social media with criticism for the officials.

One user wrote: “That Maguire goal NO way that can be considered an accidental handball when the hands assited him to control the ball.”

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

A second wrote: “Bonkers that. If Maguire scores direct it’s handball but because it’s an own goal it’s not. Who makes up these rules? Surely handball is handball?.”



A third commented: “We lost football when we lost common sense I don’t care if it’s deflected, that’s handball by Maguire.”

It was a dogged affair up until that point with Ipswich taking the lead through their left-back Leif Davis.

However, Bruno Fernandes capitalised on a mistake to race through to equalise before half-time.

Halsey explains 'handball' When Manchester United go 2-1 up with an own goal by Ipswich Town’s Greaves, in the buildup to that goal, Harry Maguire handles the ball.

The ball hits his arms.

Now, when challenging Akpom for the ball, his arms are in a natural position and it’s an accidental handball.

Then, Harry Maguire gets his shot away.

And it comes off Ipswich Town’s Greaves and goes into the goal.

Now, because Harry Maguire wasn’t the scorer, the goal stands.

Had Harry Maguire shot directly into the goal, it would have been disallowed for an accidental handball because he would have been the goalscorer.

But because he wasn’t the goalscorer, it was an own goal, the goal stands.

Now, some people say the law’s on us.

Yes, you could argue it is, but according to law 12 handling the ball, that goal was correctly given by on field and after review by VAR.

Ipswich Town and Gary O’Neill will feel aggrieved with the 2nd goal, but unfortunately the officials are correcting law.

After Bryan Mbeumo managed one of the misses of the decade to put United in front, Maguire’s deflected effort got the job done.



Fernandes went on to score his hat-trick to put United 4-1 up with 20 minutes still to play.

Sports.title: Emi Martinez reveals secret chats with John Terry and Petr Cech inspired Chelsea transfer as he backs Blues to win title

EMILIANO MARTINEZ declared Chelsea are on a mission to win the title after jumping in at the deep end.

Sports.title: Fans in disbelief at Bryan Mbeumo’s ‘miss of the season’ after rattling the bar from TWO YARDS OUT in Man Utd vs Ipswich
Sports.content:
BRYAN MBEUMO was accused of missing the “sitter of the season” after somehow fluffing his lines from yards out against Ipswich.

The Manchester United forward was given a gilt-edged opportunity after Marcus Rashford‘s cross.



But he somehow struck the crossbar from TWO YARDS out after the ball came off his knee and fans were left baffled.

Sports.title: Brilliant Bruno Fernandes and VAR loophole help Man Utd thrash Ipswich - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Brilliant Bruno Fernandes and VAR loophole help Man Utd thrash Ipswich - 5 talking points

MANCHESTER UNITED 5-2 IPSWICH TOWN: Bruno Fernandes scored a hat-trick as the hosts overcame going behind to secure a comfortable three points

View 5 Images Bruno Fernandes' hat-trick inspired Man Utd to three points

Manchester United came from behind to down Ipswich and secure their first Premier League win of the season thanks to a Bruno Fernandes hat-trick - but the win wasn't without its controversy.

‌



Leif Davis shocked the Stretford End when he put Ipswich ahead on 29 minutes before the host drew themselves level thanks to talisman Fernandes, who was sent clear after a defensive mishap.

‌



Jacob Greaves put through his own net to put United ahead for the first time, but only after Harry Maguire had handled the ball before receiving a VAR reprieve.

‌



Fernandes was on hand to score from 12 yards to give Michael Carrick's side a two-goal cushion on the hour mark before he bagged his third United treble thanks a fortuitous bounce that allowed him to score from close range. Bryan Mbuemo completed the rout before Chuba Akpom scored a consolation in stoppage time.
