The visitors, who once lost this fixture 9-0 back in the 1990s, were certainly don't going to allow a repeat. Julio Enciso showcased immense pace to race onto a long ball before Senne Lammens denied him. The Belgian was beaten though when Davis put the Tractor Boys ahead.

‌



Abdul Fatawu squared up and beat Luke Shaw before firing in his cross, which the Ipswich left-back met first time with his shot cannoning in off the crossbar to silence Old Trafford.

United, as they have done regularly in recent years, needed their PFA Player of the Year to haul them out of trouble. An Ipswich error left the hosts two-on-one and Fernandes was sent clear by Matheus Cunha, before hammering past Kjell Scherpen.

View 5 Images Harry Maguire's goal opened the floodgates for the Red Devils

‌



The Red Devils missed the chance to put themselves ahead early in the second-half when Bryan Mbuemo somehow hit the bar from a yard out, but Maguire soon had them ahead in controversial circumstances which will go down as a Greaves own goal.

United firmly took control of the contest when Fernandes scored his second from the spot after Cunha had been fouled. He would complete his hat-trick before Mbeumo got on the scoresheet to add further gloss to the result.

Here's five talking points from Old Trafford.

‌



Bruno untouchable

Having just been named the Premier League's best player off the back of what he did last season, where he broke record for assists in a single campaign, Fernandes is clearly flowing with confidence at an all-time high.

Gary Neville remarked on commentary that the Portuguese playmaker is the best signing of the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era and few could disagree. In fact it is almost impossible to disagree. Fernandes was United's talisman last season and, even with the quality around him, that status doesn't look like changing.

Maguire controversy

Never will the England defender be so glad to see a shot be heading wide, but the influence of VAR and the laws they can intervene on will be under serious scrutiny after United's second goal, which put them in charge of the contest.

‌



View 5 Images A controversial explanation saw Man Utd's second goal stand

Maguire clearly handled the ball seconds before he took his shot, but as his effort was going wide and deflected in by Greaves, it meant his actions weren't under the microscope as the goalscorer. Had he scored then we may have had a different outcome - and that will not sit well with many.

Ipswich collapse after positive hour

The last time Ipswich were in the top flight under Kieran McKenna it was off the back of successive promotions and the Tractor Boys ultimately won just four games and finished 16 points from safety. Their squad looked that bit short, but this time round they've got several of the players who will be better off for that experience.

‌



They've also got the likes of Daizen Maeda, signed from Celtic, and several individuals who've impressed in the Premier League previously, Issa Diop among them. Gary O'Neil has top flight experience as a manager.

View 5 Images Bruno Fernandes' first of the afternoon got Man Utd level

Crazy to think that you could take any positives from such a hammering defeat, but for an hour Ipswich were in this game and it needed a controversial moment before the floodgates opened. O'Neil needs to see the first 60 minutes as a blueprint for the season.

‌



Where is Sesko at?

Last season started slow and then he became known as a super sub, coming off the bench to win numerous games once United hit form. But heading into his second season the Slovenian will surely have felt he'd done enough to begin establishing himself in the first XI.

Instead he began on the bench for a second week in succession. His introduction came late against Hull and this weekend he was only given 11 minutes by Carrick. If Sesko was hoping to kick on, his plans are certainly on hold.

View 5 Images Leif Davis had given Ipswich a first-half lead

‌



Rashford's revival

Few would've thought that it would only take Rashford one game of the Premier League season before he was back starting games for United again. Their attack was purring last season under Carrick without him and there didn't seem to be any great clamour for him to return.

But a lot can change in a short space of time and Rashford was called upon at half-time against Hull last weekend, even if he couldn't turn the tide the day. Nevertheless he did enough to convince his boss that he was worthy of a start as his secondcoming at his boyhood club continues.

Sports.content:
Sons of police officer killed in horror A66 crash lead out dad's beloved Man Utd vs Ipswich

Manchester United fan PC Matthew Blades was killed in a horror head-on collision with a vehicle that was speeding down the wrong way of the A66 in Teesside last week

View 3 Images The boys were invited to lead Manchester United out today (Image: Getty Images)

The sons of a police officer killed in a head-on crash on the A66 have led Manchester United out at Old Trafford for their Premier League clash against Ipswich Town.

‌



PC Matthew Blades, described by the club as a "proud Red," was killed alongside colleague PC Tom Clough in a head-on crash with a vehicle travelling the wrong way down the A66 at South Bank, in Teeside, last weekend. Middlesborough FC also paid tribute to the officers and their colleagues at Cleveland Police on Saturday, and United invited Blades' two sons and his wife to their home match against Ipswich.

‌



The children led the United squad as mascots, with the club expressing "great sadness" at the deaths of the two officers in the matchday programme. United said: "Matthew was a proud Red, a devoted family man and a police officer who dedicated his life to helping others.

‌



View 3 Images Matthew Blades was a fan of Manchester United (Image: Facebook)

Sky News presenter forced to cut live broadcast after being 'hassled' on air READ MORE :

"For Matt, some of his happiest times were spent watching United with his boys. His wife Sarah and two children will be at today's game, with his sons leading out the Reds as mascots."

‌



An image of Blades with his two sons at Old Trafford featured in the programme, along with a tribute from an unnamed close friend and colleague. "For Matthew, United was a lifelong love, a passion he shared with his family," the tribute read.

"Since Matt's tragic death there has been an extraordinary outpouring of grief and support. That love has been seen in countless tributes and acts of kindness.

View 3 Images The two boys led Manchester United out today against Ipswich

Article continues below

"Today, we remember a fellow Red. A husband. A father. A son. A brother. A friend. A police officer. A man who gave his life in the service of others. Forever our superhero."

Across the Pennines, match officials at Elland Road for Leeds United's fixture against Brentford wore black armbands as referee Tony Harrington was a friend of PC Blades. There was a minute's applause on Saturday in the memory of the two police officers. Pictures of the two men were displayed on screen.

The occupants of the vehicle headed the wrong way down the A66 were Robert Cahill, 23, Jakob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, 17, and Cole Robert Worthy, 17. All of them died in the crash.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso has Chelsea looking like genuine title challengers - no wonder fans are happy
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso has Chelsea looking like genuine title challengers - no wonder fans are happy

Xabi Alonso is already proving a hit with the Chelsea fans and the Blues made it two wins from win against Brighton as Emi Martinez debuted in goal after his move

View 3 Images Xabi Alonso has kept up his perfect Chelsea start

Chelsea fans are notoriously hard to please. But no wonder Xabi Alonso has won them over already.

‌



This was a brilliant, entertaining and terrific seven-goal contest which had the Stamford Bridge faithful singing the new manager’s name.

‌



Let’s not forget they did not sing Enzo Maresca’s name or Liam Rosenior. And Alonso is a former Liverpool player so it could easily have been a hard sell.

‌



But not with Chelsea playing like this. Yes, they conceded three and look shaky at the back but they are also the great entertainers. Joao Pedro was electric, scored and played comedy villain with an own goal in front of the Brighton fans who gave their former striker pelters all afternoon.

Predictably, Cole Palmer stole the show with the all-important fourth goal to seal victory as he looks rejuvenated after his summer break through missing the World Cup.

Xabi Alonso speaks after axing Enzo Fernandez again and hints at Chelsea exit READ MORE :

Aston Villa and Chelsea relationship as Emi Martinez becomes EIGHTH transfer READ MORE :

Emiliano Martinez made his debut for Chelsea and, even though they concede far too many goals, at least they have top quality keeper behind their rather unreliable defence.

‌



Pedro Neto shone in his new role as right wing back and Chelsea look as if they could be realistic title challengers this season. Chelsea’s trip to reigning champions Arsenal next Sunday already looks like a blockbuster.

But really it is the flair, the movement and skill of Chelsea’s front three. Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers are as good as any forward line in the Premier League. Certainly no-one missed Enzo Fernandez who was missing again as he waits on a mega last-minute move to Manchester City while the only real concern was Moises Caicedo limping off just 14 minutes after coming on as a substitute.

View 3 Images Chelsea have scored seven goals in their opening two games

‌



But it is the entertainment value which gets Chelsea fans off their seats. They were ahead after just four minutes. Joao Pedro’s header was cleared off the line, but Mats Wieffer got in a horrible mix-up with keeper Bart Verbruggen and Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia pounced to squeeze home.

Incredibly, that was Lavia’s first goal in four very injury disrupted years. His last goal was on August 30, 2022, for Southampton against Chelsea. Maybe this season maybe the year where the talented midfielder’s luck changes.

Chelsea made it 2-0 after just 14 minutes. Jorrel Hato’s throw-in found Morgan Rogers and his low cross was swept in by Pedro Neto. Brighton’s bench were furious because Hato’s throw was so obviously taken from the wrong place.

‌



Joao Pedro missed a sitter to the delight of the Brighton fans. But their glee did not last long. Hato showed great strength to hold off Wieffer and then put over a low cross for Joao Pedro to score. It was 3-0.

View 3 Images Emiliano Martinez made his debut after joining from Aston Villa

Just three minutes later, Brighton gave themselves a glimmer of hope. Brighton striker Charalampos Kostoulas went through, Chelsea new boy Martinez saved bravely at his feet but Malick Yalcouyé smashed the loose ball in off the far post.

‌



Chelsea have not kept a clean sheet in the Premier League since last January. And worse was to follow. Martinez can expect to be busy. Then the comedy punchline. Pascal Gross’s low cross was deflected in off Joao Pedro. The Brighton fans were lapping it up and, from 3-0 down, the fightback was on. This had turned into a sensational game at 3-2.

But Brighton could not seize the opportunity. It was left to Palmer to steal the show again. Palmer strode forward from midfield, had time to pick his spot and fired into the bottom corner to make it safe at 4-2.

Still there was time for one more goal as Gross got a third for Brighton in the 96th minute. Clean sheets are a worry but who cares when you play such great attacking football? Chelsea fans don’t seem bothered.

Sports.title: Arsenal primed for chaotic end to window with winger signing and three exits agreed
Sports.content:
Arsenal primed for chaotic end to window with winger signing and three exits agreed

Arsenal are having to sanction several exits in the final days of the transfer window with some of their fringe players, Gabriel Martinelli among them, seeking pastures new

View 3 Images Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus are both poised to leave Arsenal (Image: Crystal Pix/MB Media/Getty Images)

Arsenal haven't rested on their laurels this summer and despite completing some blockbuster deals the club have still been active ahead of Tuesday's deadline.

‌



The Premier League champions looked in total control in their opening game as they hammered Coventry City at the Emirates. They did so with new signing Christos Tzolis impressing from the left wing following his summer move from Club Brugge.

‌



Mikel Arteta was without Bruno Guimaraes, who was dealing with an injury which meant he couldn't take up his role in midfield, whilst Ezri Konsa wasn't signed and registered in time from Aston Villa. He could make his debut on Monday night against his former club.

‌



Arsenal's arrivals has left them with a star-studded squad, but one that ultimately has too many senior players for even a matchday squad. Arteta has bemoaned the fact he's had to leave certain players out, suggesting the authorities should increase the size of the benches.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

He had claimed that certain absentees, the likes of Gabriel Jesus and Gabriel Martinelli, were still part of his plans, but with days left in the window both are poised to depart.

‌



Brazilian duo among three to exit

Jesus looks to have landed himself a sensational move to Barcelona having been linked with a switch to Italy for much of the summer. The Spanish champions will pay £8.4million for the 29-year-old, who had entered the final year of his contract.

Jesus was one of the signings that saw Arsenal turn into title contenders when he joined from Manchester City in 2022. He was initially a regular but over the years has seen his role decrease, in part owing to injury, and now has Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz ahead of him in the pecking order.

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta has been forced to let some of his attacking player leave such is the depth of his squad (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

‌



Compatriot Gabriel Martinelli was alongside Jesus in a front three that also included Bukayo Saka when Arsenal first challenged for the Premier League under Arteta. But, like Jesus, his role has been impacted by the club's constant desire to add more firepower.

Unlike Jesus, who Arsenal will make a loss on, Martinelli stands to represent a huge profit having been signed as an unknown quantity. A £60m switch to Saudi Arabia is now close.

Another fringe player in Fabio Vieira, who was signed in 2022 but has made just five league starts in that time, is set for a permanent switch to Hamburg. He had spent last season on loan at the Bundesliga side and is now set to call them home moving forward.

‌



Winger signed as Alvarez saga drags on

Even with Jesus and Martinelli set to leave, Arteta can still look to the likes of Gyokeres, Havertz, Saka, Tzolis, Eberechi Eze, Noni Madueke, Martin Odegaard and Ethan Nwaneri as options in the final third.

View 3 Images Julian Alvarez has been pushing for the exit door at Atletico Madrid (Image: (Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press via Getty Images))

Despite that they've still agreed a £4m deal for young Georgian winger Andria Bartishvili. The teenager was also on Liverpool's radar but has opted for a switch to the capital.

‌



Julian Alvarez's saga has dragged on all summer and, despite skipping Atletico Madrid training this week, the club are adamant he will not be sold to Barcelona. The Catalan's pursuit of Jesus does fill the void they had in their attack, which they had hoped Alvarez would fill.

If the Argentine does want to leave Atletico it would appear as though Arsenal are his only option. Diego Simeone is still prepared to welcome him back and Alvarez has returned to training, which would indicate he's much closer to staying rather than heading back to the Premier League.

Sports.title: Arsenal set to smash transfer record as Gabriel Martinelli closes in on Gunners exit
Sports.content:
Arsenal set to smash transfer record as Gabriel Martinelli closes in on Gunners exit

Arsenal have spent a considerable amount this summer as they attempt to defend their Premier League crown but a few title winners could potentially be on the way out of the Emirates over the coming days

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli is set to earn Arsenal a record amount (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal star Gabriel Martinelli is set to leave the Emirates and join Al-Hilal for a record £55m. The Brazilian winger has been linked with a move away from North London throughout the summer.

‌



Saudi side Al-Hilal had emerged as suitors over recent days and had been holding talks with the Gunners in an effort to secure a deal. And it appears that they have done just that.

‌



According to reports, Martinelli is set to fly over to the Middle East over the next few days to undergo a medical and complete a move worth around €65m (£55.7m) ahead of Tuesday's deadline.

‌



Should the move go through as expected, it would see Arsenal bank their highest fee ever for a sale, smashing the £35m that they received from Liverpool for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain back in 2017.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Asked about Martinelli's future in his pre-match press conference, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said: "That's another personal situation that we're dealing with. I think everybody knows and recognises how much we love Gabi. Whatever the outcome is, it will be because everybody agrees to that."

‌



Martinelli joined Arsenal from Brazilian side Ituano in 2019 and he has gone on to score 62 goals in 278 appearances in all competitions. He helped the club win the Premier League last season.

Martinelli is not the only league winner set to leave the club over the coming days. Striker Gabriel Jesus is anticipated to complete a switch to Barcelona.

Asked why the forward was not in training, Arteta said: "It's something to do with the numbers that we have in the squad at the moment and the way we're managing that kind of situation individually with all the players - they have some personal situations."

‌



View 2 Images Gabriel Jesus is also expected to quit Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Asked if he had held conversations with either Martinelli or Jesus, Arteta replied: "Yes, for sure. Those conversations go both ways, but I'm very satisfied with how these conversations went because I know what is in each other's hearts, and the words that come through in those conversations make me really happy.

"But it's inevitable at some point you need to have certain discussions and say certain things that sometimes are tough."

‌



Along with Jesus and Martinelli, Fabio Vieira is also set to depart, with talks over an £8.6m move to Hamburg advancing.

Leandro Trossard, Christian Norgaard and Jakub Kiwior have all left North London over recent weeks, while academy graduate Reiss Nelson saw his deal cancelled by mutual consent. Arsenal have refreshed their side with a number of big-money signings including Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis, Ezri Konsa and Piero Hincapie.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso speaks after axing Enzo Fernandez again and hints at Chelsea exit
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso speaks after axing Enzo Fernandez again and hints at Chelsea exit

Enzo Fernandez has been left out of Chelsea’s squad for their last two games and Blues boss Xabi Alonso has discussed the midfielder’s future ahead Tuesday’s transfer deadline

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez has missed Chelsea's last two games (Image: Getty Images)

Xabi Alonso has said that keeping Enzo Fernandez out of the Chelsea team is ‘for the best’, while suggesting Robert Sanchez could be shown the exit door. The Argentine midfielder has been linked with a move away from Stamford Bridge over recent days.

‌



Manchester City have emerged as suitors and Enzo Maresca’s side are expected to lodge a big-money bid soon despite having already signed Elliot Anderson and Ayoubb Bouaddi to bolster their midfield.

‌



In the meantime, Fernandez has been exiled from first-team action. He was left out of the side that took on Luton Town in the second round of the Carabao Cup in midweek, while he was also sidelined for the clash with Brighton at Stamford Bridge.

‌



Asked why he was left out once again, Chelsea boss Alonso said: "We assess what's best for the team. We need the team to be focused."

Meanwhile, another absentee was goalkeeper Robert Sanchez, the Spaniard having lost his starting berth to summer arrival Emi Martinez. And asked about the stopper, the Chelsea boss was somewhat cryptic. He said: "We will see. Sometimes you have to take tough decisions."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Alonso’s comments on Fernandez come after he made a similar claim in the week. Asked about Fernandez’s situation, the Spanish coach said: “I have said we need the players that are in the best situation to play.

“We need to take everything into consideration — players that are in a good moment, players that are not feeling that energy to play. For me, it is very important that they feel this desire to play and to have good preparation.”

Asked if Fernandez had lost the desire to play, Alonso replied: “We talked, and we decided for [Luton] it was better not to be part of the squad. He is a top player.”

‌



View 2 Images Xabi Alonso has spoken out on Enzo Fernandez's future once again (Image: Getty Images)

Fernandez, 25, signed for Chelsea from Benfica in 2023 and he has gone on to make 170 appearances for the club and scored 31 goals. He still has six years left to run on his deal in West London.

It has previously been suggested that Chelsea will only sell for around £120m. Should Fernandez move to the Etihad, he would become the latest high-profile midfield addition of the summer after Anderson and Bouaddi.

‌



City’s spending is also not expected to stop there either. They are also in pole position to seal a deal for Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo, with the two clubs now in talks to find an agreement.

Asked this week if more additions could be on the way, City boss Maresca said: “We have experienced players, for sure we have leaders. Now we need to wait 4-5 days for when the transfer window closes also to see if we can add one or two more captains to Ruben [Dias] and Erling [Haaland], at the moment they are the two captains. It’s a young squad and also we have some experienced players.”

Sports.title: Chelsea beat Brighton in seven-goal thriller to continue Alonso's winning start
Sports.content:
Chelsea held off a Brighton fightback to clinch a thrilling 4-3 victory and continue their winning start under manager Xabi Alonso.

The Blues raced into a three-goal lead through Romeo Lavia, Pedro Neto and former Brighton forward Joao Pedro in a scintillating opening period at Stamford Bridge, but the visitors responded.

Malick Yalcoule slammed home before the break to give them hope and they reduced the deficit to one goal when a Pascal Gross shot deflected off Joao Pedro and beyond Emiliano Martinez, who was making his debut following his £7.5m arrival from Aston Villa.

Brighton had further chances, with Diego Gomez going close and Martinez making several impressive stops as the visitors limited Chelsea to only 25.6 per cent possession, the club's lowest share on record in a Premier League game.

But Cole Palmer found the bottom corner in superb style for Chelsea's fourth goal, meaning there was no time for Brighton to mount a comeback when Gross headed in deep in stoppage time.

Image: Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez reacts after Joao Pedro's own goal

Chelsea were without Enzo Fernandez, who was left out of the squad for a second consecutive game amid interest from Manchester City, while Moises Caicedo had to come off injured soon after coming on for his first appearance of the season.

But the victory continues a positive start under Alonso. While the new Chelsea manager has issues to address defensively, his side's new-look attack proved too much for their opponent for the second game in a row following their 3-2 win over Fulham.

Joao Pedro and Palmer were on target for a second consecutive game, while record signing Morgan Rogers added an assist to his goal against the Cottagers when he crossed for Neto's strike.

Brighton, meanwhile, showed impressive spirit after their nightmarish start to the game despite a lengthy list of injuries, with Yasin Ayari missing out along with forwards Georginio Rutter, Jack Hinshelwood, Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh.

Key moments at Stamford Bridge

4: GOAL! Lavia pounces on an error by Bart Verbruggen to score Chelsea's opener from close range following a corner.

Lavia pounces on an error by Bart Verbruggen to score Chelsea's opener from close range following a corner. 14: GOAL! Rogers sets up Neto for Chelsea's second goal.

Rogers sets up Neto for Chelsea's second goal. 25: MISS! Joao Pedro misses a glorious chance to score when he slots wide from 10 yards out.

Joao Pedro misses a glorious chance to score when he slots wide from 10 yards out. 32: GOAL! Joao Pedro finishes of an electrifying Chelsea counter then celebrates in front of the Brighton fans having been booed.

Joao Pedro finishes of an electrifying Chelsea counter then celebrates in front of the Brighton fans having been booed. 35: GOAL! Yalcouye sends a thumping finish in off the woodwork as Brighton instantly respond.

Yalcouye sends a thumping finish in off the woodwork as Brighton instantly respond. 63: OWN GOAL! Joao Pedro inadvertently sends the ball past Martinez from Gross's shot as Brighton strike again.

Joao Pedro inadvertently sends the ball past Martinez from Gross's shot as Brighton strike again. 74: GOAL! Palmer drives forward and sends a sumptuous finish into the corner from the edge of the box for Chelsea's fourth.

Palmer drives forward and sends a sumptuous finish into the corner from the edge of the box for Chelsea's fourth. 81: INJURY? Caicedo looks emotional as he heads down the tunnel with an injury

Caicedo looks emotional as he heads down the tunnel with an injury 90+6: GOAL! Gross heads past Martinez but it's too little, too late as it's followed by the final whistle.

WATCH: All the goals

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Romeo Lavia is quick to react to score his first Chelsea goal

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Morgan Rogers sets up Pedro Neto for the second

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jorrel Hato finds Joao Pedro to add a slick third goal

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Malick Yalcouye pulls one back in style

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joao Pedro scores a own goal against his old club

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cole Palmer restores Chelsea's two-goal cushion

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pascal Gross scores Brighton's third goal

Explosive Joao Pedro silences boos

Sky Sports' Nick Wright at Stamford Bridge:

Brighton supporters made their feelings about Joao Pedro clear before the game had even started, greeting his name with cacophonous boos every time it was read out by the PA announcer. The hostility only seemed to make him more determined.

The 24-year-old, clearly fresh after his inexplicable World Cup omission by Brazil, picked up where he left off against Fulham, tearing into Brighton right from the start of the game, running the channels, holding the ball up and dovetailing with team-mates.

"I think he's in the form of his life," said Sky Sports pundit Alan Smith. "I haven't seen him play better than he has in the first two games."

Joao Pedro had his head in his hands when he dragged wide 25 minutes in but didn't have to wait long for his goal, finishing off a sensational counter-attack only a few minutes later and making the point of running over to the Brighton fans to celebrate.

Image: Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer combined impressively for Chelsea

His unfortunate own goal was only a minor blot on his afternoon and he was unlucky not to score more. He ranked top among Chelsea players for shots, touches in the opposition box, dribbles and fouls won and proved a constant menace to Brighton.

His total of 13 duels won was the second highest by any player in a Premier League game so far this season and underlined the physical prowess that contributes to making him such a handful.

Smith added: "People wondered if he was an out-and-out centre forward. He's playing like one. His movement has been brilliant, he's scoring goals. A great boost for Chelsea."

Is Chelsea's low possession a problem?

Chelsea supporters were delighted by the speed and incisiveness of their side's attacks but their victory also featured a record low share of possession. Their total of only 146 successful passes was also their lowest on record in a Premier League game.

It followed them having only 38 per cent of the possession in their opening win against Fulham. But does it matter? Few fans would say so, as long as the results continue to go their way.

Alonso was also keen to point out the importance of context. As against Fulham, his side spent almost the entire game leading against Brighton, meaning the attacking onus was on their opponent.

"You need to have context for every data for sure," he said. "After 30 minutes we scored the 3-0. Probably in that moment, we played too much with the result instead of keeping playing.

"But the data is not important, it is how you play and what we can do better. But it is never that approach, I don't say today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 cent. I never talk about those things, it is about how to prepare, how to be more competitive."

Alonso on Fernandez, Caicedo, Martinez

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso said:

"All the wins, I enjoy them a lot. It was a game of different moments, different feelings and the end we are happy with the result."

On Enzo Fernandez's future: "We'll see. We want the best for the team. That's why we made the decision against Luton and today. Anything that happens before Tuesday evening, we need to be aware of what is going to develop.

"We are not sure, we are preparing for all the scenarios, but I am sure that whatever happens from Wednesday, we will have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Emiliano Martinez says he has joined Chelsea to win the title

On Emiliano Martinez's debut: "With Emi, World Cup winner, experience all around. I spoke with him yesterday [Saturday]. We talked about the game, about our team. He felt ready.

"I don't have to say many things for him to perform. He wanted to have a clean sheet but I'm happy. He has only been here for 48 hours, so now we have to help him prepare for the next one.

"He has charisma and aura to have a very positive influence on the rest of them."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Could Emiliano Martinez be the difference for Chelsea?

On Moises Caicedo's injury: "Hopefully it was not new and it wasn't more than last time. He was cautious to stop, to say that his feeling was not the best, but we need to assess during the week. But it wasn't something new."

Hurzeler praises Brighton efforts

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said:

"I would never sit in any press conference and complain about the injuries. It's part of football. I see it more as an opportunity to step up and that's what the other boys showed today.

"Everyone who saw the game couldn't believe it was 3-0 for Chelsea. But afterwards they showed a big belief.

"We made the 3-1, we were there to control the game, create chances. We dominated the game and made the 3-2. We had a chance to make the 3-3 and then who knows?

"Overall we weren't clean enough in the basics. We missed the balance. But to come to this place and create that many chances and cause that many problems is something where I have to give my players a lot of credit. We will make a step and keep trying to improve the boys."

Sports.title: England seal series victory against Pakistan as Robinson shines
Sports.content:
Joe Root’s second stint as England captain got off to a flying start as his side cruised to a comfortable 194-run win over Pakistan at Lord’s to seal the series, going 2-0 up with a game to go.

On a pitch that was heavily weighted towards the bowlers, England advanced their lead by 32 runs on day four to set Pakistan a huge total of 389 to win.

Mohammad Abbas tore through England's tail order on Sunday, taking a haul of five wickets, as the hosts were bowled out for 208 runs.

But Pakistan were unable to eat into the hosts' total, with a ruthless Ollie Robinson, back at his happy hunting ground at Lord's, taking four wickets on Sunday to bring up a match haul of eight as the hosts rattled their way through the visitors' batting line-up.

Pakistan were bowled out for 194 on Sunday, with Robinson taking the wickets of Pakistan's Azan Awais (7) and Abdullah Shafique (0) in the space of four deliveries, before also snaring Mohammad Rizwan (1) and Abdullah Shafique (0).

Jofra Archer also impressed, again showcasing his lightning pace to take figures of 2-73.

Sports.title: Manchester United v Ipswich Town: Premier League – live
Sports.content:
2m ago 13.33 EDT “There have been 17 goals today,” says Kelly Cates. A quick recap: Chelsea 4-3 Brighton, Leeds 1-1 Brentford, Sunderland 1-0 Fulham (they don’t do seven-goal thrillers there), and now Man United 5-2 Ipswich. The highlights of this game will be well worth catching – it was fun to watch even when it was 0-1. Share

6m ago 13.30 EDT On expected goals, the score was the same, more or less. United’s xG according to Sofascore was 4.57, while Ipswich’s was 2.01. Share

7m ago 13.28 EDT Ipswich can leave Manchester with their heads held high. They were excellent for an hour and spirited throughout. Share

8m ago 13.27 EDT FULL TIME! Man United 5-2 Ipswich United fell behind again, and were lucky to draw level – but then they turned on the style as Bruno Fernandes helped himself to a hat-trick. He even scored from the spot. Share

10m ago 13.25 EDT 90+6 min Better from Dorgu, whose fierce shot draws a save from Scherpen and wins a corner. Share

12m ago 13.24 EDT 90+4 min Dorgu shows his strength, racing away on the counter, and then his weakness – making decisions in the box. He can’t decide whether to shoot or cross to Mbeumo and ends up doing both, or neither. Share

13m ago 13.22 EDT 90+3 min We’re having eight added minutes, so technically there’s time for Ipswich to get a couple more. As they advance down the left, Mbeumo resorts to a foul and collects a yellow card. But Davis’s free kick is an easy take for Lammens. Share

15m ago 13.21 EDT GOAL! Man United 5-2 Ipswich (Akpom 90+1) And there it is! Martinez dawdles on the ball and has his pocket picked by Enciso, whose cross requires only a tap-in from Chuba Akpom. Share

17m ago 13.19 EDT 89 min Ipswich push upfield, searching for the second goal they deserve. They do have a shot but it’s from way out and the whistle has gone for a foul on Tielemans. Share

20m ago 13.16 EDT 87 min In case you’re just joining us, the scoreline is very hard on Ipswich, who played really well for an hour. Share

21m ago 13.15 EDT 85 min United have had 31 shots, ten of them on target. And now they have their 32nd and their 11th – a flying header from Dorgu at the far post, straight at Scherpen. Share

23m ago 13.13 EDT GOAL!!!!! Man United 5-1 Ipswich (Mbeumo 82) This one’s a beauty. Fernandes sends a gorgeous through ball to Mbeumo, who beats the advancing Scherpen with an equally gorgeous finish – crafty, calculated, elegant and worthy of a man who loves to play chess. Share

25m ago 13.10 EDT 81 min Fernandes has yet another shot as the rain gets heavier. And another old friend is back: the Old Trafford leak. Share

26m ago 13.09 EDT 80 min Rashford is going off now, along with Cunha and Mainoo. They’ve all been good. On come Sesko up top, Dorgu on the left and Andrey Santos in the pivot, for his home debut. Share

28m ago 13.08 EDT 79 min The crowd roar for Rashford – because he’s tracked back and made a tackle! Share

29m ago 13.07 EDT 73 min United advance again. Martinez plays a wonder-ball down the middle to Rashford, who twists and turns and nutmegs someone but can’t carve out the space for a proper shot. Cunha does get a shot away, from the right, and sees it well saved by Scherpen. Share

31m ago 13.05 EDT 73 min Rashford pauses on the wing, twice, looking for his mate Shaw, who’s on the bench. Noussair Mazraoui hasn’t quite got the memo. Share

32m ago 13.04 EDT 73 min It looks as if Ipswich have gone to a back five. This may be a case of the Tractor Boys shutting the gate after the horse has bolted. Share

33m ago 13.03 EDT 73 min Two subs for either side: Maeda and Lukic give way to Furlong and Ouattara, and Carrick springs a surprise by replacing both full-backs – Dalot and Shaw off, Yoro and Mazraoui on. Share

35m ago 13.01 EDT 70 min The move for United’s fourth goal was a comedy of errors from Ipswich. It began with Rashford advancing down the left. His cross was wayward, but the ball fell to Mainoo, whose rasping shot was deflected to Mbeumo. His shot was so tame that he apologised, but again there was a ricochet. Fernandes, lurking like a poacher, took one deft touch and then passed into the corner. The man has so much main-character energy. Share

37m ago 12.58 EDT 69 min Fernandes has nearly scored a fourth! From the centre circle! But his swerving lob landed on the roof of the net. That was Beckhamesque. Share

39m ago 12.57 EDT GOAL!!! Man United 4-1 Ipswich (Fernandes 67) It’s a hat-trick for Bruno Fernandes! View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes of Manchester United scores a goal to make it 4-1. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images Share Updated at 13.06 EDT

40m ago 12.55 EDT 66 min A camera zooms in on Michael Carrick, who looks just as he did at 1-0 down – thoughtful, a touch quizzical. Rudyard Kipling would have approved of him. Share

42m ago 12.53 EDT 64 min Shot! By Rashford – a rasping volley that Scherpen does well to tip away for a corner. Share

43m ago 12.52 EDT 63 min As Alex Ferguson looks on, delightedly, Gary O’Neil may be thinking “Football, bloody hell.” He responds by reaching for his new toy, Exequiel Palacios, who replaces the unfortunate Nunez. Share

45m ago 12.51 EDT 62 min The keeper, Scherpen, stood offf-centre. “The only person he confused,” says Gary Neville, “was himself.” Share

46m ago 12.50 EDT GOAL! Man United 3-1 Ipswich (Fernandes 61 pen) Fernandes takes an age, but finds the corner! View image in fullscreen Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes scores their side's third goal of the game from a penalty. Photograph: David Davies/PA Share Updated at 12.55 EDT

47m ago 12.49 EDT 60 min Bruno Fernandes has the ball. He missed his last two penalties… Share

47m ago 12.48 EDT PENALTY TO MAN UNITED! Mainoo sends Cunha clean through and poor old Jacob Greaves brings him down. Craig Pawson points to the spot and gives him a yellow card. View image in fullscreen Matheus Cunha of Manchester United is challenged by Jacob Greaves of Ipswich Town which results in Referee Craig Pawson awarding a penalty. Photograph: Dan Mullan/Getty Images Share Updated at 12.54 EDT

48m ago 12.47 EDT GOAL CONFIRMED! Man United 2-1 Ipswich (Greaves og 57) It’s given – because it was an own goal! And an accidental handball, which is allowed from anyone bar the scorer. Share

50m ago 12.46 EDT GOAL? United 2-1 Ipswich maybe (Maguire 57) Harry Maguire scores with his foot! From the edge of the box. But did his hand play a part too? The VAR is on the case. View image in fullscreen Manchester United's Harry Maguire celebrates after Ipswich Town's Jacob Greaves scores an own goal. Photograph: David Davies/PA Share Updated at 12.53 EDT

51m ago 12.44 EDT 55 min Ipswich even get a corner, though nothing comes of it… Share

52m ago 12.43 EDT 53 min “It’s a United siege now,” says the commentator. It’s certainly ping-pong in the box as Mainoo has a shot, possibly two, but Ipswich swith theiree off the danger with some quick wits and firm blocks. Share

54m ago 12.41 EDT 52 min Mbeumo, slipped in by Fernandes, bustles into the box before picking the wrong pass. Then Rashford sends in a left-foot volleyed cross which Mbeumo has to score from – but he hits the bar! Share

1h ago 12.39 EDT 50 min Sure enough, the first shot of the half comes from Enciso, who hits it over the bar from 25 yards. “He’s been the best player on the pitch,” says Gary Neville. Share

1h ago 12.38 EDT 48 min United pass the ball around, harmlessly. Ipswich have less of the ball but use it more purposefully. They have the air of a team whose manager has just told them they can win this. Share

1h ago 12.36 EDT 47 min United kick off, but Ipswich start sharply and Enciso wins a free kick off Cunha. Share

1h ago 12.31 EDT “As a United fan,” says David Flynn, “I feel like commentators and journalists are under some sort of mass psychosis when it comes to Marcus Rashford. He has spent his entire United career being massively inconsistent, more often than not playing poorly and there’s absolutely no evidence that has changed. “He might very well score a hat trick today but the one thing you can be sure of is that there’s a ten month goal drought in his future. I think the press needs to accept that and stop getting excited when he starts.” More often than not playing poorly? That’s quite a harsh view of a player who had scored about 130 goals in 400 games for United before turning 27. And who, as he has (gently) pointed out himself, has had to cope with inconsistent management – from Van Gaal to Mourinho to Solskjaer to Rangnick to Ten Hag to Amorim and now Carrick, who seems to have handled him well so far. Rashford has been bright today, for what it’s worth. Share

1h ago 12.27 EDT Time for a glance at the post. “United fan here,” wrote Joshua Keeling about 20 minutes ago. “Can’t wait to see who this season’s caretaker manager will be.” Ouch! “They can spend a much as they want on their midfield and attack,” says Matthew Lysaght, “but persisting with any or all of Maguire/Dalot/Shaw makes that expenditure null and void.” You may be right, but one of them went to the World Cup and the other two were unlucky to be rebuffed by Thomas Tuchel. “Hey Tim,” says Alan Steenstrup in Querétaro, Mexico. “You wrote: ‘As expected, Carrick has Mbeumo on the right, Mbeumo in the middle and Rashford on the left.’ A bit of multi-talking for Mbeumo, if anyone can, he can.” Good line! Sorry, I meant Cunha in the middle. He’s been better today than at Hull, though Sesko’s height will be handy, when he comes on, in the face of Scherpen. Share

1h ago 12.20 EDT HALF-TIME! Man United 1-1 Ipswich It’s been a lively half, packed with action at both ends. Ipswich were very good for ten minutes in the middle and led through a classy shot from Leif Davis. But then Marcelino Nunez slipped on the damp, relaid turf and allowed Matheus Cunha to start a counter that ended with an equally fine finish from Bruno Fernandes. Share

1h ago 12.17 EDT 45+1 min We’re into the first of two added minutes. Dalot’s shot takes a deflection and brings a corner, but all United get out of that is a throw-in or two … until Lisandro Martinez takes a long shot, crisply struck but too high. Share

1h ago 12.15 EDT 42 min Buoyed by the goal, Fernandes brings out a back-heel (which doesn’t find its target). Then Tielemans goes down inside the box, the crowd roar for a penalty… and the ref refuses to play ball. It may have been a foul by O’Shea, but the dying fall was too theatrical to be convincing. Share

1h ago 12.12 EDT 42 min We’ve seen that goal before from Carrick’s United, but usually it’s Fernandes playing the pass and Mbeumo supplying the finish. Share

1h ago 12.11 EDT GOAL!! Man United 1-1 Ipswich (Fernandes 40) Nunez slips in midfield, Cunha breaks away on the counter and slips it to Fernandes, who blasts a left-foot shot past Scherpen. View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes scores their first goal. Photograph: Jon Super/Reuters View image in fullscreen And celebrates scoring. Photograph: Jon Super/Reuters Share Updated at 12.19 EDT

1h ago 12.10 EDT 38 min Fernandes tries a short-corner routine but messes it up by passing straight to a defender. Rashford manages a cross, only to see it gobbled up by the giant Scherpen. Share

1h ago 12.08 EDT 37 min Another foul, and it’s an ugly one. Fatawu goes sliding in on Mbeumo and gets a booking. He may be in trouble with the Union of Right-Wingers too. Share

1h ago 12.07 EDT 36 min Ipswich, by the way, haven’t won at Old Trafford since 1984. Share

1h ago 12.06 EDT 35 min United’s turn to commit a gratuitous foul as Harry Maguire manhandles Emersonn near the halfway line. Tielemans is then caught napping, but United see off the danger. Share

2h ago 12.04 EDT 34 min Sasa Lukic, who’s been a big presence in midfield, brings down Tielemans when he doesn’t need to, and gets a yellow card. Share

2h ago 12.04 EDT 33 min The cameras find Michael Carrick looking pensive, as well he may. Are United disintegrating again in the face of a promoted team with a bit of spirit? Share

2h ago 12.03 EDT 31 min Chance for Ipswich: Davis again! It’s another fine cross from Fatawu. Davis, perhaps surprised to find himself getting all these openings, shoots a bit limply at point-blank range. Share

2h ago 12.00 EDT GOAL! Man United 0-1 Ipswich (Davis 29) It’s last weekend all over again! Fatawu surges down the right wing, shrugs off Shaw and crosses to Davis, whose finish goes in off the bar. View image in fullscreen Bang: Leif Davis of Ipswich Town scores the opening goal. Photograph: Matt West/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes with that familiar sinking feeling holds his head in his hands. Photograph: David Davies/PA Share Updated at 12.06 EDT

2h ago 11.58 EDT 28 min Another minute, another United attack. Mbeumo curls in a cross from the right which is just too high for Fernandes and Rashford, coming in at the far post. Share

2h ago 11.57 EDT 27 min “United’s midfield were criticised for not being positive enough last week,” Gary Neville says, “and they’ve been better here, Mainoo and Fernandes linking well.” Share

Sports.title: Chelsea hold off Brighton in 4-3 win but remain chaotic under Xabi Alonso
Sports.content:
In the fullness of time Chelsea’s surrender against Brighton & Hove Albion last April may come to be seen as the turning point. The humiliation accelerated Liam Rosenior’s demise and forced the Stamford Bridge hierarchy into a reckoning which has led to the appointment of Xabi Alonso, a shift in the transfer strategy, the JP Morgan front three and the end of Robert Sánchez’s time as the No 1 goalkeeper.

For now, though, the argument that Emiliano Martínez is the final piece in the jigsaw seems a touch premature. There are many enjoyable parts to Alonso’s rejigged Chelsea, especially when Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and João Pedro click in attack, but other problems remain and the early evidence suggests a title challenge will only be sustained if performances become less chaotic.

Alonso looked ready to erupt when Chelsea found themselves clinging on to their lead midway through the second half. His side had made a blistering start to this game, rattling three unanswered goals past a weakened Brighton, but the level dipped. Anxiety gripped Stamford Bridge for a while and although Palmer took over during the dying stages, cutting inside to make it 4-2 with a beautiful finish, there is a sense that Chelsea’s winning start to the Alonso era has been a bit too fun.

View image in fullscreen Xabi Alonso has won his first two league games as Chelsea manager, but neither have been what you would call relaxing. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

Conceding five goals in their first two league games is not good enough. Martínez played well but was denied a clean sheet on his debut after joining from Aston Villa for £7.5m. Brighton exposed shortcomings in the system and Alonso will want more control.

Chelsea have had varying degrees of success plundering talent from Brighton during the last four years. João Pedro goes down as a hit, Graham Potter a definite miss, while Sánchez is soon to be cast aside after his unconvincing performance against Fulham convinced Alonso it was time for a change in goal.

Sánchez was not even on the bench against his old side and there was a huge ovation for Martínez before kick-off. The Argentinian’s handling was commanding and something Brighton lacked when the focus fell on Fabian Hürzeler’s goalkeeper.

Chelsea led after four minutes. João Pedro flicked a corner goalwards and Mats Wieffer blocked on the line. The danger appeared to be over, only for Bart Verbruggen to scoop the ball away from his team-mate and into the path of Roméo Lavia, who punished the Brighton goalkeeper’s mistake by jabbing a low finish into the net.

It was a lovely moment for Lavia. It was four years to the day since the Belgian’s midfielder last goal, against Chelsea coincidentally enough, and he will hope his rotten luck with injuries is about to turn.

View image in fullscreen Roméo Lavia was on hand to punish Bart Verbruggen’s early handling error and put Chelsea 1-0 up. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Lavia has had a good start to the season. His ability to start for the second consecutive league game was important given that Chelsea were a little light in midfield. Moisés Caicedo and Reece James were only fit enough to start as substitutes and Enzo Fernández was again not in the right frame of mind to play with a move to Manchester City on the cards, so Malo Gusto moved in from right wing-back to form a new partnership with Lavia.

Not that Chelsea’s selection issues came close to matching Brighton’s injury list. Jack Hinshelwood, Yasin Ayari, Georginio Rutter, Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh were all unavailable and the visitors were shambolic without them at first.

Chelsea were merciless. Morgan Rogers continued his fine start after joining from Villa, creating the second goal with a powerful surge away from Luka Vuskovic in the 13th minute. Brighton were caught cold by a throw-in and Rogers crossed for Pedro Neto to score.

Linked with a move away this summer, Neto has been repurposed as a wing-back by Alonso and was bright. The Portugal international’s commitment forced another error from Brighton, who escaped when João Pedro shot wide.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The away end jeered their old boy but João Pedro would not be denied. Soon Rogers produced a flick to send Jorrel Hato flying down the left, Wieffer trailing behind. All alone in the middle, he was ruthless this time.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro rather summed up Chelsea’s start under Xabi Alonso with a goal, an assist and an own goal. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Game over? Not quite. Brighton stayed honest and had hope before half-time, Malick Yalcouyé volleying in a debut goal after Martínez made a brave block from Charalampos Kostoulas.

There was a different feel in the second half. Palmer side-footed over from two yards and Chelsea wobbled. Diego Gómez sent a free header wide and had a shot saved by Martínez. Emboldened, Brighton pushed. They recycled possession from a corner and Yalcouyé released Pascal Gross, whose cross deflected in off João Pedro.

Gómez rattled another shot just wide and Alonso screamed at his substitutes to get ready. Caicedo, James and Josh Acheampong came on but Chelsea were anxious and Martínez had to save well from Olivier Boscagli.

Alonso was calmer when João Pedro combined with Palmer, who dipped inside to curl a brilliant shot past Verbruggen from 20 yards. The watching Thomas Tuchel and Carlo Ancelotti, who left Palmer and João Pedro out of their respective World Cup squads, must have approved. Alonso, though, finished with a few headaches. Caicedo limped off shortly after his introduction and Gross pulled another goal back for Brighton, albeit so deep into added time that there was only just time to restart the game.

Sports.title: Transfer roundup: Ollie Watkins completes move to Al-Hilal from Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Al-Hilal have signed Ollie Watkins from Aston Villa, ⁠the two clubs announced on Sunday, as the 30-year-old striker ended a successful ⁠six-year spell with ⁠the ​Midlands club where he became their top scorer in the Premier League. The England international, who had ​two years left on ‌his Villa contract, has moved for a reported £51m.

Watkins ‌signed a three-year contract as Al-Hilal acquired ‌a proven goalscorer after he scored 21 goals in all competitions last season, including five goals in the Europa League as he helped deliver a European trophy to Unai Emery’s side.

However, an ‌exit was on the cards before the transfer window closed, with Emery revealing the ​striker had apologised for making himself unavailable for the club’s Premier League opener, a 4-0 defeat at Brighton.

Watkins scored 91 Premier League goals for Villa and 108 ⁠in all competitions since arriving from Brentford for £28m in ​2020. The striker is among ​a string of departures from Villa ​in the ‌close season following ​the ​exits of key players such as Morgan Rogers and Emi Martinez to Chelsea – the latter moving on Sunday – Ezri Konsa to Arsenal and Youri Tielemans to Manchester United.

Quick Guide How do I 

Roma have stepped up their Serie A challenge with the acquisition of two captains, midfielder Marten De Roon coming over from Atalanta and centre-back Leonardo Balerdi joining from Marseille. The 35-year-old De Roon evolved into Atalanta’s skipper after a decade spent in Bergamo over two spells. He will reunite with Roma’s manager Gian Piero Gasperini, who formerly coached him at Atalanta.

And the former Serie A MVP Rafael Leão has completed a €38m transfer from Milan to Galatasaray. The Turkish side confirmed a deal for the Portugal winger, signing him to a four-year contract with a net salary of €10m per season.

Sports.title: Sunderland’s Wilson Isidor applies the finishing touch to sink Fulham
Sports.content:
At the final whistle Álvaro Arbeloa provided a study in pensiveness while Régis Le Bris simply looked relieved. An almost palpable fear of losing formed the subtext of a match decided when two of the Sunderland manager’s second-half substitutes, Habib Diarra and Wilson Isidor, combined for the latter to score.

Isidor’s goal not merely supplied Sunderland with their first win of the season while leaving Arbeloa’s side pointless but ended his club’s 17-year run without a Premier League victory against Fulham.

The tone of a cagey, risk-averse first half was raised by a typically superior central midfield performance on the part of Sunderland’s Noah Sadiki. Indeed the Democratic Republic of the Congo international extinguished so many potential visiting fires that Fulham’s sole real chance during the opening 45 minutes involved Josh King finding himself confounded by geometry as he miscued a tightly angled opening conjured by Alex Iwobi. Otherwise the home goalkeeper, Robin Roefs, was left pretty much undisturbed.

That apart, a slightly nervous impasse endured. Despite dominating possession, Sunderland’s attacking edge proved anything but serrated, leaving Bernd Leno severely underemployed in Fulham’s goal.

It all left both Le Bris and Arbeloa with much to ponder at the interval. If the watching Sunderland owner, Kyril-Louis Dreyfus, required a reminder as to precisely why Le Bris is so keen to sign a specialist right-winger and another striker before the transfer window’s closure, he had received it.

At least Sunderland’s manager had Nordi Mukiele restored to central defence after injury. The former Paris Saint-Germain defender’s importance on Wearside was underscored early in the second half when his tremendous sliding challenge blocked Gonzalo García’s path to a near-certain goal after Sander Berge’s stellar through pass.

View image in fullscreen Wilson Isidor salutes the fans after scoring. Photograph: Matt McNulty/Getty Images

García had scored in each of his first two competitive games since joining Fulham from Real Madrid but found Sunderland’s rearguard difficult to decode. Yet Le Bris, perhaps sensing that the visitors were gaining the initiative, made a double substitution.

On came Diarra and Isidor for the largely ineffective Nilson Angulo and Brian Brobbey. Within minutes Sunderland should have been ahead after Enzo Le Fée played a beautiful first-time ball across goal.

It seemed easier for the onrushing Isidor to score than miss, but somehow he ended up striking the base of a post and Le Bris ended up sinking to his knees in disappointment.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Poor Isidor looked mortified but redemption beckoned. Moments later he surged on to another fabulous delivery across the box – from Diarra this time – and atonement arrived as his high-velocity incisive shot whizzed past Leno.

Diarra and Isidor had succeeded in breathing new life into Sunderland – not to mention capitalising on Fulham’s high defensive line – but the former’s cameo proved short-lived as an injury necessitated his replacement by Chris Rigg.

No matter: Diarra, like Isidor, had already done just enough.

Sports.title: Calvert-Lewin cancels out Schade’s opener as Leeds salvage point against Brentford
Sports.content:
Leeds and Brentford continued their unbeaten starts to the Premier League season with a draw that had enough moments to suggest both can be optimistic about what lies ahead.

Both sides won on the opening weekend, albeit in differing circumstances. Leeds crafted a hard-earned win at Nottingham Forest while Brentford were outstanding in dismantling Tottenham. They cancelled one another out in a quintessential game of two halves at Elland Road, in which both managers will probably see plenty of positives.

Kevin Schade’s wonderful finish for the visitors as half-time approached was the least that Keith Andrews’s side deserved by that stage after comprehensively outplaying Leeds. Andrews himself deserved immense credit for producing the tactical lineup that unpicked the hosts’ back five but Daniel Farke himself responded at the interval.

The German reverted to a back four to match Brentford’s shape and it worked. Leeds – in particular Ao Tanaka and Lukas Nmecha, both on as substitutes – were hugely influential in turning round the fortunes of the hosts and they got a deserved equaliser with 11 minutes remaining, as Dominic Calvert-Lewin turned home a Nmecha cross.

On the balance of play, it was the right result. But Brentford may have felt they should have been further ahead before half-time after dominating Leeds for almost all of the opening 45 minutes. James Trafford was called upon multiple times in that first half, denying Schade and Igor Thiago with smart reaction saves.

View image in fullscreen Kevin Schade stretches to reach Keane Lewis-Potter’s cross and flicks the ball home with the outside of his boot. Photograph: Molly Darlington/Getty Images

Leeds were struggling to play through Brentford and resorted to going long to Calvert-Lewin, who was having little joy. It was ultimately no surprise when Brentford did go ahead as Schade’s clever flick turned home a Keane Lewis-Potter cross. The hosts were booed off at the interval, but Farke responded.

His switch to a back five last November against Manchester City ultimately transformed Leeds’s season and his tactical flexibility paid dividends again here. Leeds went to a 4-2-3-1 and were almost instantly the better side with parity in midfield. James Justin forced a save from Caoimhin Kelleher before Dan James then came close on the break.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

With the Elland Road crowd now alive, the equaliser felt inevitable. That moment arrived as James and Nmecha combined, and Calvert-Lewin prodded home to ensure the spoils were shared.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Shankland on the spot to ease pressure on McInnes and Rangers
Sports.content:
Lawrence Shankland’s second-half penalty gave Derek McInnes and Rangers some much-needed respite with a 1-0 win against Aberdeen at Pittodrie.

The tale since the Rangers manager arrived from Hearts in the summer has been one of constant change in formation and personnel amid exits from two European competitions and a poor start to the Premiership campaign. The Ibrox side turned in a better performance than many of late and in the 69th minute the captain, Shankland, a former Don, converted a spot-kick won by Djeidi Gassama.

The Aberdeen captain, Kevin Nisbet, had the ball in the Rangers net in the 81st minute but was judged to have pushed the full-back Dujon Sterling and the goal was ruled out.

McInnes has brought in 12 players including Kim Min-su, the 20-year-old South Korean winger signed from Girona on a four-year deal for a reported fee of about £8.5m, and who performed well on debut before he was replaced in the second half. Progress is proving frustratingly slow for their fans but three hard-fought points will bring some positivity to Ibrox.

“Probably for the first time this season, I’ve really enjoyed watching the team,” said McInnes. “There’s been moments of enjoyment. There’s been a couple of wins and some passages of play, but we know when you come here you can’t be sparkling for 90 minutes but you need to compete, and you need to bring quality, and I thought we did all that in abundance today.

View image in fullscreen Derek McInnes congratulates Ben Godfrey after the final whistle. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

“Strong performance, deserved win. I thought we were good in the game. I thought we looked like a team, a sense of the team that I would like us to be. I think the added bit of quality from Min-su at the top of the pitch was much needed. We’ve been looking for that for a while now, so it’s great that we managed to get him in. Any sort of win today was vitally important for obvious reasons. So the fact of the matter is we’ve won a tough away game, and deservedly so.”

The debutant Jardell Kanga scored a stoppage-time equaliser to earn Motherwell a 3-3 draw with St Mirren in a pulsating clash in Paisley. Goals from Tawanda Maswanhise, who also had a first-half penalty saved, and Regan Charles-Cook had the visitors in control in the early stages. Saints, though, recovered and scored three times before half-time through Paul Nsio, Declan John and Samuel Ramos to lead going into the closing stages. Motherwell had one final chance and the Swede Kanga, signed two days earlier from Finland’s Ilves, lashed a volley high into the net to snatch a point for his new side.

Hibernian secured a narrow but deserved victory over Dundee at Dens Park. Martin Boyle fired the visitors into the lead in the first half with Callum Wright doubling their advantage after the break. Dundee netted late on through Joe Westley but the Edinburgh side held on to take all three points, with the victory moving the capital club up to fifth as the hosts dropped down to fourth.

On Saturday, Camilo Durán, in his preferred position of centre-forward, scored both goals for Celtic in their 2-1 win over Falkirk. The Colombian hit two striker’s goals in the opening 29 minutes and set up several teammates for chances. Falkirk improved after the break and their ambition was rewarded by Colby Donovan’s own goal in the 72nd minute.

The win continued Celtic’s perfect start to the domestic season, but it was preceded by a display of frustration over the club’s inability to secure Champions League qualification after a four-goal aggregate lead was squandered in Thursday’s 5-1 defeat by Lask.

The Celtic ultras mocked the club board’s declaration that they aim to be “world class” in everything they do with banners listing the teams who have beaten Celtic in the Champions League qualifiers in the past 14 years, below one that read “‘world class’ embarrassment”.

However, fans got behind the team throughout the afternoon and one chant of “sack the board” emanating from the standing section did not take off around the rest of Celtic Park.

View image in fullscreen Fans hold up banners with the names of teams that have eliminated Celtic from Europe. Photograph: Stuart Wallace/Shutterstock

Hearts held firm at the end of a gruelling week to close out an unconvincing 2-1 home win over St Johnstone and climb to second in the table. Buoyed by their midweek Conference League playoff triumph away to Rapid Vienna Hearts were good value for their two-goal lead after James Wilson’s early strike was followed by a second that went down as an own goal from the Saints debutant Enes Alic.

But the hosts faded after the break and they were left clinging on in the closing stages after Ruari Paton pulled one back for the visitors early in the second half.

Dundee United produced a fine performance in the absence of their manager, Jim Goodwin, as they thrashed Kilmarnock 4-0 at Rugby Park. Goodwin was admitted to hospital on Thursday and the club said on Saturday morning the 44-year-old “continues to deal with an ongoing medical matter”.

His players, under the guidance of assistant Lee Sharp, did him proud as three first-half goals helped ease them to a first Premiership victory of the campaign. United, who had not scored in their previous three games in all competitions, were three up by 41 minutes thanks to Emmanuel Agyei’s opener, Zac Sapsford’s penalty and a Will Ferry beauty.

Jesse Randall added a late fourth as Killie conceded for the 13th time in three top-flight matches to remain bottom of the table without a point.

Sports.title: ‘I’ve had a very hectic career’: Mario Balotelli on Italian football’s troubles and his future
Sports.content:
Whenever the name Mario Balotelli is brought up, particularly in Italy, the conversation is almost inevitably laced with a sense of regret. There is that lingering “What if?”, a collective sigh over a player who possessed the raw, undeniable potential to be one of the best in the world, if only things had been different.

Yet being in front of him, with a smile on his face, it becomes clear the 36-year-old striker has reached an unexpected level of wisdom and maturity, traits that shine through in his lucid analysis of Italian football’s current struggles and the vanishing street culture of the sport. As Balotelli reflects on what he would tell his adolescent self, there is also a distinct feeling that he has finally made peace with his own turbulent narrative, that he isn’t chasing the ghosts of unfulfilled expectations.

Balotelli joined Al Ittifaq in the United Arab Emirates simply to enjoy the game, to find pure joy on the pitch, and to realise a long-held family dream of playing alongside his brother, Enock Barwuah. “To tell you the truth, it was an idea that came up more or less at the last minute,” he says. “The president wanted to meet me, and we talked. The project interested me. Everyone always says: ‘You go to Dubai for the money,’ but thank God, I’m not short of that. So, money wasn’t the only goal. The project was actually nice and competitive. I grew fond of the idea and decided to give it a try.”

View image in fullscreen Mario Balotelli signed for Al-Ittifaq in January 2026 on a two-and-a-half-year contract. Photograph: Al-Ittifaq

The realities of playing in the Middle East present a stark contrast to Balotelli’s past experiences. “Infrastructure-wise, it’s very good. The stadiums are beautiful. The problem is the public: there’s no crowd, which is a bit sad,” he says. “The organisation is also lacking a bit, but I think they’ll improve on that with time. I’m talking about all the teams across the board.” On linking up with his sibling, he says: “It’s beautiful. Ever since we were little, we always said we’d play together one day. He’d always ask me: ‘If you play for Inter, Milan, or [Manchester] City, how can I play with you?’ I used to tell him that when I got older, I might play in a team of a slightly lower level and maybe they’d give us that opportunity. It’s always been a dream, and now it’s coming true.”

Despite his new surroundings, Balotelli remains acutely aware of the deep-rooted problems plaguing football back home, particularly after Italy’s failure to qualify for three successive World Cups. “The problems, in my opinion, are very simple,” he says. “I prefer to give practical explanations rather than technical ones, based on everyday life and what I see in Italy.

“When we were little, we played hours and hours of football. I remember my mum getting mad at me because I’d stay out until it was too dark to see the ball. They’d threaten you that you couldn’t go out to play the next day. Now, when I walk around cities like Brescia, though I see it in other Italian cities too, the parks are empty. There’s no one around.”

Balotelli continues: “Computers, phones, and PlayStations have ruined a lot. Above all, the parents’ mentality has changed. A seven‑year-old kid today might play football for two hours every three days. We had the same structured training sessions, plus three hours of playing at the park every day, which felt like fun but was actually extra training. I truly believe talents were born on the street and in the parks. You played a lot, learned a lot, and tested yourself against older kids. If you were good, they didn’t let you play with kids your age; they made you play with the older ones. Those were tests that served me well in the long run. Playing with people older than me has always been one of the most important things in my career.

“Today, kids are on their phones. They feel like Ronaldinho because they watch his videos. I felt like Ronaldo because I could actually pull off the same tricks at the park. It’s very different.”

Despite his pessimism over the state of Italian football, Balotelli, who earned 36 caps for the Azzurri, scoring 14 goals, remains confident of a bright future. “Yes, I think so for the upcoming generations,” he predicts. “Maybe not right away, but in the next two or three generations. It’s normal for a country to have downturns but then you bounce back. Spain, France, and Germany have all had them.”

View image in fullscreen Mario Balotelli has won 36 caps for the Italian national team – the last in September 2018 – scoring 14 goals. Photograph: Luca Bruno/AP

When it comes to the national team, it’s impossible to ignore Roberto Mancini, reappointed as head coach and someone who acted as a mentor for Balotelli, as well as a defining figure throughout his most successful years. “He texted me to wish me a happy birthday, and I joked with him, saying: ‘Look, I can still play!’” Balotelli reveals. “I’m very happy he’s back with the national team; I’m very fond of him and I wish him the best. In Italy, people tend to blame the coaches a lot but, honestly, the system should take more of the blame. It’s the truth that nobody wants to say.”

As a curious footnote, the last time Balotelli played for Italy was on 7 September 2018, against Poland in Bologna. It also happened to be Mancini’s first competitive game in his first spell in charge of the national team. So, could Balotelli play for Italy under Mancini again? “If I keep scoring, yes,” he replies emphatically.

Balotelli’s time in England remains a standout chapter in a career filled with highs and lows, especially the three years he had at Manchester City when he won the Premier League and FA Cup – under Mancini. “It remains one of the best memories of my career,” he says. “At that time, City wasn’t as renowned as it is today. We joined the team that took the first steps for City to become what it is today. That gives you a special feeling. It means a lot more, actually.”

View image in fullscreen Mario Balotelli had an eventful three years at Manchester City, where he won the Premier League and FA Cup. Photograph: Matthew Peters/Manchester United/Getty Images

As he navigates the twilight of his career, Balotelli’s focus is clear. “I’m feeling good,” he states. “I’m recovering from a slight leg issue but I’m training, and it’s going well. It’s hot, which makes it a bit difficult to give 100%, but if you pace yourself and use your head, you can manage to play quite well. The heat is definitely a drawback, however.

“On the pitch I want to play as long as I feel good. Playing is what I love doing, so as long as my body doesn’t say: ‘Enough,’ I’ll keep going. Off the pitch, once I finish my career, I definitely want to manage my businesses and focus on my kids. I’d prefer tranquillity, though. I’ve had a very hectic career, so a sedentary lifestyle wouldn’t be a bad thing.”

If Balotelli could offer one piece of advice to his 16-year-old self, what would it be? “I’d tell him not to make certain choices,” he says, “and to listen to certain people at specific times.”

Sports.title: Emiliano Martínez finally gets his Villa exit with £7.5m move to Chelsea
Sports.content:
Chelsea have completed the signing of the Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez. The 33-year-old, who has been agitating to leave Villa for the last two summers, has finally got his wish as he has moved for £7.5m, signing a three-year contract at Stamford Bridge.

Martínez, who won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina and twice secured the Yashin Trophy for the best goalkeeper, is set to displace Robert Sánchez as Chelsea’s No 1 goalkeeper.

“I’m delighted to be at this football club,” Martinez told their website. “Coming to Chelsea, for me and my family, was an easy decision to make and I’m just over the moon – I can’t wait to get started. I want to be successful here. I’m someone who wants to win at everything I do and I want to bring that here to this football club because it’s a football club that wins titles, so I think it’s a good match.

“I’m all passion and I play with my heart. I will give 100% every game, every training session to make the club, my teammates and the supporters proud.”

Martínez became the latest high-profile player to leave Villa, following Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne out of Villa Park, with Ollie Watkins also set to make an exit. The Argentinian joined Villa in 2020 and was a key player in their rise to the top table of English football, culminating in last season’s Europa League success. He had tried to leave last summer but a move never materialised and another exit attempt fell through this month when a deal with Juventus collapsed.

Villa said in a statement: “Emi joined the club from Arsenal in 2020 and has been a commanding presence in goal throughout his time at the club, which culminated in him helping Villa win the Europa League in May. He earned his first international caps while at Aston Villa, going on to win two Copa América titles and a World Cup with Argentina. He was also twice named the world’s No 1 one goalkeeper, picking up successive Yashin Trophies in 2023 and 2024 as well as two The Best Fifa Football awards.
