Sports.content: 'Disgraced and hairy... that's all your lot ever call me!': RICHARD KEYS and ANDY GRAY on fleeing bombs in Qatar, why Keys had to laser his hairy hands, the truth about his younger wife, Gray's regret, and what they think of today's pundits

Sports.title: 'Disgraced and hairy... that's all your lot ever call me!': RICHARD KEYS and ANDY GRAY on fleeing bombs in Qatar, why Keys had to laser his hairy hands, the truth about his younger wife, Gray's regret, and what they think of today's pundits
Sports.content:
‘Disgraced and hairy, that’s all your lot ever call me,’ says Richard Keys.

Instinctively, I look to his hands. Where’s the hair gone? ‘Laser,’ he answers.

What, a vanity move? ‘Yes!’ intercepts Andy Gray.

‘No, no, no,’ corrects Keys. ‘I'll tell you what it was. After so many years of putting my hand into a bowl of crisps, and everybody else taking theirs out scared, I thought, “I have to do something about this”.’

There are no crisps on our table and Keys’ smooth paws are wrapped around a glass of pink champagne. Gray lowers his flute to imitate the buzzing of the laser treatment. ‘It’s true,’ he says. ‘He was f****** frightening everybody, me included!’

An afternoon with Keys & Gray is seldom anything but entertaining.

An afternoon with Richard Keys (right) & Andy Gray (left) is seldom anything but entertaining

This is the pair's first newspaper interview since returning to Britain after 13 years with Qatar-based beIN Sports

There is 2011 and their spectacular exit from Sky. Bombs over Doha. Marriage and morality. And, above all, perception

But here, on the top floor of the OXO Tower overlooking the Thames, in their first newspaper interview since returning to Britain after 13 years with Qatar-based beIN Sports, there is serious stuff, too. There is 2011 and their spectacular exit from Sky. Bombs over Doha. Marriage and morality. And, above all, perception.

‘I genuinely don’t know what people here think of me,’ says Gray. ‘But since I’ve come back, there have been more smiles than moans.’

Later, our French waiter returns excitedly after watching Gray’s goals on his phone. It is a nice moment, and a reminder of the player before the pundit.

Keys has a bigger battle with perception. ‘Honestly - and I haven't said this to anybody - the perception of me is, “Old man who left his dying wife for his daughter's best friend”. No one's ever bothered to ask, “Is that true?”.’

Is that true? ‘Of course it isn’t,’ says the 69-year-old.

Keys and his wife of 34 years, Julia, separated in 2016. He has been with Lucie, 31 years his junior, ever since. They married in 2023. Lucie and his daughter, Jemma, were routinely described as ‘best friends’ in the media.

‘I fell in love again, totally unexpectedly,’ he begins. ‘I just got blown off my feet. It was with someone who was not my daughter's best friend but had spent time in her company.

'My wife had cancer nearly 10 years before I left home. “Recovered” is a hard word with cancer, because you’re always aware of it, but she was not dying of cancer and I’m pleased to say she is still with us and hasn’t died. So the narrative suited those that wanted to find a reason to not like me.’

‹ Slide me › Keys and Gray presented the flagship Monday Night Football show on Sky until their exit in 2011

The duo moved to Qatar to work for beIN Sports from 2013 until the end of last season

Gray, 70, has been married three times. Still time for another? ‘My wife might say there's one or two left in her, so I don't know what that means for me!’ says Gray, a father of five.

How about children? ‘I think I'll answer that honestly as well,’ says Keys. ‘I don't have the right at my time of life to say to Lucie, “You cannot be a mother”. If she said she wanted children, then I need to partake in that.’

‘You better get a move on, then,’ says Gray. ‘That is also true,’ Keys laughs. ‘I had open-heart surgery nine years ago. My surgeon said two more days and I would have been dead. So now, as our great friend Peter Reid would say, “I’m going to enjoy my life”.’

So we were only 48 hours from Gray & Gray? ‘Wouldn't that be a good day!’ says Gray. ‘Gray & Gray. I like that.’

The truth is, he wouldn’t. They have been a double act for more than three decades and the future is Keys & Gray Unleashed, a podcast launched this month and already making headlines. They had Match of the Day in their crosshairs this week, Harry Redknapp the week before.

What was all that about? ‘I think Richard teased it by saying we could have gone to jail because of what happened,’ says Gray. ‘But you’ll have to wait for the full story.’

Keys disagrees: ‘Harry put us in a very difficult situation. We were confronted with a problem that we didn't want and had not created. Whether with malice or not, we don't know. But if you put together the different component parts, he was under a bit of pressure himself at the time, facing court action…’ Gray’s stare wins and Keys trails off.

‘I'm told he's bemused by what the problem is,’ says Keys. ‘One day, I hope to be able to tell him.’

Gray, 70, has been married three times. Still time for another? ‘My wife might say there's one or two left in her, so I don't know what that means for me!’

Keys, 69, marries Lucie, 31 years his junior, in Devon in 2023

Gray with Rachel Lewis, his third wife, in 2019

There is so much of their past still to pick through, we should not lose sight of the present. Why exactly are they here? They were the face of beIN’s Premier League coverage and, unlike Sky Sports, the parting was not hostile. The hostilities were happening outside.

‘I hit the wall about a year ago,’ says Keys. ‘I'd run out of steam when it came to match time. And the game, I hate to say, is not as enjoyable as it could be. And yes, the bombs were unsettling. What Andy Burnham did with the wildfire alert, we were getting that four times a night. We s*** ourselves.’

Gray takes over: ‘I was on my terrace one night. The next minute there's four streaks of light across the sky. Then, there's another four coming from the US airbase, taking them out. They exploded right above me. You think, “hmmm”.’

‘We were living and working in a war zone,’ says Keys. ‘We later led the chaps back into the studio after we were forced off air for a period. We presented, listening to missiles being blown up above us.

‘When I later got the first flight out… the delay at the terminal, leaving the gate, then at the end of the runway. You just think, “Get this f***ing thing on the move”. The relief when it did, I cannot describe.’

Keys wants to be in London now, living permanently at his West Kensington home with Lucie, who is a lawyer. He also wants to wear a blue cap and white trainers. ‘This is me now. I’ve been in a suit for 40 years.’

Television, insists Keys, is over. With Gray, though, you detect regret that his departure from Sky took him away from his favourite domain beyond the penalty box – the commentary box.

‘I'd like to think, somewhere, I could do a bit of commentary,’ he says. ‘Not television, maybe, but radio. Just to see what it feels like again. I would like that.’

With Gray, you detect regret that his departure from Sky took him away from his favourite domain beyond the penalty box - the commentary box

Keys wants to be in London now, living permanently at his West Kensington home with Lucie, who is a lawyer

Keys turns towards Gray: ‘I would be happy for you if that happened. I think you deserve it. I’ve had my moment and I'll still be talking football. But to hear him back, analysing a football match, that would be special. He’s the best I’ve ever known.’

Keys is warming to his theme now. ‘He means the world to me. What happened in 2011 brought us together in a way I did not expect. I remember saying to him, now more than ever we need to be together, because they were trying to divide us - and then we are weaker. He has trusted me implicitly with everything we've done ever since.’

So, 2011. Gray was sacked after an off-air conversation between the pair was leaked to the press in which they questioned whether female assistant referee Sian Massey understood the offside rule. Keys resigned soon after as further off-air footage emerged, including his infamous ‘Did you smash it?’ remark about Jamie Redknapp’s love life.

‘I could never defend it and never pretend it's not unpalatable,’ says Keys of the Massey incident. ‘I fully accept the responsibility for my part and he does his. It should not have happened.

‘But at the time, it was a smaller part of a bigger picture. Rupert Murdoch was trying to buy all of Sky. I’m told that Jeremy Hunt, the culture secretary, had said it would help if Sky News could prove they were an independent operator.

‘What better way to do that than fry your own? So, these two f****ers that work for Sky, it was open season on us in the media.’

Gray says: ‘I can’t imagine saying today what I said then, I just can’t. I think we were two of the first people ever cancelled. I had 20 reporters outside my house for weeks.’

Keys apologised to Massey at the time and she accepted it. In 2022, Gray found himself spending seven hours on a flight with her.

Keys watches on from the Sky Sports studio in 2011 at Molineux, where leaked audio of his and Gray's discussion of assistant referee Sian Massey led to their exit from Sky

Keys later apologised to Massey, who retired this summer

‘We chatted and I gave her my number and offered to help her with anything in Doha. It was nice.’

Keys says: ’Sian was brilliant with us. She messaged me that day and said, “You’ll never guess who I’m sitting in front of on the plane?”. I replied, “Does that make you offside?”.’ A bad dad joke, perhaps, but not one for which Keys should be cancelled this time.

‘I've taken a black-and-blue kicking, I promise you. Andy knows that. He’s lived with me through it. But if my wife thought I was the person described in the media, she wouldn't be with me.

‘So to be back here, this is liberating. I've been staggered by the reaction and enormously grateful, because the majority of people are saying, “It's good to have you boys back”. That’s touching. I have been beaten up. I've been kicked from pillar to post for a long time.’

It is a rare glimpse of his vulnerability. 'Everyone thinks I've the skin of a rhino...' he says.

The sun is setting beyond the capital’s skyline and it feels like a good time to pivot to some lighter conversation. This is my quick-fire round, much like Keys when it comes to ordering champagne.

One presenter, three pundits. Who are you watching?

‘Graeme Souness, Glenn Hoddle,’ starts Keys. ‘And Lianne Sanderson. She’s funny and knows football. I don’t want to sit and listen to guffawing buffoons. I can go to the pub for that. Frank Lampard is also brilliant and we like Alan (Shearer), he’s just a good lad. But those are my three. As for a presenter, Kelly (Cates) is very good. I'm proud to say that I helped her when she started.’

Both Keys and Gray list Graeme Souness (left) and Glenn Hoddle (right) among their favourite pundits on TV today

Kelly Cates (right), who presents on Sky and Match of the Day, is also a Keys favourite

Gray picks the same three but swaps Cates for Laura Woods. OK, which lineup would make you change the channel?

‘Oh no, I'm not answering that,’ says Gray. ‘He will!’

‘I have a deep affection and exchange messages with Phil Neville,’ says Keys. ‘I like Phil Neville.’

‘No,’ says Gray. ‘We want to know who you'd turn off.’

‘I've just answered the question,’ says Keys. He does later concede admiration for Gary Neville and the way he has impacted punditry.

What about Roy Keane? ‘Keane is a little like Graeme (Souness),’ says Keys. ‘He can say things that grab your attention. What I had to say to Graeme at one point was, “You now need to start watching football. You're only going to get so far with the story of being at the front of the line and looking behind for warriors”. And we love Graeme dearly.

‘But if I wanted to know about a football match and have someone tell me something different, it wouldn't be Keane. I think he's ideal for the modern world. He will give you something you're going to bite on.’

The rest of the world certainly bit when Keys recently revealed that he once spent Christmas Day alone with a can of tuna, a bottle of champagne and watched The Great Escape, Where Eagles Dare and The Guns of Navarone back to back.

'Roy Keane is a little like Graeme,’ says Keys. ‘He can say things that grab your attention'

'If I wanted to know about a football match and have someone tell me something different, it wouldn't be Keane. I think he's ideal for the modern world'

We turn the question on Gray – what would his Christmas Day alone look like? ‘I wake up and straight away I’d have smoked salmon chopped into scrambled eggs.’ Keys interrupts: ‘Andy, it’s just a quick question - food and three films.’

‘You’ve spoken for long enough,’ Gray shoots back. ‘I’ll continue. So, I’d go downstairs for a glass of champagne. Then, it would be a traditional dinner, the whole works. For dessert, apple crumble and custard. Then to the sofa, with a glass, to watch The Great Escape, The Bridge on the River Kwai and 633 Squadron.’ What’s the last one? ‘You’ve never seen it?’ says Gray, incredulous. No, I was born in 1982.

‘It’s like the Dam Busters, but the target is more difficult,’ he explains. ‘They fly in low and have to go up a mountain and drop a bomb so it hits where the German cannons are. Ah, it’s brilliant.’ Keys cannot resist: ‘Wait a minute, Andy. We’ll get a monitor and tactics board so you can explain this one in more detail…’

For two fellas who came home partly because they'd had enough of bombs over Doha, their choice of films is somewhat ironic.

Next. If you could take one moment from your career with you? ‘Bayern Munich. Goodison Park. 1985. All day long. Thank you. Good night,’ says Gray.

Keys does not hesitate, either: ‘Kevin Keegan has obviously been on my mind recently. I was fortunate to be part of his “I would love it” tirade, asking the questions. I just knew he had something to say and the producer was in my ear telling me to leave him alone. What he then said will always be remembered.

‘When Kevin came to Qatar we only ever called him King Kev, everywhere we went. So yeah, that moment, because it was the gateway to someone who was very special to me.’

Finally, how would you like to be remembered? ‘I would just like to be remembered!’ says Gray. ‘But I don’t know. As a good lad who was good fun to be with and was decent.’

If you could take one moment from your career with you? ‘Bayern Munich. Goodison Park. 1985. All day long. Thank you. Good night,’ says Gray, pictured right scoring that night

‘When Kevin (Keegan) came to Qatar we only ever called him King Kev, everywhere we went'

'I don't think people know me in a way I would have wished,' says Keys, while Gray adds: 'I would just like to be remembered!'

Keys, inevitably, has more to say: ‘In a manner that is different to the way I'm perceived now. I don't think people know me in a way I would have wished. There's a lot of good things I've done, in broadcasting and away from it, that have been scrubbed or ignored. And it does, if I'm by the Thames with a glass or two, yeah, it hurts.

‘I’ve probably accepted that won’t change. So when the likes of Andy and Souness - and they’ve worked with everyone - say what they do about me, that means a lot. I bow to that and say, “Thank you”.’

Thirteen years away has changed plenty. The hairy hands have gone. The suits, too. And so, in time, they hope will some of the old perceptions.

Keys & Gray, however, remain very much Keys & Gray. An afternoon in their company is seldom anything but entertaining.

Sports.title: Fulham say yes to Everton over £9.4m deal for Kenny Tete as Spurs agree fee for Iliman Ndiaye, Jesus is set for Barca... and Villa close on Harwood-Bellis transfer: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
There are just three days left of the transfer window and it's sure to be busy as several clubs look to make big signings before 11pm on Tuesday. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... Liverpool eye Genk stopper Liverpool are among clubs monitoring highly rated Genk goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans. The 18-year-old is a player Liverpool are interested in but so are Real Madrid. The teenager is a Belgium U19 international and at 6ft 7ins tall he has drawn comparisons already with Madrid’s number one Thibaut Courtois and it is anticipated he will follow suit by moving to the Bernabeu. Liverpool are aware of his situation but there are no guarantees he will be moving to Anfield this window. Juve make Sarr offer Juventus have offered a £1.7m loan fee for Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr. The deal would become permanent for £23million if Juventus qualify for the Champions League. Villa to wrap up Harwood-Bellis deal Aston Villa are finalising a £30m package with Southampton to sign centre back Taylor Harwood-Bellis. Talks are ongoing but the fee is £25m plus £5m in add-ons. Villa are set to bring in English centre back Taylor Harwood-Bellis from Southampton Jesus heads to Barca Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus is set for a late move to Barcelona, who are closing in on a cut-price deal worth around £8.6m. Jesus was left out of the Arsenal squad for their first two games this season and has been training away from the first team. Arsenal midfielder Fabio Vieira is set to move to Hamburg on a permanent deal. The 26-year-old spent last season on loan at the German club and the clubs have agreed a £7.4m deal. For more on this story click HERE Tete's set to be a Toffee Everton have agreed a £9.4m deal with Fulham to sign Kenny Tete. David Moyes wanted to sign him when his contract was expiring at Fulham last summer and came close, but Tete got an improved deal and stayed. Moyes has been wanting to sign a right-back as a matter of priority before the window ends on Tuesday and had narrowed a list down to two with Nottingham Forest’s Ola Aina. Fulham are in talks to sign Rayo Vallacano's Andrei Ratiu as a new right-back. Kenny Tete is heading to Hill Dickinson Stadium Foxes' Hamza on verge of Blades move Leicester City midfielder Hamza Choudhury is having a medical at Sheffield United. The Blades stepped in for the 28-year-old Bangladesh international as he was on his way to Derby County after the clubs agreed a deal. However, a late bid from Sheffield United has resulted in Choudhury choosing to return to the Blades. Coventry land City's Mfuni Coventry City have signed Stephen Mfuni on a season-long loan from Manchester City. The 18-year-old, who can play at left-back and centre-back, made his senior Man City debut last season in the 10-1 victory over Exeter City in the Emirates FA Cup. Mfuni said: “I feel blessed to be here, it’s exciting. These are moments you dream of and to do it with such a good team and a good squad, I’m looking forward to it. 'I spoke to the gaffer, he wants me to show what I normally do on the pitch, whether I’m at left-back or centre-back, and for me to keep being me and do what I do.’ Stephen Mfuni has joined promoted Coventry on a season's loan Brentford in for Larsson Brentford are talking over a deal for Eintracht Frankfurt midfielder Hugo Larsson, who has also been targeted by other Premier League clubs. Collyer heads to West Brom Manchester United midfielder Toby Collyer has joined West Bromwich Albion for £3m, potentially rising to £7.6m. United also inserted a 40 percent sell-on clause. Sports.title: England second Test ratings: Seamers shine once again in big Lord's victory... but for which player is the jury still out?
Sports.content:
England second Test ratings: Who has a lot to prove? Which star is struggling to find a solution? And who quietened the debate about his future?

England completed a crushing 194-run victory over Pakistan at Lord's on Sunday and took the three-match series with one game to spare.

Here, Lawrence Booth runs the rule over their display...

Ben Duckett: 3/10

Trapped lbw once more by Mohammad Abbas, then chipped tamely to mid-off. His average, just under 39, is at its lowest for three and a half years.

Emilio Gay: 5/10

Strangled down leg in the first innings, he battled hard in tough conditions on the second evening, only to be undone by a grubber once play restarted on the third afternoon. The jury remains out.

The jury remains out on Emilio Gay who has now played five Tests for England and averages 23

Jordan Cox: 7.5/10

Looked the classiest player on either side while making a patient half-century on the first day, confirming the view that he must keep his place when Jacob Bethell returns. An asset at third slip.

Joe Root: 4/10

Has grown in stature off the field over the past fortnight, but can’t avoid falling lbw, whether or not the wicketkeeper is up to the stumps. Has now been dismissed that way in nine of his last 12 Test innings, with no solution in sight.

Harry Brook: 6/10

Did his best to overcome the conditions, and fought especially hard on the third afternoon, but – like Root – he still looks shackled when the wicketkeeper comes up to the stumps.

Dan Lawrence: 7/10

Did his long-term prospects no harm with an intelligent half-century between the showers on the third day. His run-out on the first day was less smart.

Dan Lawrence showed his class at No6 on a tricky pitch in the second innings

Jamie Smith: 7.5/10

Helped dig England out of a hole on the first day, kept well – both up to the stumps and back – and lost his wicket trying to force his pace on the third. Quietened the debate about his future.

Gus Atkinson: 6/10

Deserved better than to go wicketless, but there’s no doubt he poses less of a regular threat now that he has been elbowed away from the new ball. Batted well for 45 to give England a match-winning buffer.

Ollie Robinson: 9/10

Unplayable at times, nipping the ball both ways at going at less than one and a half an over. Of his type, and on his day, he is among the best in the world.

Ollie Robinson was England's star man with the ball again and is enjoying a super summer

Jofra Archer: 8/10

Bowled as fast as he did in his 2019 pomp, and in another game might have doubled his match haul of five wickets. Brutally bounced out Babar Azam in the second innings.

Josh Tongue: 7.5/10

Worked over Babar brilliantly in the first innings, and was used as the battering ram to bounce out Shakeel in the second. Also made 42 runs for once out from No 11.

Pakistan: Shan Masood 5, Azan Awais 6, Abdullah Shafique 1, Babar Azam 2, Saud Shakeel 7.5, Mohammad Rizwan 5, Ali Usman 5, Khurram Shahzad 4, Mohammad Abbas 8.5, Mohammad Ali 6, Imam-ul-Haq 0.

Sports.title: Leeds 1-1 Brentford: Daniel Farke praises side's 'never-say-die' attitude after Dominic Calvert-Lewin snatches a late point against red-hot Bees
Sports.content:
Leeds 1-1 Brentford: Daniel Farke praises side's 'never-say-die' attitude after Dominic Calvert-Lewin snatches a late point against red-hot Bees

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

There has been plenty of hype surrounding Leeds this summer after some big-money signings and a stadium redevelopment which is now underway.

But they needed a late equaliser from Dominic Calvert-Lewin to salvage a point against an upwardly mobile Brentford side who outplayed their hosts comprehensively during the first half.

Keith Andrews' dashing men in black threatened to run amok but Kevin Schade's delightful 41st-minute strike was their only reward before the interval.

There was even a smattering of boos from the home stands but Daniel Farke boldly changed formation at the break – switching from his customary back three to a flat back four – and Leeds improved markedly as the second half unfolded.

With eleven minutes remaining, Calvert-Lewin fired home from close range to leave both managers satisfied at maintaining their respective unbeaten starts to the season.

Leeds boss Farke, who handed home debuts to James Trafford, Tarik Muharemovic, Nico Elvedi and Harry Wilson, said: 'I'm very proud of my boys for their reaction in the second half.

Leeds and Brentford shared the spoils - Kevin Schade put the visitors ahead with a great strike

Calvert-Lewin bundles the ball home 11 minutes from time to ensure Leeds got on level terms

'After back-to-back wins at Nottingham Forest in the league and Carabao Cup, everyone was excited.

'But we were up against a red-hot, in-form Brentford side who showed so much quality in the first half.

'I asked a lot of my players because we changed formation at half-time but we didn't crumble – we showed a never-say-die attitude and got our rewards.'

Brentford, still bubbling from their opening-day 3-0 win over Tottenham and 6-1 victory at Birmingham in the Carabao Cup, had Leeds on the ropes during the first half.

The Whites were not helped by the loss of defender Joe Rodon to a hamstring injury and Brentford led when Schade provided a deft touch to dispatch Keane Lewis-Potter's left-wing cross.

But the switch to a back four – and second-half introduction of Ao Tanaka, Wilson, Dan James and Lucas Nmecha – saw Leeds gradually ask questions of an impressive Bees backline.

The pressure told when Nmecha's low right-wing cross was fired in by Calvert-Lewin to deny Brentford victory.

Andrews reflected: 'We could have tested Trafford a bit more with the territory and control that we had in the first half.

Daniel Farke praised his team's 'never-say-die attitude' to continue their unbeaten start to the season, a record also held by Brentford

'We became a little bit content with being in their final third without really putting the knife in.

'The storm was always going to come – Daniel made changes at half-time – and it's not easy when the crowd get going here.

'It's an amazing place to play and always a spicy atmosphere which I really love but you've got to be ready for every punch that gets thrown at you.'

Brentford had 22 shots – five on target which saw Trafford make some decent saves – and always held a lingering threat through Igor Thiago.

They were denied a penalty midway through the second half when Jayden Bogle appeared to foul Schade inside the 18-yard box.

Andrews said: 'The fact I've been asked about this a few times would suggest there's something in that.'

The Bees finished ninth last term, and Leeds 14th, but some ambitious recruitment has both clubs well placed to kick on again this season.

Andrews spoke of a new-found confidence in his team's attacking ambition and admitted to a slight disappointment at not taking all three points.

Leeds, meanwhile, are trying to add to their squad before the window closes.

Nmecha and Calvert-Lewin – who combined to deadly effect for Leeds' equaliser – both arrived on free transfers last summer and Farke is continuing to scour the market for reinforcements.

He added: 'I'm very happy with the players I've got but it's not the biggest group and one or two more additions would definitely be helpful.'

Sports.title: Gianni's grounded! Mystery as Infantino cancels New York trip to address Wall Street billionaires... just days after INSIDE SPORT revealed how embattled FIFA president had been clocking up the air miles in bid to save his job
Sports.content:
Gianni's grounded! Mystery as Infantino cancels New York trip to address Wall Street billionaires... just days after INSIDE SPORT revealed how embattled FIFA president had been clocking up the air miles in bid to save his job

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Gianni Infantino's gargantuan carbon footprint came to a mysterious, temporary halt over the weekend.

Last week, Inside Sport revealed how the FIFA president had been clocking up the air miles at a staggering rate as he continues to attempt to save his job in the wake of the World Cup sell-off scandal.

Infantino was due to rub shoulders with US senators and Wall Street billionaires at a Milken Institute event in the Hamptons, outside New York, on Friday night.

But his Qatari-funded private jet stayed on the tarmac in Doha, where he has a home, after he cancelled plans to speak at the exclusive gathering.

Gianno Infantino has been fighting to save his job after the World Cup sell-off scandal

The day before, UEFA filed court papers in several US states seeking documents it believes could support a prosecution for criminal mismanagement in Switzerland over Infantino’s failed plot to flog stakes in the World Cup.

Mystery also surrounds the jet’s movements earlier in the week. On Tuesday it flew from Paris, where Infantino had attended the Esports World Cup, to Majorca for a matter of hours, then on to Pisa for roughly seven more before carrying him to Hanoi for the ASEAN Cup final.

While Inside Sport would not want to make any assumptions, it is interesting to note that Josh Kushner, the brother of president Donald Trump’s son-in-law heavily implicated in the scandal, has holidayed there in the past.

...as Olympic Movement despairs over his sell-off plan

Qatar appears to be treading a fine line – balancing support for Infantino with an attempt to curry favour with the IOC to host the 2036 Olympics. That said, most of the Olympic world is not opposed to the notion of selling off shares in competitions to private equity firms as, unlike FIFA, other international federations need the cash. However, there is uniform disapproval across the Olympic Movement at the lack of transparency and governance in the way Infantino introduced the plan.

Football unites to pay tribute to fallen officers

Tributes were paid at Premier League matches on Sunday to the two police officers killed in Middlesbrough.

The match officials at Leeds v Brentford wore back armbands with referee Tony Harrington a friend of PC Matthew Blades, who died along with PC Tom Clough, when their vehicle was hit by a car driving the wrong way down the road. Over the Pennines at Old Trafford, PC Blades’ two children were mascots at Manchester United’s clash with Ipswich Town.

PC Blades was a keen United supporter. Meanwhile, on Friday United unveiled a platform at their ground in tribute to Chas Banks MBE, the former secretary of the club’s disabled supporters' association who passed away in 2024. Banks was a strong voice for those who often needed one, and the platform – in the Stretford End – is a fitting tribute.

All eyes on Margot and Bradley

While the great and good of European football descended on Monaco last week for the Champions League draw, many eyes in the principality were elsewhere. Hollywood big-hitters Bradley Cooper and Margot Robbie were in town to shoot scenes for an Ocean’s Eleven prequel.

Part of the story is set against the backdrop of the 1962 Grand Prix, with the famous circuit taken back 60 years thanks to the arrival of replica vintage cars from the era.

Margot Robbie is filming a prequel to Ocean's Eleven with Bradley Cooper

Cricket comms chief departs a year before Ashes

Eyebrows have been raised at the recent departure of popular England cricket men’s team head of comms Danny Reuben after 10 years in the role. Inside Sport has previously reported that the Yorkshireman has admirers within the Australian set-up. One to watch ahead of the next Ashes.

Trapeze-y does it as UEFA keep costs down

The traditional after-draw party usually features the opening of the roof at the Monte-Carlo Sporting centre, so guests from the continent’s elite can enjoy a no-expenses-spared light show.

This year, however, the roof remained closed with a pair of trapeze artists dressed as human disco balls the main entertainment at the UEFA event.

Some wondered, with FIFA under fire for its apparent obsession with money, if its European rivals had toned it down on purpose.

Sports.title: Dignity in the face of tragedy: Sons of A66 victim PC Matthew Blades walk out as mascots for Manchester United as they take on Ipswich Town
Sports.content:
The two sons of a police officer killed in the A66 crash led out the Manchester United team as mascots for today's Premier League match against Ipswich Town.

PCs Matthew Blades, 37, and Tom Clough, 38, died alongside five young occupants of a VW Passat that was travelling on the wrong side of a dual carriageway in the early hours of Saturday, August 22.

PC Blades was described as a 'proud Red' by United, having been a regular at Old Trafford.

In a tribute in their programme, the club said: 'Matthew was a proud Red, a devoted family man and a police officer who dedicated his life to helping others.'

His widow Sarah attended today's game alongside their children, who led out the team as mascots in honour of their father.

The eldest child was walked out by Bruno Fernandes, captain of Manchester United, while the youngest was led by goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

It followed a minute's applause in memory of PC Blades and PC Clough yesterday before Middlesbrough's Championship encounter with West Brom at Riverside Stadium.

Mourners also gathered to pay their respects at Seaton Carew FC's game against FC Hartlepool - with PC Blades a former junior football coach at both teams.

The two sons of a police officer killed in the A66 crash led out the Manchester United team as mascots for today's Premier League match against Ipswich Town

Bruno Fernandes, captain of Manchester United, led out PC Blades's eldest child

The youngest child (right) was walked out by goalkeeper Senne Lammens

PCs Matthew Blades with his two children and a Manchester mascot

PC Blades, 37, was killed when his police vehicle was struck by a Volkswagen Passat travelling the wrong way down the A66 near Middlesbrough

PC Tom Clough, 38, also died in the crash, which occurred around 10 seconds after a police pursuit of the Volkswagen was called off

The club paid a long and moving tribute to PC Blades in their programme, in which they said: 'It is with great sadness that Manchester United learned of the death of PC Matthew Blades and his colleague PC Tom Clough in an accident near Middlesbrough last weekend.

'For Matt, some of his happiest times were spent watching United with his boys. His wife Sarah and two children will be at today's game, with his sons leading out the Reds as mascots.'

They added that a friend and colleague of PC Blades sent them a tribute, which read: 'For Matthew, United was a lifelong love, a passion he shared with his family. Since Matt's tragic death there has been an extraordinary outpouring of grief and support.

'That love has been seen in countless tributes and acts of kindness. Today, we remember a fellow Red. A husband. A father. A son. A brother. A friend. A police officer. A man who gave his life in the service of others. Forever our superhero.'

Middlesbrough and County Durham have been gripped by a wave of violence since the crash, which has left some residents too intimidated to leave their homes.

Theo Rae, 17, Cole Worthy, 17, Michael Cahill, 23, Jakub Matusiak, 23, and Makai Saddington, 18, were driving in the Passat and all lost their lives in the smash.

Four of the five youths had previous criminal convictions, and were believed to be associated with another car which was seen ramming properties on the morning of the crash.

Police are investigating whether the spate of violence, including the fatal A66 crash, is linked to organised crime.

Middlesbrough, which has the highest crime rate in England bar central London, was rocked again when a seven-year-old girl, Valentina Foster, and her aunt, Natalie McDonald, 34, died in a house fire. Two men were arrested on suspicion of murder.

Although police did not link the blaze to the A66 crash, they did not rule out a connection to wider organised crime.

Barely 24 hours later, armed police were responding to another serious incident in Middlesbrough, with claims of a machete attack that left a man with stab wounds.

Makai Saddington, one of the five killed in the Volkswagen, posted videos on TikTok of him being chased by police and was awaiting trial for racially abusing and assaulting officers

Jakub Matusiak, another occupant of the car which hit the officers, also posted videos of himself driving recklessly

Close friends Theo Rae (left) and Cole Robert Worthy both died in the crash on Saturday

Michael Robert Cahill was one of the five in the VW Passat

Seven more men were later held as part of a broader operation to disrupt organised crime, taking the total number of arrests to 24.

Police in Middlesbrough had five pleas for help ignored by the Government before an outbreak of gang violence which led to the fatal A66 crash.

Matt Storey, Cleveland's police and crime commissioner, had written at least seven letters to the Government since July 2024 warning that officers were 'woefully underfunded' and struggling to protect the public.

Only two received a response, his office said, while more requests for additional support were ignored.

The most recent warning, sent to Andy Burnham last month, said shrinking recruitment was driving 'concern about whether help will be there when it is needed most'.

Cleveland police was forced to call in 200 officers from nearby regions last week after the crash.

Sports.title: Chelsea MUST tighten up their defence if they want to mount a title charge - Xabi Alonso cannot rely on outscoring the opposition every week, writes KIERAN GILL
Sports.content:
Chelsea MUST tighten up their defence if they want to mount a title charge - Xabi Alonso cannot rely on outscoring the opposition every week, writes KIERAN GILL

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Leading 3-0 after 32 minutes, the conversations were inevitable. About Chelsea as surprise title contenders. About Arsenal being worried. About everyone else in the Premier League inheriting a problem with the arrival of Xabi Alonso as a manager.

What Chelsea can offer in front of goal is frightening good. Whether you prefer ‘JPMorgan’ as a nickname or ‘CPR’, in Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers, they have an attacking trident worthy of title talk. It is as elite as any other in England, maybe even Europe, arguably up there with those boasted by Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich.

Entertaining as it is to watch, however, Chelsea cannot rely on outscoring the opposition every week in order to challenge at the very top. Control tends to trump chaos when it comes to crowning champions, and what followed after Chelsea stormed into their 3-0 lead told us why we are right to have reservations about a sudden charge.

First, how they secured such a lead.

Chelsea’s opening goal came from a corner which was fumbled by Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen and tapped in by Romeo Lavia, but Alonso immediately turned to congratulate his new set-piece specialist Austin MacPhee for how he set it up.

Their second arrived after Jorrel Hato’s throw-in was flicked on by Joao Pedro for Rogers. Out of nowhere, Pedro Neto burst into the box to bury his team-mate’s pass with perfect timing.

Their third was the consequence of a clever turn and pass from Rogers in his own half as Hato flew forward down the left-hand side, his speed and the accuracy of his pass inside setting up Joao Pedro.

Chelsea bared their teeth against Brighton to score four goals - but they were leaky at the back

The Blues cannot simply rely on outscoring the opposition every match if they want to be serious title contenders

The Brazilian did not quite copy Emmanuel Adebayor, whose celebration in front of the Arsenal end after scoring for Manchester City in 2009 went down in Premier League folklore, but he made a point of positioning himself in front of the Brighton fans. They had been taunting their former player all afternoon. He was within his rights to respond.

The fast and furious nature of Chelsea’s third goal arguably summer up Alonso’s approach. They finished this match with only 25.6 per cent possession, having managed only 38.1 per cent at Fulham. From back to front in three passes, Chelsea were coasting, three goals to the good.

However, it is at the other end of the pitch where pressing questions have to be asked.

Chelsea have tried to help correct those problems at the back by bringing in Emiliano Martinez for £7.5million from Aston Villa, and he is an upgrade on Robert Sanchez.

It was Sanchez’s performance at Fulham in the Premier League’s opening weekend which forced Chelsea into this rethink after a summer spent insisting they were not in the market for goalkeepers. It was painfully obvious they would not stand a chance of rivalling Arsenal if they stood by their 28-year-old Spaniard. It was not only the two avoidable goals he conceded in that 3-2 victory. Sanchez even dribbled the ball out of play for a corner at one stage.

Chelsea rushed through the signing of Martinez. The goalkeeper, who turns 34 in the next week, had to be registered before Friday 12pm in order to be eligible to face Brighton. He was officially announced on Sunday morning, then started in the afternoon, with 21-year-old Mike Penders on the substitutes’ bench and Sanchez informed how he is up for sale.

Martinez performed well overall, particularly considering this was his first appearance since the World Cup final six weeks ago, which Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain. Yet Chelsea’s defence was unable to cope with the pressure applied by Brighton.

The visitors’ first goal was from a counter-attack which Neto should have killed early on when the ball was there to be won. Martinez initially stopped Charalampos Kostoulas, but Malick Yalcoule volleyed in the rebound, with a little luck involved as it smacked the woodwork on its way in.

Xabi Alonso is toasting two wins from two in the Premier League after also beating Fulham

Their front three of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro, and Morgan Rogers is as good as any three in the Premier League

Brighton never stopped fighting but left themselves with too much ground to make up

Their second came from a corner which was worked short. Palmer did not spy the run behind him from Pascal Gross, whose cross took a wicked deflection off Joao Pedro to beat Martinez.

Suddenly, Chelsea’s 3-0 advantage had been reduced to a marginal 3-2 lead.

It was only because of their awesome attack that Alonso’s side were able to win. Palmer’s finish was fabulous, and with that, Alonso’s technical area could no longer hold him. The Blues boss jumped out of his box and into the air while pumping his fists toward the fans.

England manager Thomas Tuchel was sat next to Brazil boss Carlo Ancelotti in the stands of Stamford Bridge. They may as well have had a conversation about their regretful summers, after leaving Palmer and Joao Pedro at home for the World Cup.

Palmer’s strike gave Chelsea enough daylight that Brighton’s stoppage-time header from Gross was merely a consolation, after Moises Caicedo needed to be substituted injured and with Enzo Fernandez yet again missing amid Manchester City’s circling. Midfield will be a particular area worth watching in the build-up to deadline day.

Stamford Bridge's Shed End unveiled a ‘Not too Xabi – Alonso is a Blue’ banner before kick-off. They are already captivated by their new manager.

However, if Alonso's Chelsea are to stay in this title conversation after two wins from two, they need to find a way to be as tight at the back as they are free-flowing up top.

Sports.title: Why Harry Maguire goal was allowed to stand despite refs seeing Man Utd handball
Sports.content:
Why Harry Maguire goal was allowed to stand despite refs seeing Man Utd handball

Manchester United's second goal against Ipswich Town was allowed to stand after an initial VAR check as Harry Maguire's shot found the bottom corner

View 2 Images Harry Maguire's goal for Manchester United against Ipswich Town was allowed to stand

Manchester United's second goal against Ipswich Town was allowed to stand despite the ball hitting Harry Maguire's HAND in the build-up.

‌



Maguire, 33, fired United into a 2-1 lead in the 57th minute at Old Trafford after controlling the ball on the edge of the box before drilling a low shot that was deflected home by Jacob Greaves for an own goal.

‌



However, the ball appeared to hit Maguire's hand when he won it back, leaving the Ipswich players incensed that the goal should be disallowed. But, because he is not the actual goalscorer, the goal is allowed to stand.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

If Maguire had directly benefited from the handball and been the scorer, a free-kick would have awarded to Ipswich. As he was not, United were given a second goal and took the lead for the first time in the game.

"The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball," the Premier League said.

‌



VAR added: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you award the goal."

Gary Neville delivered his verdict on the incident and repeated what was said by VAR when they were discussing about disallowing the goal. "If that shot had been on target it wouldn't have been a goal," Neville told Sky Sports.

View 2 Images Harry Maguuire put Manchester United ahead against Ipswich Town (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"VAR say to the referee 'hear me out and listen to me' because they know it's going to be complicated."

United had fallen behind in the 29th minute as Ipswich took a shock lead. Abdul Fatawu went past Luke Shaw with ease on the right-hand side before pulling the ball back for Leif Davis to smash home.

But the Reds responded 11 minutes later as Matheus Cunha pounced on an error from Marcelino Nunez to slide a pass through to Bruno Fernandes and he did the rest, slotting the ball beyond the Ipswich goalkeeper.

‌



Although Ipswich hadmade a bright start to the second half, United were ruthless in attack. After Greaves' own-goal put them ahead, Fernandes scored from the spot soon after to make it 3-1 to the Reds.

Fernandes wrapped up his hat-trick in the 68th minute, tucking the ball into the bottom corner after the ball fell into his path, before Bryan Mbeumo made it 5-1 to United with a well-taken lobbed effort.

There was still time for Ipswich to reduce the deficit to three and make it 5-2, however, as Julio Enciso robbed Lisandro Martinez before squaring to substitute Chuba Akpom to prod home from close-range.

Article continues below

That is how it ended in Manchester as the Reds secured their first win of the season and bounced back from last weekend's dismal opening defeat at Hull City.

Sports.title: Julian Alvarez makes Atletico Madrid decision after Arsenal transfer call with Mikel Arteta
Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez makes Atletico Madrid decision after Arsenal transfer call with Mikel Arteta

Julian Alvarez has missed three training sessions this week and did not feature in his side’s trip to Sevilla on Saturday as his transfer standoff continues

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez during a Atletico Madrid training session (Image: (Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press via Getty Images))

Julian Alvarez has returned to Atletico Madrid training after Diego Simeone vowed to welcome him back into his squad. Alvarez missed three training sessions this week and did not feature in his side’s 3-1 victory over Sevilla on Saturday night due to what the club said was a stomach bug.

‌



Atletico are standing firm in their refusal to sell Alvarez to Barcelona, with Arsenal leading the race to sign the forward. However, it has been claimed that the Argentine informed Gunners boss Mikel Arteta during talks that he does not want to return to England.

‌



Providing an update on Alvarez, Atletico sporting director Matheu Alemany said: "He trained yesterday, and we hope he recovers quickly and is ready for the upcoming La Liga match."

‌



He added: "We have been very clear and firm on this matter. The board issued a statement about it, and the chief executive confirmed it clearly and firmly. I refer you to that. Why should I say more?”

Simone said ahead of their 3-1 win against Sevilla on Saturday night: "I understand that all the questions will be about Julian. The club has been very clear about what will happen.

‌

"From a sporting perspective, I hope to help him continue being as important as he still is. My focus is on Sevilla, where he won't be available.

"When he returns, we’ll give him everything he needs to feel important. In life, anything can be reversed, as long as we have our health."

‌



Atletico have issued two public statements insisting they will not sell Alvarez to Barca, with a move elsewhere now appearing to be the only realistic option. And speaking on Thursday, Atletico chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin told Spanish broadcaster Movistar Plus: "Our intention and ⁠my personal dream is for him to stay with us, to remain at Atletico.

View 2 Images Diego Simeone talks to Julian Alvarez during an Atletico Madrid Champions League game (Image: (Manu Reino/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images))

"To compete among ‌the greats, you need great players, and Julian is one. If he believes that staying at Atletico Madrid is no longer feasible, we will look for an alternative, but it will never, ever be Barcelona.”

‌



Gil Marin continued: "The truth is that it outrages us even more. We are repulsed by the dishonesty, the lack of ethics, transparency and professionalism, and we can only insist that we will not negotiate with Barcelona under any circumstances.

"I have the support of everyone working with me, from shareholders ⁠to directors, and the only certain ‌and firm decision is that we will not negotiate with Barcelona under any circumstances; you have my word – which is one of the few things I have – the ‌player will most certainly not be transferred to Barcelona.”

Sports.title: Arsenal complete move for record-breaking EFL wonderkid after signing Man Utd starlet
Sports.content:
Arsenal complete move for record-breaking EFL wonderkid after signing Man Utd starlet

Arsenal have altered their transfer strategy this summer with the Gunners having moved for some of the country’s most promising young footballers and they’ve announced another deal

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal have been busy in the transfer market this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal have reached an agreement to sign Cardiff City wonderkid Axel Donczew. The Gunners were linked with the youngster earlier this summer as part of their strategy to move for some of the brightest young talents across the UK and further afield.

‌



And Donczew’s switch to North London has now been confirmed. A statement from Cardiff on Sunday read: “Cardiff City FC can confirm that an agreement has been reached for the transfer of Axel Donczew to Arsenal. Axel became our youngest player aged 15 years and 234 days old in October 2025, a record now held by Noah Anyadike.

‌



“The Club had offered terms for Donczew to continue his development with the Bluebirds and made efforts to retain the player, but he opted to pursue a move away from the Welsh capital. We wish Axel the best of luck for the future.”

‌



Donczew, 16, will now play a part in the Gunners’ academy with potential for first-team exposure in the future. His switch follows a number of incomings in North London over the past few days.

Igor Tyjon has been recruited from Cardiff’s Championship rivals Blackburn Rovers. After his move was made official, he said: "It feels amazing. I've waited a long time for this and I can't wait to get started.

‌



“It's a dream come true for [my family] as well, it's always a nice feeling when you make your family happy, so I'm buzzing for them as well.

"Who doesn't want to join the champions? I can't wait to be part of the team. The pathway, the staff, the players, everything about it, it's just top. I'm excited to meet the group, meet the players, hit the ground running and have a good season."

View 2 Images Arsenal have also signed James Scanlon this summer (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Arsenal have also signed James Scanlon from Premier League rivals Manchester United, while they are also interested in Red Devils youngster Habeeb Ogunneye.

Arsenal have also completed a deal for Vincent Joseph, who left Liverpool at the end of last season, albeit a tribunal will now decide how much the North London side will have to pay for the 16-year-old.

It’s also been a very busy summer from a first-team perspective. Arsenal have spent heavily in an effort to defend their Premier League crown.

Article continues below

Piero Hincapie returned on a permanent deal following an initial loan move from Bayer Leverkusen, while Bruno Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa and Christos Tzolis have also been recruited for big money. Arsenal remain linked with a move for Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez.

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk gives verdict on Bradley Barcola transfer and warns Liverpool bosses
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk gives verdict on Bradley Barcola transfer and warns Liverpool bosses

Liverpool are set to complete the £123million signing of Bradley Barcola, with Cody Gakpo now tipped to join Manchester City before the transfer window closes next week

View 2 Images Liverpool look set to sign Bradley Barcola (Image: PSG via Getty Images)

Virgil Van Dijk has backed Liverpool's decision to land Bradley Barcola in a £123m deal, but warned allowing Cody Gakpo to leave is a mistake.

‌



Barcola will have a medical on Merseyside before signing a five-year contract, after Paris Saint Germain accepted an initial £110m deal, plus £13m in add-ons.

‌



Supporters have criticised the club's decision to land another forward - and insist new boss Andoni Iraola needs to strengthen his midfield and defence instead.

‌



But Van Dijk believes Liverpool are landing a world class talent, who will sprinkle some stardust on a team which has failed to win its first two league games of the new season. Barcola will become the second most expensive signing in the club's history.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



And Van Dijk said: "He's a good player, that's the only thing I can say. I don't think there's any doubt that a club like Liverpool is very attractive to very good players.

"This is one of the biggest clubs in the world. We all know that we're going through a little bit of a transition. You either want to be a part of it or you don't. The window is open until Tuesday, right? Let's see what happens.

"He's a player with pace. I remember a goal he scored against Chelsea. If he comes here then he will be welcomed with open arms. But until it's official, there's no point speaking about it."

‌



View 2 Images Virgil van Dijk wants Cody Gakpo to remain at Anfield

Barcola's arrival is expected to see Gakpo leave Anfield, with Tottenham and Manchester City keen on landing the Dutchman. But Van Dijk has told Liverpool bosses that selling Gakpo would be a big mistake.

When asked if he wanted the winger to stay, Van Dijk added: "What do you think? He's a quality player. I think we should keep quality players.

Article continues below

"Let's see what the next few days bring. I want him to stay not only because he's a quality player, but also because he's a friend of mine. He's very important for us."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick hits out 'lazy' Man Utd critics after nightmare start to the season
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick hits out 'lazy' Man Utd critics after nightmare start to the season

Manchester United had the worst possible start to the 2026/27 season with defeat to newly-promoted Hull City but Red Devils boss Michael Carrick is not getting too downbeat

View 2 Images Michael Carrick endured a frustrating start to the season (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has further slammed criticism that Manchester United lack passion as ‘lazy’. The Red Devils boss was left irritated after his side’s opening day defeat to Hull City.

‌



He criticised a reporter in the aftermath of the game and claimed his comments about a potential lack of passion were ‘ridiculous’. Carrick was asked about that criticism ahead of this weekend’s clash with Ipswich Town and again did not agree with the sentiment.

‌



Speaking in his pre-match press conference, he said: "It's one game. I think there's enough leadership in our dressing room that we'll have it throughout the season.

‌



"Just because we lose a game doesn't just mean leadership, or I got passion thrown at me after the game, it's not just that. You lose two set-plays like we did, changes the game."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

He added: "Teams lose games, so there's different reasons. I don't have to give you the total reason, because we know what we're trying to improve on.

‌



"But I'm just saying to you, I think it's so easy and lazy to just, team loses a game, everything's wrong. This is wrong, this is wrong, not trying enough, not enough passion. It's just like the obvious answer."

And while Carrick is refusing to panic after United’s difficult start, he has told his players that they need to improve if they want to secure victory against Ipswich.

He said: "We've probably played like that and won games, and everyone goes, 'What a great team, what a great coach, what a great load of players,' when we find a way to win 1-0. So, from my perspective, when you're analysing it, it's not the feeling and just that because of the feeling.

‌



View 2 Images Carrick has refused to panic following defeat to Hull (Image: Getty Images )

"We've got to dig deeper than that and understand the details of it. And we do, don't get carried away when we win certain games because we know it's not been perfect. And sometimes when you lose games, we know what we need to improve on.

"But there's certainly things that we can be a little bit clearer on, and calmer on in certain moments, to understand that, and keep the belief that things that we'll do well, which we will do, will win us games."

Article continues below

United have spent heavily in the transfer market this summer, having added midfielders Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba to Carrick’s squad. The latter is unavailable ahead of this weekend’s game as he continues his recovery from an ankle injury he picked up with former club Brighton.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
