Summary

Tuesday’s preliminary hearing in the cocaine trafficking case against former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor has been pushed to Wednesday, September 2, at 10:00 a.m., after the Ministry of Justice requested a last-minute continuance. The delay comes as questions grow around the state’s timeline linking her to an alleged cocaine network.

Court Grants Continuance Hours Before First Hearing Was Set to Open

By Rodney D. Sieh, [email protected]

MONROVIA — The preliminary hearing in the cocaine trafficking case against former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor will not go forward until next as Wednesday, September 2, 2026.

Early this morning, The Ministry of Justice’s Office of the City Solicitor asked the Monrovia City Court for a continuance just hours before the case was due to open, and Stipendiary Magistrate Cllr. L. Ben Barco granted it.

The hearing will now resume Wednesday, September 2, at 10:00 a.m.

In its request, the government said the Supreme Court’s closing of its March Term of Court had pulled several senior lawyers away to attend on their supervisors, leaving the prosecution short of the counsel it needed for the day.

It is a short delay, but it lands at a moment when the state’s own account of the case is drawing closer scrutiny. Howard-Taylor faces nine charges built around allegations that a businessman, Sheikh Bassirou Kante, introduced her to an alleged Croatian-Ukrainian cocaine network in “early 2022,” first at her Congo Town residence and later in Dubai.

What has quietly complicated that narrative is a matter of public U.S. court record: Kante was arrested in Maryland on April 20, 2022, on wire fraud and money laundering charges unrelated to narcotics.

The charge sheet gives no specific date for the Congo Town meeting or the Dubai trip, and no travel records placing Kante in Liberia or the Gulf ahead of his arrest have yet been made public. That gap has left room for a question the defense is expected to press hard on Wednesday: where, precisely, was everyone when this was supposed to have happened?

Howard-Taylor has denied all charges.

Her legal team has called the case baseless and politically motivated and says it will contest it vigorously when the hearing resumes.

FrontPageAfrica will continue to follow this story as it develops.

World.title: Liberia: River Tragedy Escalates Into Violence in Bong as Rep. Koinah Moves to Restore Calm
World.content:
GBARNGA, Bong County — A canoe accident on the St. John River has plunged communities in Bong County into tension after the disappearance of a couple sparked allegations, retaliatory attacks and the burning of homes and a rice kitchen in Duah Town.

The incident, which occurred on August 27, 2026, involved Kennedy Nyah and his wife, Ruth Nyah, residents of Kpanquoi Town, who reportedly went missing after the canoe in which they were traveling capsized at a crossing point along the St. John River.

What initially began as a search for the missing couple later developed into a violent confrontation, with several residents reportedly injured and at least 10 houses destroyed.

The violence reportedly occurred in Duah Town, Senwein Clan, Boinsen Administrative District, where a rice kitchen and several houses were allegedly set ablaze following the canoe accident.

Relatives and other community members reportedly became angered by the circumstances surrounding the capsizing and allegedly accused the canoe operator of deliberately causing the incident.

The allegation has not been independently established, and the circumstances that led to the canoe capsizing remain subject to investigation.

The growing anger reportedly resulted in some residents targeting properties in Duah Town, turning the aftermath of the river accident into a wider security and community dispute.

Amid the escalating situation, Bong County Electoral District One Representative Prince K. Koinah has stepped in, calling for an immediate end to the violence and urging residents of the affected communities to exercise restraint.

Rep. Koinah’s office has condemned the attacks in the strongest terms, describing the destruction of property and injuries as deeply unfortunate and stressing that residents must allow the appropriate authorities to investigate the incident and pursue justice.

As part of his intervention, Representative Koinah has dispatched a team comprising his Chief of Staff and Administrative Officer to the affected communities.

The team has been tasked with engaging residents and supporting efforts to calm tensions while working alongside law enforcement and local authorities.

The intervention is aimed at preventing further violence and creating an environment in which authorities can conduct their investigation without additional confrontation.

The Liberia National Police and local county authorities have also moved into the area as efforts continue to restore law and order.

The security intervention comes at a time when the fate of the couple remains a major concern for relatives and residents.

The body of Ruth Nyah has reportedly been recovered from the St. John River, while search efforts remain underway for her husband, Kennedy.

The recovery of Ruth’s body has intensified the urgency surrounding the search for Kennedy and has further underscored the need for calm as relatives await answers about the circumstances surrounding the tragedy.

Representative Koinah has expressed frustration over the violence that followed the accident, particularly the reported destruction of homes and other properties.

The lawmaker has urged residents not to resort to retaliation or take the law into their own hands, warning that such actions could further deepen tensions and result in additional injuries and destruction.

He has instead encouraged residents to cooperate with law enforcement and allow investigators to establish what happened before, during and after the canoe capsized.

The District One lawmaker is also urging residents of both Kpanquoi and Duah to protect the peace and avoid actions that could widen the dispute between the communities.

His office said Koinah remains engaged in efforts to ensure the safety and welfare of residents affected by the incident, while his dispatched team continues its engagement with community members.

The incident has highlighted broader concerns over the potential for local disputes to escalate rapidly when communities are confronted with tragedy, uncertainty and unverified allegations.

For residents of Kpanquoi and Duah, the immediate priorities remain the restoration of calm, the continued search for Kennedy Nyah and an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the canoe accident and subsequent attacks.

Authorities are expected to maintain their presence in the affected communities as the situation develops.

Representative Koinah has meanwhile reiterated his call for peace, emphasizing that any person found responsible for wrongdoing should face justice through the established legal process rather than through retaliatory attacks.

He has appealed to residents to remain calm, cooperate with the authorities and refrain from further violence as efforts continue to resolve the crisis.

State House has dismissed as cheap propaganda claims that the Executive is pressuring Chief Justice Mumba Malila to ignore a presidential election petition, after opposition figure Clayson Hamasaaka alleged that pressure was being applied on the judiciary to have the Chief Justice sit on the matter rather than let it proceed.

Brebner Changala said Chief Justice Malila, who has acknowledged receiving the petition and forwarded it to the Constitutional Court, should resist external pressure and ensure the petition gets its day in court, according to a report carried by the Daily Nation.

The Judiciary confirmed that the petition, filed by opposition leader Brian Mundubile, has in fact been forwarded to the Constitutional Court, contradicting suggestions that it had been ignored or suppressed.

The dispute comes against the backdrop of the brief closure of courts on August 24, the very day the deadline for filing a presidential petition was expiring, a development that drew criticism from civil society and opposition figures who questioned the timing.

A Judiciary memorandum at the time instructed staff not to report for work, citing security concerns, while police presence around court premises restricted access. The Judiciary has said the closure does not establish that President Hakainde Hichilema personally ordered it, and has stressed that determining the effect of the closure would require evidence rather than speculation.

With the petition now formally before the Constitutional Court, the practical question is one of timing: the ceremony marking the start of President Hichilema’s second term falls on Tuesday, leaving a narrow window for the court to signal how, and how quickly, it intends to deal with a challenge of this weight.

Changala’s intervention places him among a small number of civil society voices who have spoken publicly on the judiciary’s independence in the days since the election, distinct from the separate legal questions raised over the conduct of the Mandevu rerun and the various election petitions already lodged at the Ndola High Court.

Government has maintained that the courts remain independent and that the petition process will be allowed to run its lawful course, with the Constitutional Court now seized with the matter.

The controversy over court access follows weeks of tension since the August 13 election, during which President Hichilema was declared the winner, opposition figures were arrested, and a raid on Mundubile’s home left former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya dead.

As the Constitutional Court prepares to consider the petition, both government and opposition supporters will be watching to see whether the process is seen to be free, transparent and untainted by outside interference.

World.title: A Day After Fresh Mandevu Order, ZCLU Questions ECZ’s Legal Authority
World.content:
LUSAKA: A day after the Electoral Commission of Zambia ordered a fresh parliamentary election in Mandevu constituency, the decision is facing a direct legal challenge, with a civil rights group insisting the Commission had no lawful basis to call the rerun.

ECZ announced on Saturday that it would conduct a fresh poll in Mandevu following a security breach at the constituency’s totalling centre on August 13. Unknown individuals attacked the centre, destroyed result transmission kits and fled with documentation, preventing declaration of results in the seat.

The Zambian Civil Liberties Union has now questioned the legal authority behind that decision. Executive director Isaac Mwanza said there is no law that mandates the Commission to cancel and conduct fresh parliamentary elections outright.

ZCLU said it had examined the Electoral Process Act of 2016, as amended in 2025 and 2026, particularly Sections 56 and 75, and found that neither provision applies to a cancellation or a fresh call for nominations of this kind. “The two sections cannot both apply,” Mwanza said, since the Mandevu incident occurred after voting and during aggregation. He argued the only proper course open to ECZ was to approach the Constitutional Court for guidance on whether a by-election could be held at all, given that no law empowers it to order one unilaterally.

Candidate reaction has hardened in the day since Saturday’s announcement. Citizens First’s Steven Mwale argued the fresh poll would impose a heavy financial and logistical burden on candidates who had already invested heavily in their campaigns, saying the commission should instead have pursued those responsible for the alleged ballot tampering rather than ordering a complete rerun.

Independent candidate Adrian Banda said he remained too disturbed to comment further, while Resolute Party’s Jean Kapata has still not spoken to journalists on the matter.

Socialist Party’s Teddy Mwaba maintained his welcome of the decision a day on, describing it as a step toward restoring fairness following irregularities in the original vote, and repeated his call for ECZ to release a full election timetable without delay.

Green Party leader Peter Sinkamba, who warned on Saturday that the disputed August 13 poll could be reduced to an academic exercise unless the manipulation that marred the process is addressed, has since gone further. He is now challenging ECZ to consider fresh mayoral elections in Lusaka alongside the Mandevu rerun, given how much the mayoral vote draws from Mandevu.

ECZ now faces a choice: defend its authority to order the rerun as announced, or clarify whether it intends to seek the Constitutional Court’s guidance that Mwanza says the law actually requires. Ten parliamentary candidates remain on standby for the reignited Mandevu seat once, or if, nomination and polling dates are confirmed.

World.title: State Agents Search Makebi Zulu’s Home As Church Denies Political Deal Claim
World.content:
Security agents have searched the Lusaka residence of opposition running mate Makebi Zulu, a search his lawyer Sakwiba Sikota says was carried out without his legal team being notified beforehand, raising fresh questions about how the operation was conducted.

The search comes as an eight-member church mediation team dismissed suggestions that it had brokered, or attempted to broker, a political settlement between government and the opposition. In a statement, the churches said their mandate was never to negotiate a political deal between the two sides, but rather to facilitate a peaceful and dignified transition through the United Nations premises to legal representatives.

The clarification followed reports that Brian Mundubile and Zulu had been handed over as part of a negotiated arrangement, a narrative the churches were keen to correct given the sensitivity of the treason case against the pair.

Sikota’s objection centres on the absence of prior notice to counsel, a procedural point that lawyers say matters regardless of the seriousness of the allegations under investigation, since it goes to whether the rights of an accused person are being observed at every stage of an operation, not only once a matter reaches court.

The search of Zulu’s home follows a similar operation at Mundubile’s Kabulonga residence on August 14, during which former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya was killed and various weapons recovered. Eleven people associated with Mundubile were arrested during that operation.

The Law Association of Zambia has continued to follow the handling of the case, with its leadership convening briefings to update the public on developments affecting the accused, including procedural questions of the kind Sikota has now raised over his client’s search.

With both principal opposition figures now facing treason charges and their properties searched, how each search was conducted, and not only what was found, is likely to feature prominently once the matter reaches open court.

World.title: Mundubile And Zulu Charged With Treason As Case Widens To 18
World.content:
Opposition leader Brian Mundubile and his running mate Makebi Zulu have been charged with treason, bringing to 18 the number of people accused in a widening case that has followed Zambia’s August general election.

Lawyer Milner Katolo, who represents several of the accused, confirmed the development in an interview with Muvi TV, saying his clients, including Mundubile and Zulu of the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity, had each been charged with one count of treason.

Katolo said police should have gathered sufficient evidence before laying the charge, and insisted the matter must be taken to court within 48 hours in line with constitutional detention requirements.

Among those already facing the charge are Patrick Mwansa, husband of Tasila Lungu, and Valden Findlay. A separate list named 16 people in total who were confirmed by Katolo to have been charged over an August 14 security operation at Mundubile’s Kabulonga residence.

Mundubile and Zulu remain in custody, having spent more than a week held at a United Nations compound before their transfer to police hands. Officers interrogated both men at Lusaka Central Police Station over the weekend.

Police spokesperson Godfrey Chilabi told Diamond TV that the police station remained open to the public and fully operational, dismissing suggestions that it had been sealed off. “Just like the Inspector General of Police said, all persons in custody are given their full rights, which include interacting with their relatives as well as having access to their legal counsel,” Chilabi said.

The raid on Mundubile’s house, during which former Cabinet minister Mutotwe Kafwaya was killed, has become the flashpoint of the post-election crisis. Police said various military-grade weapons and devices were recovered from the property, and among those arrested were former special forces operatives and a retired police officer.

Mundubile had rejected the outcome of the August 13 election, in which President Hakainde Hichilema was declared winner with 2,965,326 votes against Mundubile’s 1,856,217, and had signalled his intention to challenge the result before the courts.

The Law Association of Zambia has continued to monitor the case, with president Arnold Kaluba addressing a press briefing on developments affecting the accused.

International rights group Amnesty International raised concerns about the arrests, prompting a rebuttal from UPND media director Mark Simuwe, who said Zambia’s justice system required investigations to be completed before charges were determined, and that focus should fall on whether suspects had been subjected to trumped-up charges rather than on the mere fact of arrests involving allegations of possessing military weapons.

With the accused now formally charged, attention turns to how the matter proceeds through the courts, and whether the process will be seen to meet the standard of fairness that both prosecution and defence say they want upheld.

World.title: Zesco Girls fall in COSAFA final
World.content:
‎ZESCO Ndola Girls missed out on the CAF Women’s Champions League COSAFA Qualifier 2026 title on Saturday evening after a 2-1 defeat to South Africa’s Mamelodi Sundowns in the final.

‎

‎It was a case of déjà vu for the Zambian champions, who were also losing finalists in last year’s COSAFA Qualifier.

‎

‎Sundowns made a perfect start when Refilwe Tholakele opened the scoring in the 2nd minute.

‎

‎ZESCO responded and fought back, equalizing deep in first-half stoppage time through Charity Mubanga to send the teams into the break locked at 1-1.

‎

‎The second half turned on two key moments. The Ndola Girls suffered a huge blow when star midfielder Eneless Phiri was injured and replaced by Fridah Kabwe.

‎

‎Then in the 64th minute, the referee awarded Sundowns a penalty after a VAR review confirmed a foul inside the ZESCO penalty area.

‎

‎Tholakele stepped up and converted to score her second of the match and restore Sundowns’ lead.

‎

‎ZESCO pushed for another equalizer but could not break down the South African defense.

‎

‎ZESCO reached the final after edging Silver Strikers of Malawi 2-1 on Thursday.

‎

‎Earlier in the tournament, the Ndola Girls topped Group A with 9 points from 3 wins.

‎

‎The COSAFA Qualifier serves as the regional pathway for Southern African clubs to reach Africa’s premier women’s club competition — the CAF Women’s Champions League. With the win, Mamelodi Sundowns will represent the COSAFA region at the continental finals.

‎

‎It was a heartbreaking end for ZESCO, who conceded a controversial late penalty to lose the regional crown for the second year running.

World.title: Kazungula woman dies in suspected suicide
World.content:
A 26-year-old female suspect was found hanging in the female cells at Kazungula Police Station.

The deceased identified as Milimo Mpongo of Makalanguzu village in Chief Sekute’s area in Kazungula district was detailed alone in the cells in connection with four theft complaints.

Southern Province Commanding Officer, Moono Namalongo revealed in a statement availed to the media that the deceased was discovered hanging in the female cells using a chitenge material she was wearing, which had been tied to a window burglar bar on August 28, 2026 between 07:00 hours and 08:00 hours.

Mr Namalongo explained that on August 27, 2026 between 14:00 hours and 16:00 hours Ms Mpongo allegedly visited four different Airtel money businesses in Kazungula district and requested transactions ranging from K1, 000 to K3, 400 to be deposited into her mobile money number.

“It is alleged that after the transactions, she would open a small black laptop bag she was carrying and claim that she had forgotten the money at home before disappearing from the respective places,” Mr Namalongo explained.

He said following the complaints, the deceased was apprehended and placed in police custody where the suspected incident of suicide happened.

Mr Namalongo further said officers on duty spoke to her the same day, August 28, 2026 around 07:00 hours, and was later discovered hanging in the female cells using a chitenge material she was wearing.

He added that Police informed the deceased’s relatives about the incident stating that the body was untied in the presence of a relative and taken to Kazungula District Hospital where she was certified dead.

“The body was later taken and deposited at Livingstone Hospital Mortuary awaiting postmortem examination. The investigations into the matter are ongoing,” said Mr Namalongo.

World.title: Govt. praised on timely payment of farmers
World.content:
Newly elected Lumwana Member of Parliament, Mathews Mashimamgo has applauded the government for the timely payment of farmers selling maize to the Food Reserve Agency (FRA), saying the new payment system allows farmers to receive their money within three days.

Speaking during a spot check at the Mutanda FRA Depot in Kalumbila District, Mr Mashimamgo said the prompt payments would enable farmers to invest their earnings in other businesses as they prepare for the next farming season.

Mr Mashimamgo also assured farmers that the challenge of constructing a concrete slab at the Mutanda FRA Depot would be addressed.

He said a contractor would be engaged next year with support from the community to improve the depot and provide farmers with a better environment in which to sell their maize.

Mr Mashimamgo further appealed to the government to consider opening more FRA depots in the constituency to improve access for farmers travelling from distant areas.

“As we get to Parliament, we will appeal to the President through the Ministry of Agriculture to open more FRA depots to ease access for farmers coming from far distances such as Kamiba, Mushingashi, Kayonge and Kananga,” he said.

Mr Mashimamgo said opening additional depots would help address the challenges faced by farmers who currently have to travel long distances to sell their produce.

He added that his office would continue visiting FRA depots across the constituency to obtain first-hand information on the challenges farmers are facing.

“We are going round to all depots in our constituency to have first-hand information and see what is happening on the ground,” he said.

Meanwhile, a farmer, Anna Shakopo thanked the government for purchasing maize from farmers and implementing the Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP).

Ms Shakopo said the new payment system had made it easier for farmers to access their money through banks and mobile phones.

“We thank the government for the new payment system. We can now receive our money through the bank and mobile phone,” she said.

She said previously, farmers had to spend long hours and sometimes sleep at banks while waiting to access payments from the FRA.

Ms Shakopo added that the improved payment system together with timely FISP-related payments and FRA funds had reduced the need for farmers to travel long distances to collect their money.

Another farmer, Friday Matebo, thanked the government for the initiatives being implemented to support farmers and called for an increase in the FISP allocation.

World.title: Chipata’s Kagunda community set to receive electricity
World.content:
More than 2,000 people in Kagunda Community of Chipata Central Constituency are set to access electricity for the first time following the implementation of an electricity connection project by the Chipata City Council.

The project, which will be implemented at a total of K907,524.32, by the Chipata Council through the Constituency Development Fund (CDF), has reached 90 percent completion.

Chipata City Council Assistant Public Relations Officer, Grace Lungu, says the project would connect households and community institutions to the national electricity grid and improve access to reliable power.

The provision of electricity would also create opportunities for socio-economic development in Kagunda Community.

She explained that access to electricity was expected to stimulate economic activities by supporting small and medium-sized businesses, improving productivity and creating an enabling environment for new enterprises to thrive.

Ms.Lungu said the Council remained committed to implementing infrastructure projects that respond to the needs of local communities and contribute to improved livelihoods.

She expressed confidence that completion of the project would help transform Kagunda into a more vibrant, connected and economically empowered community.
