World.title: The Croatian Island Settlement Once Called the Village of Millionaires
World.content:
August the 29th, 2026 – There’s a very old Croatian island settlement that was once often referred to as the village of millionaires, but today a mere 20 people remain there.

On the beautiful central Dalmatian island of Hvar there are an incredible 936 monuments, six of which are protected by UNESCO. It’s home to the oldest public theatre in all of Europe, one of the larger town squares in the entire Mediterranean, beautiful churches, fortresses and summer residences… As Putni kofer writes, listing all of Hvar’s beauty and attractions would take hours, and for most people, there’s never quite enough time to see them all.

Many people therefore only focus only on the coast and miss the picturesque interior and the fascinating areas it is home to. One of them is the old, now eerily quiet Velo Grablje, once known as the village of millionaires.

ancient stone homes locked in another time

Hidden among the hills, vineyards and dry-stone walls, Velo Grablje at first glance looks as if it has remained frozen in another time. Narrow stone streets, old houses with wooden shutters and an almost unreal silence only reinforce that impression. Today, according to the latest census, the village has only 20 inhabitants, but a hundred years ago there were as many as 500. That means that in one century the place lost 96 percent of its former population.

Today tourists visit the village for its authentic Dalmatian atmosphere, but the reason for its prosperity a hundred years ago was not tourism. There were never luxury villas, swimming pools or wealthy foreigners here, but there was something far more valuable at the time: lavender. The story begins in the late 1920s, when Hvar’s vineyards were going through a difficult period because of downy mildew. Looking for a new crop that could thrive on the rocky and dry soil, local resident Bartul Tomičić was the first to start growing lavender and producing essential oil.

Lavender had existed on the island earlier, but it was he who, at the end of the 1920s, began cultivating it as a commercial crop and producing oil from it. It was not an easy decision. After the problems with the vineyards, the island’s inhabitants had to look for new crops that could succeed on the stony soil and bring in income. Tomičić became convinced about lavender after a lecture by two experts from Split. At first his neighbours found the idea strange. Planting flowers instead of the usual crops? Many thought it frivolous. However, it turned out that Hvar’s climate is ideal for this plant, and production soon began to spread across the entire island.

every household was involved in the harvest

The centre of production was precisely Velo Grablje. In the middle of the 20th century lavender brought such good income that the villagers were among the wealthiest on the island, and their village earned the nickname “village of millionaires.” For a time Velo Grablje was the largest producer of lavender oil in Dalmatia. For decades, lavender shaped the life of the local people. Almost every family took part in the harvest, distillation and sale of the oil, and the scent of the purple fields became the trademark of the whole island. Until the 1970s, the island of Hvar was among the most important lavender-growing areas in the entire Mediterranean.

Naturally, the glorious age of lavender did not last that long. Purchase prices fell, young people left for the mainland or abroad, some plantations were destroyed by fires, and the old village gradually emptied. In the hardest times only seven permanent residents remained in Velo Grablje.

only around 20 people remain in velo grablje today

Although the number of inhabitants is smaller than ever, the village still lives, but at a slower and quieter pace. That emptiness, peace and old stone architecture are exactly what delights tourists who arrive from the busy and noisy coast into its narrow stone lanes. In recent years Velo Grablje has even been experiencing a kind of revival, precisely thanks to the preservation of tradition and cultural heritage. The golden age of lavender has been turned into a brand of the small place, whose highlight is the Lavender Festival held at the beginning of July.

This year, the festival took place on the 3rd and 4th of July. The story of lavender on Hvar is wider than Velo Grablje. Lavender fields are also found around Brusje and in the area of the Stari Grad Plain, and since 2015 almost a hectare of plantations has been grown near Jelsa. Individual lavender bushes can be seen in other parts of the island as well, along roads and on old terraces.

World.title: Mate Rimac Talks Super Cars, Bugatti and Tech
World.content:
August the 29th, 2026 – Bugatti CEO Mate Rimac has discussed the future of super cars, the situation at Bugatti and the technology current and future buyers are turning towards.

“The automotive industry is a bit like the watch industry. Digital and smart watches have taken over most of the market, while expensive Swiss mechanical watches remain popular among the wealthy” explained Mate Rimac, CEO of Bugatti. He added that the super car market is entering its “Swiss watch phase.” Poslovni reports that he claims that the wealthiest buyers are turning their backs on high technology and electric vehicles in favour of precision mechanics and handcrafted details.

Rimac, who took over Bugatti back in 2021, said that the car market is splitting into two parts: the main global car market is beginning to be dominated by cheaper electric vehicles, many from China, while the very top of the car market will be led by wealthy buyers who prefer “old” cars with loud internal combustion engines and emotional appeal, according to CNBC.

“For normal cars, for normal people, the vast majority will be electric,” Rimac said. “The upper segment, like sports cars and above, will ‘burn’ for a long time, just like watches. Only about 5 percent of watches are produced in Switzerland, but 90 percent of the profit is made there. An Apple Watch or any kind of smartwatch can do many more things. But no one will pay 200,000 dollars for that.”

a totally new vehicle

The hybrid Tourbillon has an 8.3-litre V16 engine that delivers 1,000 horsepower, combined with electric motors for a total of 1,800 horsepower. When the Rimac Group took control of Bugatti from Porsche and Volkswagen in 2021, many expected the newly formed Bugatti Rimac Group to launch an electric Bugatti. Instead, Rimac built a completely new car powered by one of the largest internal combustion engines ever made for a production car. The hybrid Tourbillon has an 8.3-litre V16 engine that delivers 1,000 horsepower, combined with electric motors for a total of 1,800 horsepower.

“It’s a bit ironic that I’m now making the largest internal combustion engine in the world,” he said. “Now you have a crazy situation in our plant in Croatia. On the same production line, you have the most powerful electric car in the world being built right next to the world’s largest internal combustion engine. Life is sometimes strange.” Bugatti will produce only 250 Tourbillons, which are sold out at a starting price of around $4.5 million. Rimac said that the average Tourbillon buyer adds an extra $600,000 to $700,000 in personalisation options, such as special colours, leather, stitching, and other design features.

The rise of personalisation and customisation has become one of the biggest profit drivers for super car companies like Bugatti, Ferrari, and Lamborghini. Super car companies are also launching special one-off cars for their customers that can cost tens of millions of dollars. At Monterey Car Week, Bugatti presented its latest model called Destrier. Rimac said that customisations and unique examples reflect the desire of today’s wealthy to have objects that show their identity. A staggering two billion dollars is the price for which Porsche AG sold its 45 percent stake in Bugatti Rimac back in April.

maintaining exclusivity

“Those clients want something that is truly theirs, that is connected to them, that tells their story, their personality, their preferences, not just as a car. There’s a whole story behind it.” Mate Rimac said that his goal for Bugatti is to continue increasing production, quality, and profit while maintaining exclusivity. He said production will never be higher than “low three-digit numbers.” The company made 200 million euros in profit before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation last year and will continue to grow, Rimac said.

Porsche AG agreed to sell its 45 percent stake in Bugatti Rimac back in April to a global consortium led by HOF Capital. While some reports put the valuation of Bugatti at over 1.1 billion dollars, Rimac said the price was “significantly higher” than 2 billion dollars. “What I want to do is produce the best cars in the world, the most exciting cars in the world, and have the most profitable car company in the world on a percentage basis,” he concluded.

World.title: New Health Tourism Hotel Opened in Zagorje in 17.6 Million Euro Investment
World.content:
August the 29th, 2026 – A brand new health tourism hotel has opened its doors in beautiful Zagorje as part of a 17.6 million euro investment made with EU cash.

The final conference was recently held in Stubičke Toplice regarding a project called “Construction of the pool and hotel of the Special Hospital for Medical Rehabilitation Stubičke Toplice”. Zagorje.com reports that that took place alongside the opening of the Thermal Hotel Wrello.

With the opening of the Thermal Hotel Wrello, the Special Hospital Stubičke Toplice begins a new chapter in its development. The project, worth more than 17.6 million euros, included the construction of a brand new four-star hotel and the covering of the pool complex with wellness and accompanying facilities, which will now be available year-round. The new health resort and hotel in the green heart of Zagorje boasts 36 rooms and two apartments (approximately 70 beds) and a restaurant with 100 seats. It’s connected to the existing hospital premises, uniting medical rehabilitation, thermal facilities, and hotel accommodation into a functional whole.

a step forward for continental croatian health tourism

Director of the Special Hospital Stubičke Toplice, Zorica Capar, emphasised that this facility is not only a combination of modern design and top technology, but also a symbol of vision, perseverance, and joint work.

“This project represents a historic step forward for our hospital and for the entire Krapina-Zagorje County. Stubičke Toplice has been known for centuries for its sources of healing thermal water and its tradition of treatment. With this hotel, we are combining that rich tradition with the highest standards of modern medicine, rehabilitation, and hospitality. We can now offer our patients and guests the care and comfort they truly deserve,” the director said, reflecting on the development path. The investment journey began back in May 2021 with the opening of the outdoor pool, the first phase worth 3.5 million euros. The hotel construction and outdoor pool covering project officially started in September 2024 and took 23 months to complete. The total value of this capital investment is 17,426,263 euros. From the National Recovery and Resilience Plan, 16,564,159 euros was secured, of which 16,452,978 euros are non-repayable EU funds. The 99.32% support intensity testifies to the sheer excellence of the project.

“Through extensive construction work, a four-star hotel was built, the existing pool was covered, and a new wellness centre was constructed, covering a total area of 6,500 square metres. A connecting corridor was also built that enables direct indoor communication between the hotel and the hospital, which is crucial for patients. On the ground floor, the Thermal Hotel offers top-quality hospitality facilities with a kitchen and restaurant, while the first and second floors house accommodation capacities with 37 rooms and two apartments with loggias. On the first floor there is a completely new physiotherapy department equipped with the most modern equipment, and the third floor offers a rooftop terrace and a social space. All works have been successfully completed, the occupancy permit has been obtained, and the hotel has received a four-star categorisation,” the director said.

an employment boost for krapina-zagorje

“Through this investment, 34 people from the Krapina-Zagorje County area have been newly employed, thereby directly strengthening the local community. The new tourist infrastructure will operate all 12 months of the year, and all additional hotel facilities will also be available to citizens, tourists, and visitors, ensuring the full potential of year-round health tourism. Special thematic wellness service packages have been designed to provide top-quality spa and wellness tourism services. The spaces of the new covered pool are equipped with the most modern water exercise equipment, including special bikes, treadmills, and elliptical trainers, raising medical recreation and rehabilitation to a new level,” Capar emphasised.

The authenticity of the offer is further enriched by a special food corner within the complex, where local products will be offered through cooperation with local family farms (OPGs). “This project raises standards for hospital staff, ensures top-quality care for users of health services, and creates a new experience for all users of spa and wellness tourism services,” the director noted, expressing gratitude to everyone who participated in the project.

“May this spa hotel be a place of recovery, rest, and shared success,” Capar concluded.

the largest project in the history of the municipality

Mayor of the Municipality of Stubičke Toplice, Josip Beljak, stressed that this day will remain written in golden letters in the history of the municipality.

“This is individually the largest project in the history of the municipality. The opening of the Thermal Hotel Wrello and the new pools is not just the opening of a new facility. It is the beginning of a new centre of health, rehabilitation, and tourism. Every quality investment that takes place in our municipality, regardless of who the investor is, means the development of Stubičke Toplice, a better offer, new jobs, new guests, greater recognition of the place, and also opportunities for all our people and our entrepreneurs. And when we put today’s project into the broader picture of everything currently happening in Stubičke Toplice, I think only then can we see the scale of what we are witnessing. Another historic moment awaits us soon, and that’s the completion of the extension of our primary school and the completion of the school gymnasium. The hotel and pools, the school and sports hall — different projects with different investors, but they have one thing in common: our Stubičke Toplice and the people who live here.

When we add up these two major investments, we’re talking about more than 23 million euros invested in the municipality area in the last two years alone. For such a small municipality, these are exceptionally large figures, an exceptional investment cycle, and I think we can all be proud of that together. Stubičke Toplice has a long and valuable tradition. Generations before us recognised the value of our thermal springs and built the identity of our place on them. Our task is not only to preserve that tradition, but also to develop it. We want modern Stubičke Toplice that will remain recognisable as a place of health, but we also want to be a place of quality living, sport, tourism, quality education, and pleasant life. We want to be a place where our young people will have a reason to stay, where families will want to live, and where our guests will always return. That is why I do not see today’s day only as the completion of one large project; I see it as the beginning of the direction in which Stubičke Toplice is heading,” Beljak emphasised.

health in the palm of your hand

County Prefect Željko Kolar pointed out that this project is the result of a long-term vision and continuous investment in health tourism, with the goal of positioning Zagorje as the leading region in rehabilitation and health services, highlighting the “Health in the Palm of Your Hand” project.

He emphasised that this is the realisation of a long-term vision started back in 2017, aimed at uniting all health institutions to provide top-quality services. Kolar stressed that the key to success is the excellent people in healthcare and the rich tradition of rehabilitation in Stubičke and Krapinske Toplice. The project was realised in five phases, the first of which, with an investment of 3.5 million euros, was completed back in 2021.

“With this, the government enabled us to combine the second, third, and fourth phases, which we would objectively have done over the next ten years or so without this European funding call,” Kolar explained. He expressed particular pride that domestic designers and contractors participated in the realisation.

The saga doesn’t end with the opening of the new health resort in Zagorje. Kolar announced further investments until 2030. As early as next spring, the adaptation of the Antonina facility, worth around 6 million euros and financed by the County, will begin. A project for the energy renovation of the old hotel of the Special Hospital for Medical Rehabilitation, worth 5 million euros and co-financed from the Environmental Protection Fund, has also been submitted. This will mean almost 10 million euros invested in Stubičke Toplice over the last decade.

World.title: Iraq’s central bank freezes assets of senior officials in anti-graft sweep
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) has ordered the immediate freeze of moveable and immovable assets for political figures, parliamentarians, and former officials as part of a comprehensive judicial anti-graft effort.

Following security operations, the CBI asked all licensed commercial banks to restrict transaction flows, confiscate properties, and disclose accounts associated with the targeted individuals in accordance with Anti-Corruption Investigative Court guidelines.

Financial institutions must compare client account activity to official monthly government salaries to identify abrupt asset increases or excessive wealth buildup.

Monitoring procedures apply directly to bank accounts held by spouses, intimate family members, and close business partners to prohibit the use of third-party front businesses for asset concealment.

This step is part of a countrywide anti-graft campaign led by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government. The campaign, known as “Operation Dawn,” aims to expose deeply rooted financial corruption among Iraq’s crucial ministries.

The Iraqi prime minister’s legal advisor, Munir Haddad, revealed in early July that more than $2 trillion have been stolen from Iraq since 2003.

According to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Haddad stated that the number of suspects continues to increase as investigations with the arrested ones are ongoing.

The countrywide anti-corruption campaign resulted in the arrests of several lawmakers and senior officials, as well as the recovery of millions of dollars, gold, luxurious cars, and real estate.

World.title: Iraq to speed up construction of strategic oil pipeline network
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi stated on Saturday that the oil export pipeline project is important to the country since it would diversify export routes and increase export capacity.

During a meeting with senior officials in the oil industry and representatives from the project’s implementation company, al-Zaidi emphasized the importance of moving quickly with the implementation of the oil pipeline network, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Al-Zaidi directed the Oil Ministry to provide the best possible conditions for the implementing companies to ensure the project’s completion according to the highest standards as it serves Iraq’s economic and developmental interests.

The prime minister reviewed the project’s technical and economic specifics, as well as its long-term developmental implications, export routes, and estimated oil quantities through the Basra-Haditha-Fishkhabur and Haditha-Baniyas pipelines.

Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair met last week with officials from Qatar’s UCC Holding in Baghdad to discuss the oil pipeline projects that aim to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

The discussions addressed establishing technical frameworks, project schedules, and contractual structures for the Basra-Haditha-Fishkhabur pipeline to Turkey and the Haditha-Baniyas pipeline to Syria.

Iraq is prioritizing this oil pipeline network to build alternate export routes to the Mediterranean to minimize its longstanding vulnerability and reliance on maritime shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Qatar-based UCC Holding is leading the consortium that includes Chevron, TI Capital, and TotalEnergies to carry out the project.

The project is a network of pipelines that will be extended to the Turkish port of Ceyhan and the Syrian port of Baniyas, providing two additional outlets to enhance export flexibility.

The Basra-Haditha pipeline project is an Iraqi venture estimated at $4.6 billion aiming to transport crude oil from the southern Iraqi province of Basra to Haditha in the western Iraqi province of Anbar.

Reaching Haditha opens up three distinct offshore export routes: the Turkish port of Ceyhan, the Syrian port of Baniyas, and Jordan’s port of Aqaba.

Iraq’s proposed oil pipeline network indicates an anticipatory initiative to lessen reliance on Gulf maritime routes, which are prone to interruptions.

World.title: Iraq’s foreign reserves hit $79.2 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The financial adviser to Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, Mazhar Saleh, confirmed on Sunday that Iraq’s foreign reserves remain at relatively safe levels.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated Iraq’s total reserves at approximately $79.2 billion for 2026, according to Saleh.

The reserve efficiency index considers covering more than six months’ worth of imports to be a generally safe level.

According to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the reduction in reserves this year needs more care, not because they have reached a critical level, but because there is worry that the loss will continue and negatively impact the safety buffer in the future.

Foreign reserves play a crucial role in maintaining the stability of the Iraqi dinar’s exchange rate and protecting against pressures on the national currency. The capacity of the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) to meet the genuine demand for US dollars is essential for ensuring economic stability and growth.

The heavy dependence on oil revenue is one of the most apparent sources of risk. A decline in oil revenues leads to lower government revenues and reduced foreign currency inflows, which further strains reserves and undermines exchange rate stability.

Saleh emphasized the need to maintain the CBI’s monetary policy independence and not to use foreign reserves to finance the budget deficit, as these measures may lead to reserve depletion and a spike in inflation.

World.title: New intellectual biography explores life and legacy of Iraqi sociologist Ali Al Wardi
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A new intellectual biography examining the life and critical scholarship of Iraq’s founding father of sociology, Ali Al-Wardi, has been released by the American University of Iraq, Baghdad (AUIB) Press.

Authored by Iraqi philosopher and translator Ali Hakim Saleh, the 300-page volume—titled Ali Al-Wardi: An Intellectual and Social Biography — traces Al-Wardi’s transformation into an urban modern intellectual (effendi), his systemic deconstruction of official state narratives, and the subsequent censorship and institutional marginalization he faced.

The biography structures Al-Wardi’s life and academic legacy across several defining phases:

The Rise of the “Effendi” and the Public Intellectual: Tracing Al-Wardi’s emergence from traditional quarters to Western academia (earning his Ph.D. from the University of Texas at Austin in 1950) and his creation of a broad reading public outside elite scholarly circles.

Theorizing the Iraqi Persona: Examining his foundational sociological frameworks, notably the dialectic between nomadism (Badawa) and urban civilization (Hadara), and the concept of psychological duality (Izdawajiyya) within Iraqi society.

Direct Critique of Political Power: Analyzing Al-Wardi’s rigorous critique of state structures and his disruption of official historiography, most prominently captured in his multi-volume opus, Social Glimpses from Modern Iraqi History.

State Friction, Censorship, and Disillusionment: Documenting the political suppression, academic sidelining, and personal disillusionment that followed his confrontation with authoritarian state narratives.

The publication has generated significant interest across Iraqi cultural and academic circles. Prominent author and University of Basra professor Louay Hamza Abbas praised the work as a major cultural milestone:

World.title: Iraq recovers 1.35T dinars in anti-corruption drive
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi federal government has successfully recovered public funds, financial assets, and real estate valued at over 1.359 trillion IQD (approximately $1.04 billion) during its anti-corruption campaign, “Sawlat al-Fajr” (Dawn Assault), government spokesperson Haider Al-Aboudi announced on Saturday, August 29, 2026.

In a statement delivered to Al Iraqiya News and reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Al-Aboudi revealed that the Federal Commission of Integrity has received more than 26,000 formal corruption reports, reflecting heightened institutional activity and public reporting.

Key Operational Milestones & Asset Recovery Figures

Total Asset Value Recovered: Surpassed 1.359 trillion IQD in seized liquid funds, frozen financial instruments, and confiscated real estate properties.

Integrity Commission Reports: Over 26,000 tips and corruption filings registered with the Federal Commission of Integrity during the ongoing enforcement phase.

Whistleblower Financial Incentives: In accordance with the Informants Law (قانون مكافأة المخبرين), individuals who submit verified information leading directly to the recovery of stolen public funds are entitled to financial rewards of up to 5% of the total recovered sum.

Al-Aboudi outlined that the government’s anti-corruption strategy balances punitive judicial enforcement with systemic preventive reforms:

Judicial Safeguards: Emphasized that the Iraqi judiciary stands as the core guarantor supporting the legitimacy, evidence verification, and success of anti-corruption actions.

Direct Prime Ministerial Oversight: Highlighted the Prime Minister’s recent field visit to the Commission of Integrity, confirming direct executive backing for specialized investigative judges and investigators.

Preemptive Contract Auditing: Instituting mandatory advance audits on high-value public procurement contracts to identify irregularities before fund disbursements take place.

Digital Transformation and Automation: Accelerating the digitization of state transactions and public registries to minimize arbitrary human interference, extortion, and bribery opportunities across ministries.

Al-Aboudi characterized systemic corruption as a deeply entrenched web linking financial schemes, administrative loopholes, and political influence that drains public wealth and stalls infrastructure projects.

He reiterated that there will be no halt or political compromise in the government’s anti-corruption drive, noting that institutional transparency, automated governance, and aggressive asset recovery remain long-term priorities.

World.title: Sanad: Iraq targets simultaneous nationwide 5G rollout
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi federal government is actively working to coordinate a simultaneous rollout of next-generation 5G telecommunications services across all Iraqi governorates and the Kurdistan Region, Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad announced on Saturday, August 29, 2026.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Sanad stated that existing technical and administrative differences between the federal ministry and the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) are manageable, emphasizing that bilateral discussions are progressing toward unified protocols.

Key Discussion Tracks & Technical Files

Synchronized 5G Commercial Launch: Noting that the Kurdistan Region had taken earlier exploratory steps toward 5G deployment, the federal ministry is coordinating with regional authorities to synchronize spectrum allocation and commercial launches nationwide.

Transit Fiber-Optic Backbone (Basra to Europe): Coordinating agreements regarding the strategic international transit fiber cable routed from Basra through the Kurdistan Region onward to European hubs, requiring unified commercial terms with operators operating in the region.

Unified International Representation: Sanad underscored Baghdad’s position that Iraq must engage as a unified entity before international telecommunications bodies and multilateral organizations, with the federal Ministry of Communications serving as the sovereign representative.

Regulatory Coordination & Operator Oversight: Addressing regulatory discrepancies stemming from the KRG’s direct ministerial oversight over regional mobile operators (including Korek Telecom), in contrast to the federal model where licensing and sector oversight are managed through an independent communications and media commission.

Sanad confirmed his intention to lead an official delegation to Erbil following a formal written invitation extended by KRG Prime Minister Masrour Barzani during Sanad’s first week in office, which was reaffirmed during a visit to Baghdad by the KRG Minister of Transport and Communications.

The upcoming ministerial meetings aim to finalize an integrated operational framework for cross-border fiber traffic, harmonize telecom licensing standards, and establish joint technical committees to oversee spectrum readiness for 5G network integration.

World.title: 'Oldest trick in RSS playbook': Owaisi attacks Mohan Bhagwat over Hindu-Muslim remarks
World.content:
NEW DELHI: AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi on Sunday criticised RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat over his remarks on Hindu-Muslim unity, alleging that the RSS projects a different image of itself to the world while the writings of its key thinkers reflect a different view of minorities.

Owaisi's remarks came a day after Bhagwat, speaking at at event in New York, said that a Hindu who believes Muslims should not live in India would not remain a Hindu.

Reacting to the remarks, Owaisi said, âThis is the oldest trick in the RSS playbook: some words are for the world, and some are for its own members. The RSS has never disavowed its key thinkers and writers. What do they say about Muslims and other minorities?â

Owaisi referred to a biography of RSS founder K B Hedgewar, published by the RSS, to claim that Hedgewar had opposed the Congress's emphasis on Hindu-Muslim unity.

Quoting from the biography, Owaisi said, âGandhiji worked constantly with one eye on Hindu-Muslim unity... But Doctorji sensed danger in that move. In fact, he did not even relish the newfangled slogan of 'Hindu-Muslim Unity'.â

The AIMIM chief also cited former RSS chief M S Golwalkar's writings, referring to his book Bunch of Thoughts and its chapter titled 'Internal Threats'.

âGolwalkar's 'Bunch of Thoughts' has a long chapter titled 'Internal Threats', in which Muslim and Christian citizens of India are described as threats number one and two, respectively,â Owaisi said.





He also referred to Golwalkar's statement that the Sangh was âinspired by one flag (saffron), one leader and one ideologyâ.

Owaisi alleged that the RSS did not contribute to India's freedom struggle and claimed that Hedgewar left the Congress because he opposed the participation of different religious communities in the anti-British movement led by Mahatma Gandhi.

Owaisi also invoked the 2002 Gujarat riots while criticising the RSS, asking, âShould we forget what happened to the Muslims of Gujarat under the RSS's proxy rule?â

He alleged that Muslims and Christians continued to face discrimination and claimed that Muslims were being subjected to Hindu law in the name of the Uniform Civil Code, while Christians were being targeted through âdraconianâ anti-conversion laws.

The AIMIM chief also raised concerns over the alleged misuse of laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).

Earlier on Saturday, addressing the âOne World One Humanityâ event in New York, Bhagwat said different religions may follow different paths, but humanity and truth remain one. âWe come from a society that believes humanity is one,â he said.

âIf any Hindu thinks that there should be no Muslim in Bharat, he will not remain Hindu.

If you want to call yourself Hindu, you must believe that all paths are leading to the same goal and that every human has dignity. There is no difference between human beings,â Bhagwat had added.

Bhagwat also used the occasion to speak about perceptions of the RSS. He said the organisation was often viewed through narratives that, in his view, did not reflect its work on the ground.

World.title: IISc eco-friendly foam moves from lab to market; TOI story drew industry
World.content:
BENGALURU: An eco-friendly bio-based foam developed by researchers at the Indian Institute of Science (

), is moving from the laboratory towards commercialisation, with Absolute Cold LLP working on its use in cold-chain and temperature-controlled packaging.

The foam, developed by Prof Suryasarathi Bose and Prof Subodh Kumar, along with the team comprising Sampath Parasuram, Akshay Sunil Salvi, Supriya H, Sandeep Kumar Singh and Amit Malakar, is an alternative to conventional polyurethane (PU) foam, which is widely used for insulation but is difficult to recycle after use.

The IISc material was designed to combine the properties needed for insulation with a more sustainable approach to what happens to the material at the end of its life.

The journey from laboratory to industry also had a link to TOI.

Bose said a report on the development published by TOI on Nov 11, 2024, helped bring a potential industry partner on board. âYour [TOI] article brought in a potential licensee on board and helped take the technology to market. Absolute Cold director saw your story and reached out to us,â he said.

The original IISc work involved making the foam using epoxidised fatty acids derived from non-edible oils and polyphenol-based materials derived from tea leaves.





The researchers also incorporated a chemical structure that allows the material to be reprocessed, rather than simply being discarded after use.

Absolute Cold, which works in the cold-chain and temperature-controlled logistics sector, subsequently became interested in the technology. The company is now working towards translating the laboratory material into a product for applications where maintaining temperature during storage and transport is critical.

This could include packaging used to transport pharmaceuticals and other temperature-sensitive products. Such packaging needs to provide insulation while also being lightweight and strong enough to withstand handling and transportation. Its environmental impact after use is an increasing consideration as well.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The move is the latest step in Boseâs broader work on more sustainable polymeric materials. His research has included efforts to find ways of reusing or upcycling plastics that are otherwise difficult to recycle, with the aim of keeping materials in use for longer rather than sending them to waste.

For IISc, the foam's progress also shows the less visible part of academic innovation: getting a material developed in a laboratory into a form that industry can manufacture and customers can use. The licensing and scale-up process can require changes to the formulation, manufacturing process and product design even after the underlying research has been demonstrated.

The next test, therefore, is whether the foam can be produced at commercial scale while retaining the insulation, strength and durability demonstrated during development. Its performance in actual cold-chain applications will ultimately determine whether the IISc innovation can become a practical alternative to conventional foams.

For a material conceived around the problem of what happens to foam after its useful life, that commercial journey is as important as the laboratory breakthrough itself.

World.title: ‘Violation of High Court order won't be tolerated’: Agnimitra Paul reacts after FIR against Mamata Banerjee
World.content:
NEW DELHI: West Bengal minister Agnimitra Paul on Sunday said that any violation of a Calcutta High Court order, irrespective of the person involved, "would not be tolerated", after an FIR was registered against former chief minister

over alleged violations during a Trinamool Chhatra Parishad (TMCP) programme in Kolkata.

Speaking to news agency ANI, Paul alleged that the previous Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress government had shown disrespect towards the Calcutta High Court and that judges were repeatedly insulted during its tenure.

"Any violation of the High Court's order, whether by Mamata Banerjee or anyone else, will not be tolerated. The previous government showed disrespect to the High Court; judges were repeatedly insulted...

now, such things will not be tolerated," Paul said.

FIR over alleged violation of court order

Banerjee and organisers of the West Bengal Trinamool Chhatra Parishad (WBTMCP) programme have been booked by Hastings Police over the alleged violation of a Calcutta High Court order during the organisation's foundation day programme at Cathedral Road on August 28.

According to police, the case was registered at Hastings Police Station on August 28 based on a written complaint submitted by Sub-Inspector Apu Baidya.





The FIR includes Sections 61(2), 223, 125(a), 132 and 285 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to allegations including criminal conspiracy, disobedience of an order duly promulgated by a public servant, acts endangering life or personal safety, assault or criminal force against public servants, and negligent conduct with respect to public ways.

Police alleged that Banerjee and the organisers violated an order passed by the Calcutta High Court in connection with WPA No.

21728 of 2026.

According to the complaint, the programme was scheduled to be held from 12 noon to 3 pm under the permission and directions referred to in the complaint. Police alleged that the organisers continued the programme beyond the permitted time.

Police allege barricades were breached

The complaint alleged that Banerjee and the organisers provoked supporters during the programme, following which the crowd pushed aside barricades put up by police.

Supporters allegedly jostled with police personnel deployed at the venue, creating a chaotic situation, according to the police account. The gathering also allegedly obstructed vehicular movement on one flank of Cathedral Road.

The Calcutta High Court had imposed conditions for the programme, with Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya directing on Tuesday that efforts be made to keep attendance within 1,500.

The court had also directed police to ensure that law and order was maintained and that vehicular movement on one flank of the road was not affected.

Indranil Khan also attacks Mamata

West Bengal minister Indranil Khan also criticised Banerjee, alleging that she had repeatedly disrespected constitutional institutions and the judiciary.

"Mamata Banerjee never respected the country's laws or its Constitution. Even while serving as Chief Minister, she made highly objectionable and disrespectful remarks against the Calcutta High Court and its judges. Today, although the people of West Bengal have removed her from the post of Chief Minister and she is no longer even an MLA, she remains unable to shed that mindset," Khan told reporters.

In the future, we will promote direct linkages, co-production, and co-development between the defense industries of both nations,â he said.PM Modi said India and Uzbekistan shared a commitment to combating terrorism, extremism and separatism.âWe believe that terrorism, extremism, and separatism pose serious challenges to the entire region. Maintaining a policy of zero tolerance against these threats has been, and will continue to be, our shared resolve,â he said.The prime minister also highlighted cooperation in agriculture, healthcare and traditional medicine, saying the strengths of the two countries could complement each other.âBy combining Uzbekistan's experience in horticulture with India's modern agricultural practices, we will contribute to the food security of both nations. Uzbekistan's medicinal herbs and India's expertise in Ayurveda form a natural combination,â PM said.PM Modi also announced that India and Uzbekistan would establish three sister-city and sister-state arrangements to expand cooperation beyond the national capitals.âWe aim to ensure that our partnership is not limited merely to our national capitals; therefore, we are establishing partnerships between our cities and states,â he said.He also highlighted the potential for cooperation between Uzbekistan's New Tashkent project and India's GIFT City.âMega-projects like 'New Tashkent' are underway in your country, while in India, we have developed GIFT City in Gujarat. We would be delighted to welcome a delegation from your country to study best practices and the use of technology in these developments,â PM Modi said.Mirziyoyev said the talks had identified several new areas where India and Uzbekistan could expand cooperation, including energy, culture, critical minerals, pharmaceuticals, jewellery and agriculture.âDuring our discussions, we identified new areas where we can realize our existing potential. We aim to advance cooperation in sectors such as energy, culture, critical minerals, pharmaceuticals, jewelry, and agriculture,â he said.âWe will prepare roadmaps for each of these sectors; specific teams from India will visit here, and our teams will travel to India, enabling us to clearly define our objectives in these fields,â Mirziyoyev added.The Uzbek president said the two countries would continue to coordinate on global issues and support each other at international platforms including the United Nations, BRICS and the Non-Aligned Movement.He also highlighted growing educational and cultural ties, noting that four Indian universities are currently operating in Uzbekistan. Mirziyoyev said a 30-day visa-free regime and efforts to promote direct flights would further boost people-to-people exchanges.âOur partnership has ascended to a new level of quality, emerging as a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership,â Mirziyoyev said.During his visit, Mirziyoyev conferred Uzbekistan's highest state honour, the Order of âOliy Darajali Dustlikâ, on PM Modi. We will honour this friendship in every way,â he added.The Prime Minister also witnessed a special yoga session in Tashkent featuring 52 practitioners from Uzbekistan.âUzbekistan loves Yoga!â PM Modi said in a post on X, highlighting the country's participation in the first World Yogasana Championship held in Ahmedabad earlier this year.âUzbekistan was a proud participant in the first-ever World Yogasana Championship held in Ahmedabad earlier this year. Some of the medalists were also present today. They came back with great memories of India and the Championship,â he said.PM Modi also commended the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan for promoting yoga in the country.The prime minister is on a two-nation visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic. From Tashkent, he will travel to Bishkek to attend the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit on August 31 and September 1.

World.title: China, Bangladesh to start two-plus-two dialogue in the ‘very near future’, says Humaiun Kobir
World.content:
Bangladesh-China two-plus-two dialogue will commence in the “very near future”, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir announced in Dhaka on Sunday (August 30, 2026). Mr. Kobir announced this soon after the Chinese Ambassador to Bangladesh, Yao Wen, called on him to discuss a number of projects, including the Teesta River Comprehensive Management and Restoration Project (TRCMRP).

“The groundwork for the 2+2 engagement is currently being laid for further interactions. So yes, it will commence at a mutually convenient time in the very near future,” Mr. Kobir told members of the media at the Foreign Ministry. Mr. Kobir, who was inducted into the Ministry on August 21, said the dialogue will include diplomacy and defence verticals at the level of Minister of State and then will move to the Foreign Minister-level.

“We have not fixed any specific dates yet. However, discussions will take place at that level,” he said. The announcement came two months after Prime Minister Tarique Rahman visited China, where the two sides discussed major projects, including plans for the Teesta River. Mr. Kobir described China as an important development partner and reaffirmed Bangladesh’s commitment to the ‘One China policy’.

In his meeting with the Chinese Ambassador, Mr. Kobir discussed a number of items that were taken up during Prime Minister Rahman’s China visit including the Teesta River Comprehensive Management and Restoration Project (TRCMRP). They also discussed the China-Myanmar-Bangladesh corridor project, China Economic and Industrial Zone (CEIZ) and signing of a commercial contract for modernisation of Mongla Port. Possible Chinese cooperation in establishing a Mongla Export Processing Zone (EPZ) also featured in the discussions, BSS, the state-run news outlet of Bangladesh, has reported.

World.title: Salem traders threaten to shut shops if Corporation does not slash taxes
World.content:
Traders in Salem city have urged the Corporation to reduce the property tax fixed for commercial buildings and warned of strike if their demand is not met.

The Salem Corporation’s annual tax revenue for the current fiscal is expected to be ₹207 crore, which includes property tax collection from 2.15 lakh assessees, professional tax from 28,260 assessees, and vacant land tax from 17,290 assessees. Traders, however, allege that property tax for commercial buildings is not calculated properly, and the tax fixed by the civic body is exorbitant.

Salem City Chamber of Commerce general secretary A. Jayaseelan said the Corporation has fixed ₹28 per sq. ft as property tax for commercial buildings in the city, which is higher than that in Coimbatore and Tiruchi cities, where the maximum tax is ₹16 per sq. ft.

“The Salem Corporation has not categorised industrial and commercial structures properly. We met the Corporation officials more than 20 times in this regard but no action was taken,” he alleged.

Stating that the Salem Corporation passed a resolution before the elections on the demand to reduce the taxes, Mr. Jayaseelan said that following elections, the government did not act on the resolution. Now, the Corporation is demanding taxes it had fixed earlier. “If the taxes are not reduced over the next 10 days, the traders will shut their shops,” Mr. Jayaseelan warned.

Ward 34 Councillor Esan D. Elango (DMK) alleged that the areas were not properly classified as A, B and C centres. The tax collected by Salem Corporation is higher than that in other cities. The resolution passed to reduce the taxes was also not sent to the government properly. The view expressed during the council meeting was not updated in the minutes. The Corporation should re-classify the areas properly and fix the taxes, Mr. Elango added.

According to Salem Corporation officials, property tax was hiked in Salem city after 20 years in 2022. Resolutions were passed in the council meeting in this regard and taxes are collected based on it.
